definition_zh: 影响；影响力；势力；施加影响；（酒、药物的）作用
definition_en: the power to affect people or things, or a hidden force that flows into them and changes them
core_image: 看不见的星力像水一样从天上流下来，注进一个人的身体，悄悄改变他的性情与命运
scene: A teacher watches a shy student and says: Her grandmother's letters had a quiet influence on her choice to become a writer.
sceneCN: 这里 influence 是「潜移默化的影响」（第 4 个义项：长期而不可见的感化）；句意：祖母的信对她选择当作家的决定有一种安静的影响。画面里有旧信件、书桌和窗外的光。

pos.zh: 影响；影响力；势力；作用
影响；左右；促使

derivatives.zh: 流行性感冒（旧说由星力致病）

senses.title: Unseen power: the force that changes things
senses.titleCN: 影响力：改变人与事的那股无形之力
senses.definition: the power that someone or something has to affect people, events, or things
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物影响他人、事件或事物的力量
senses.example: Her teacher had a lasting influence on her career.
senses.exampleCN: 她的老师对她的事业产生了持久的影响。
senses.why: The noun is first recorded in late 14c. as an astrological term for a power streaming down from the stars. That invisible force became any unseen power that produces an effect, and by the 1650s it was 'capacity for producing effects by invisible means'.
senses.whyCN: 名词最早记录于 14 世纪后期，是占星术语，指从星辰流下的力量。这种看不见的力后来指任何产生效果的无形之力；到 17 世纪 50 年代，它指“以无形方式产生效果的能力”。

senses.title: To affect: let the current do its work
senses.titleCN: 施加影响：让那股流自己起作用
senses.definition: to affect someone or something, especially in an indirect or gradual way
senses.definitionCN: 影响某人或某物，尤指以间接或渐进的方式
senses.example: Parents influence how their children handle failure.
senses.exampleCN: 父母影响着孩子如何面对失败。
senses.why: The verb appears in the 1650s, converted straight from the noun: to influence is to let that inflowing force act on someone. English often turns a noun for a force into a verb for using it.
senses.whyCN: 动词出现于 17 世纪 50 年代，直接由名词转化而来：influence 就是让那股流入的力作用在某人身上。英语常把一个表示“力”的名词直接变成“使用这股力”的动词。

senses.title: Personal pull: power that opens doors
senses.titleCN: 势力、门路：能替人开门的权力
senses.definition: the power to affect decisions that comes from position, wealth, or personal connections
senses.definitionCN: 来自地位、财富或人脉的、能左右决策的权力
senses.example: He used his influence to get the proposal onto the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 他动用自己的势力把这项提案送上了议程。
senses.why: By the 1580s the word covered 'exertion of unseen influence by persons', a sense already present in Medieval Latin. When the invisible power is attached to a person's standing, influence becomes the pull that connections give.
senses.whyCN: 到 16 世纪 80 年代，这个词已包含“人施加无形影响”的义项，中世纪拉丁语里已有此义。当那股无形之力附着在某个人的地位上，influence 就成了人脉带来的“拉动力”，即势力。

senses.title: Slow shaping: the force that seeps into character
senses.titleCN: 潜移默化：渗进性情里的那股力
senses.definition: a gradual, often unnoticed effect on someone's character or thinking
senses.definitionCN: 对某人性格或思想缓慢而往往不被察觉的作用
senses.example: Her calm influence changed the tone of the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉稳的性情潜移默化地改变了整个团队的氛围。
senses.why: The oldest image is fluid: influence flows in like water and seeps into character without a single visible act. This is why the word suits slow moral or educational shaping better than sudden persuasion.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是液体：影响像水一样流入，不必有哪一个看得见的动作，就渗进了性情。所以这个词更适合形容缓慢的道德或教育塑造，而不是突然的说服。

senses.title: Star-power: the astrological birth sense
senses.titleCN: 星体流射：占星术里的本义
senses.definition: in old astrology, a power believed to stream from the stars into a person's character or fate
senses.definitionCN: 旧时占星术所信的一种力量，认为它从星辰流入人的性格或命运
senses.example: Medieval doctors blamed the planet's influence for the sudden fever.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生把这场突发的高烧归咎于那颗行星的星力。
senses.why: This is the word's birth sense (late 14c.): Medieval Latin influentia named a 'flowing in' from the stars, from influere 'to flow into'. The heavens were thought to pour an ethereal substance into human lives.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的出生义（14 世纪后期）：中世纪拉丁语 influentia 指星辰的“流入”，来自 influere“流入”。当时人相信天体会把一种精微物质倾注进人的生命。

senses.title: Under the influence: the substance inside
senses.titleCN: 酒力发作：进到体内的那种东西
senses.definition: the effect of alcohol or drugs on a person, as in the phrase under the influence
senses.definitionCN: 酒精或药物对人的作用，如短语 under the influence
senses.example: He was arrested for driving under the influence.
senses.exampleCN: 他因酒后驾车被捕。
senses.why: 'Under the influence (of alcohol)' is attested by 1866. The old astrological force is now a substance in the blood: it has flowed in and taken over the driver's judgement.
senses.whyCN: “under the influence（受酒精影响）”记录于 1866 年。昔日占星意义上的力，如今成了血液里的一种物质：它流进身体，接管了司机的判断。

senses.title: A factor: the force made countable
senses.titleCN: 影响因素：被数出来的那股力
senses.definition: a factor or variable that affects an outcome, especially in analysis or research
senses.definitionCN: 影响结果的因子或变量，尤用于分析或研究
senses.example: Income is one of the strongest influences on health outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 收入是影响健康结果最强的因素之一。
senses.why: Once influence means any power producing an effect, researchers can count such powers as factors. The unseen flow becomes a measurable variable in a model.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 influence 泛指任何产生效果的力量，研究者就能把这些力量当作因子来计数。看不见的流，在模型里变成了可以测量的变量。

senses.title: To sway: push a decision one way
senses.titleCN: 左右、促使：把决定推向一边
senses.definition: to persuade or sway someone toward a decision, often by pressure or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 说服或左右某人做出某个决定，常带压力或诉求
senses.example: Lobbyists tried to influence the committee's vote.
senses.exampleCN: 游说者试图左右委员会的投票。
senses.why: The verb's 1650s sense 'modify or affect by intangible means' narrows here to directing a decision. To influence a vote is to make the invisible pull decide which way the lever falls.
senses.whyCN: 动词在 17 世纪 50 年代指“以无形方式改变或作用”，这里收窄为“引导一个决定”。左右一次投票，就是让那股看不见的拉力决定杆子往哪边倒。

senses.title: A flowing in: the literal old sense
senses.titleCN: 流入：字面意义上的古义
senses.definition: a flowing in of water or other fluid, an archaic literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 水或其他液体的流入，古旧的实指义
senses.example: The old physician spoke of an influence of humors into the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老医生谈到体液向血液中的流入。
senses.why: Latin influere was literally 'to flow into'. English kept the physical image for centuries beside the figurative one; it survives now mainly in the Latin-shaped doublet influx.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 influere 字面就是“流入”。英语让这个实指意象与比喻义并存了几个世纪；如今它主要活在拉丁形的同源词 influx 里。

intro.en: Influence begins as astrology: a fluid power pouring from the stars into a person. The metaphor of flowing in then spreads to people, institutions, alcohol, and finally statistics.
intro.cn: influence 起于占星：一股流体般的力量从星辰倾注到人身上。“流入”这个隐喻随后扩展到人、机构、酒，最后扩展到统计学。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow, stream, run'. Its deeper PIE form *bhleu- 'to swell, overflow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: fluere 意为“流动、涌流”。它更深的印欧语形式 *bhleu-“膨胀、溢出”是重构出来的，没有书面记录，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Influentia meant 'a flowing in', from influere 'to flow into', built from in- 'into' plus fluere 'to flow'. It was used for the astrological emanation of the stars.
items.cn: influentia 意为“流入”，来自 influere“流入”，由 in-“进入”加 fluere“流”构成。它被用来指星辰的占星流射。

items.en: Old French influence carried both 'a flow of water, a flowing in' and 'an emanation from the stars that acts upon one's character and destiny'.
items.cn: 古法语 influence 兼有“水的流入”和“从星辰流出、作用于人的性格与命运的力量”两义。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as an astrological term: 'streaming ethereal power from the stars, acting upon character or destiny'. Middle English still applied it to any outflowing energy, fluid or immaterial.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为占星术语：“从星辰流出的以太之力，作用于性格或命运”。中古英语仍用它指任何流出的能量，无论是有形的流体还是无形的力。

items.en: The sense 'exertion of unseen influence by persons' is from the 1580s; 'capacity for producing effects by insensible or invisible means' from the 1650s. The verb 'to affect by intangible means' also dates from the 1650s.
items.cn: “人施加无形影响”的义项始于 16 世纪 80 年代；“以不可感知或无形的方式产生效果的能力”始于 17 世纪 50 年代。动词“以无形方式影响”同样记录于 17 世纪 50 年代。

items.en: 'Under the influence (of alcohol)' is attested by 1866. The astral fluid has become a substance in the body, completing the word's long journey from sky to bloodstream.
items.cn: “under the influence（受酒精影响）”记录于 1866 年。星体之流变成了体内的一种物质，完成了这个词从天空到血液的漫长旅程。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: wealth; an abundant flow of money or goods. It shares the -fluence ending but takes ad- 'to' rather than in-.
entries.definitionCN: 富足；财富的丰盛流入。它与 influence 共享 -fluence 词尾，但前缀是 ad-“向”而非 in-。

entries.definition: the flu. Italian borrowed the astrological word for an illness blamed on star influence.
entries.definitionCN: 流行性感冒。意大利语借用了这个占星词，用来指被归因于星力的疾病。

entries.definition: a flowing in of people, money, or things. It keeps the physical image that influence turned into a metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 人、钱或物的涌入。它保留了 influence 转成比喻之前的那个实指意象。

entries.definition: a change produced by a cause. It names the result, while influence names the force behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 效果；结果。它命名结果，而 influence 命名背后的那股力。

entries.definition: a powerful or direct effect. It is stronger and more sudden than the slow influence.
entries.definitionCN: 冲击；强烈影响。它比缓慢的 influence 更强、更突然。

entries.definition: to move someone toward one opinion or decision. It matches influence as a verb of persuasion.
entries.definitionCN: 左右；动摇。它对应 influence 作为“说服”的动词义。

entries.definition: the recognized right to give orders or make decisions. It is formal power, not the informal pull of influence.
entries.definitionCN: 权威；职权。它是正式的权力，而非 influence 那种非正式的拉力。

entries.definition: the power to influence decisions, especially in politics or business.
entries.definitionCN: 势力；影响力，尤指政治或商业上的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin fluere 'to flow', Medieval Latin influentia, and the English words built from the same stream.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 fluere“流”、中世纪拉丁语 influentia，以及从同一股水流里长出的英语词。

normal.en: influence = in- 'into' + fluere 'to flow': a power flows into you and changes what you do.
normal.cn: influence = in-“进入”+ fluere“流”：一股力流进你体内，改变了你的所作所为。

normal.en: The same fluere gives fluent, fluid, influx and confluence: every one of them is about flowing.
normal.cn: 同一个 fluere 给出 fluent、fluid、influx、confluence：每一个都与“流”有关。

normal.en: Influenza is the same word in Italian: the flu was once blamed on an influence from the stars.
normal.cn: influenza 就是同一个词进了意大利语：流感曾被归因于星辰的影响。

normal.en: An influencer is literally a person who pours a current into a crowd.
normal.cn: influencer 字面上就是往人群里注入一股水流的人。

normal.en: under the influence keeps the old image: the drink has flowed in and is now steering.
normal.cn: under the influence 保留了旧意象：酒已经流进体内，正在握着方向盘。

abstract.en: The core is invisible flow: power with no hand, moving like water.
abstract.cn: 核心是看不见的流动：没有手在推，力量却像水一样移动。

abstract.en: It travels from sky to person to number: star-force, personal pull, statistical factor.
abstract.cn: 它从天空走到人，再走到数字：星力、人脉拉力、统计因子。

abstract.en: Influence and influenza are siblings: both imagine something pouring in and taking hold.
abstract.cn: influence 与 influenza 是同一家的：两者都想象某种东西倾注进来并占据身体。

examples.en: Social media has a huge influence on how teenagers see themselves.
examples.cn: 社交媒体对青少年如何看待自己有着巨大的影响。

examples.en: The climate strongly influences what crops farmers can grow.
examples.cn: 气候强烈影响农民能种哪些作物。

examples.en: She was under the influence of painkillers when she signed the form.
examples.cn: 她签那份表格时正受到止痛药的作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ flu（flow 流）——一股力流进你心里，把你悄悄改变 → influence 影响

root: 源自拉丁语 fluere“流动”，加 in-“进入”构成 influere“流入”，经中世纪拉丁语 influentia 与古法语进入英语；核心是“看不见的力量像水一样流进人身上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, all one image: something invisible flows into a person and changes what they do. It begins as star-power, becomes personal pull, then a measurable factor, and finally a legal phrase about alcohol.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共用同一个意象：某种看不见的东西流进一个人，改变他的行为。它从星力开始，变成人脉的拉力，再变成可测量的因子，最后成为关于酒精的法律用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible current flowing into a person and changing them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的水流进入一个人，并改变了他。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN CURRENT: the power to affect, and its slow shaping of character.
branches.cn: 无形之流：影响的力量，以及它对性情的缓慢塑造。

branches.en: PERSONAL PULL: influence from standing or connections, and the act of swaying a decision.
branches.cn: 人脉拉力：来自地位或关系的势力，以及左右一个决定的行为。

branches.en: THE LITERAL FLOW: star-emanation, and the old physical flowing in.
branches.cn: 字面之流：星体流射，以及古老的实指流入。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE WITHIN: alcohol or drugs taking over judgement.
branches.cn: 体内之物：酒精或药物接管了判断。

branches.en: THE COUNTABLE FORCE: the verb 'to affect', and the factor counted in an analysis.
branches.cn: 可数的力：动词“影响”，以及分析中被计数的因子。

intro.en: Influence is in- plus flu- plus -ence. Its family shows the prefix in-, con-, af- and ef-, the root flu- 'flow', and the suffixes -ent, -id, -ence and -ly.
intro.cn: influence 是 in- 加 flu- 再加 -ence。它的词族展示前缀 in-、con-、af-、ef-，词根 flu-“流”，以及后缀 -ent、-id、-ence、-ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere 'to flow' is the base of fluent, fluid and influx; with prefixes it yields influere, affluere and effluere, and the noun influentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere“流”是 fluent、fluid、influx 的基础；加前缀又给出 influere、affluere、effluere，以及名词 influentia。

items.meaning: a power that flows in and affects
items.meaningCN: 影响；影响力（流入之力）
items.example: His advice had a strong influence on my decision.
items.exampleCN: 他的建议对我的决定有很大影响。

items.meaning: having the power to affect people or events
items.meaningCN: 有影响力的（-ial 形容词后缀）
items.example: She became one of the most influential writers of her time.
items.exampleCN: 她成为那个时代最有影响力的作家之一。

items.meaning: flu, an illness once blamed on astral influence
items.meaningCN: 流行性感冒（源自星力致病说）
items.example: The influenza season begins in late autumn.
items.exampleCN: 流感季从深秋开始。

items.meaning: a flowing in of people or things
items.meaningCN: 流入；涌入（-flux 即流）
items.example: The town grew quickly after an influx of workers.
items.exampleCN: 大批工人涌入后，小镇迅速发展。

items.meaning: flowing easily, especially in speech
items.meaningCN: 流利的（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: He is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 他能流利地说三种语言。

items.meaning: a substance that flows; able to flow
items.meaningCN: 流体；流动的（-id 后缀）
items.example: The patient needs more fluids.
items.exampleCN: 这位病人需要多补充液体。

items.meaning: the place where two streams flow together
items.meaningCN: 汇流处（con- 共同 + 流）
items.example: The city stands at the confluence of two rivers.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市位于两条河的交汇处。

items.meaning: wealth flowing in; abundance
items.meaningCN: 富足（财富流入）
items.example: The family lived in comfort but not affluence.
items.exampleCN: 这家人生活舒适，但算不上富足。

items.meaning: liquid waste flowing out of a place
items.meaningCN: 废水；流出物（ef- 向外 + 流）
items.example: The factory was fined for dumping effluent into the river.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂因向河里排放废水而被罚款。

items.meaning: in a smooth, flowing way
items.meaningCN: 流利地（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: She speaks Japanese fluently.
items.exampleCN: 她日语说得很流利。

definition_zh: 最初的；开始的；首字母；姓名缩写；用首字母签署
definition_en: belonging to the beginning, or the first letter of a word or name
core_image: 一本书的第一页第一行，第一个字母被放大成金色花纹，后面的一切都从它开始
scene: The editor circles the first letter of each name and says: Just give me your initials on this form.
sceneCN: 这里 initials 是「姓名首字母缩写」（第 3 个义项：用名字开头的字母代表全名）；句意：在这张表上写下你的姓名缩写就行。画面里有表格、笔和圈出的字母。

pos.zh: 最初的；开始的；词首的
首字母；姓名缩写；装饰性首字母
用首字母签署或标注

senses.title: At the start: the first moment
senses.titleCN: 最初的：时间上的第一步
senses.definition: happening at the beginning; first in a series
senses.definitionCN: 发生在开始时的；一系列中的第一个
senses.example: The initial results look promising.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
senses.why: The adjective is recorded from the 1520s as 'of or pertaining to a beginning'. Latin initialis came from initium 'a beginning', literally 'a going in' — the first step into something.
senses.whyCN: 形容词记录于 16 世纪 20 年代，意为“与开始有关的”。拉丁语 initialis 来自 initium“开始”，字面是“一次走入”——踏进某事的第一步。

senses.title: The first letter: where a word steps in
senses.titleCN: 首字母：一个词进门的地方
senses.definition: the first letter of a word or name
senses.definitionCN: 单词或姓名的第一个字母
senses.example: The poem's initials are decorated in gold.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的首字母用金色装饰。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1620s, shortened from the adjective in the specialized phrase 'initial letter'. A letter standing at the start of a word takes the name of the start itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，是由短语 initial letter“开头的字母”中形容词的专指用法而来。站在一个词开头的字母，就直接借用了“开头”这个名字。

senses.title: Initials: several beginnings as one name
senses.titleCN: 姓名缩写：几个开头合成一个名字
senses.definition: the first letters of a person's names, used together to stand for the full name
senses.definitionCN: 一个人各名字的首字母合在一起，代表全名
senses.example: Please write your initials beside each correction.
senses.exampleCN: 请在每处修改旁写上你的姓名缩写。
senses.why: Once a single initial marks a word, the set of such letters can mark a whole name. The plural initials turns several beginnings into a compact signature.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个 initial 能标记一个词的开头，那么一组这样的字母就能标记整个姓名。复数 initials 把好几个“开头”压成一个紧凑的签名。

senses.title: To initial: sign with the first letters
senses.titleCN: 签首字母：用开头的字母代替签名
senses.definition: to mark or sign something with one's initials
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的姓名首字母标记或签署某物
senses.example: He initialed every page of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他在合同的每一页上签了姓名首字母。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from 1837, formed directly from the noun: to put the first letters where a full signature would go, a quick legal mark.
senses.whyCN: 动词记录于 1837 年，直接由名词构成：在本该写全名的地方写下开头的字母，是一种快捷的法律标记。

senses.title: At the front: a matter of position
senses.titleCN: 词首的、句首的：说的是位置而非时间
senses.definition: standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, or line
senses.definitionCN: 位于单词、句子或诗行的开头
senses.example: An initial consonant often carries the stress in English words.
senses.exampleCN: 英语单词的词首辅音常常承载重音。
senses.why: The 1620s adjective also meant 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.' Here initial names a position, not a time: whatever occupies the front slot is initial.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代的形容词也指“位于词、句的开头”。这里 initial 命名的是位置而不是时间：占据最前面那个位置的，就是 initial。

senses.title: Initial sound: the consonant at the gate
senses.titleCN: 声母：守在音节门口的那个音
senses.definition: in phonetics, the sound or consonant at the start of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 语音学上，音节开头的音或辅音
senses.example: Mandarin syllables are analysed as an initial and a final.
senses.exampleCN: 普通话的音节被分析为声母和韵母两部分。
senses.why: Phonology borrowed the positional sense: the initial is the consonant that opens a syllable, the part that stands at the gate before the vowel.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借走了那个位置义：声母是打开一个音节的那个辅音，是在韵母之前守在门口的部分。

senses.title: Early stage: the first, faint signs
senses.titleCN: 初期的：最早、最轻的那些迹象
senses.definition: early in a process, before later stages develop
senses.definitionCN: 处于过程的早期，后阶段尚未展开
senses.example: Initial symptoms of the disease are easy to miss.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病的初期症状很容易被忽略。
senses.why: From 'belonging to a beginning', medicine takes initial for the first, often faint stage of an illness. The later stages exist, but this is what shows at the door.
senses.whyCN: 医学从“属于开头”这一层取用 initial，指疾病最初、往往很轻的阶段。后面的阶段当然存在，但这一刻在门口露面的只是它。

senses.title: Starting setting: the value before change
senses.titleCN: 初始设置：改变之前的值
senses.definition: in computing and mathematics, the value or setting that exists at the start of a process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或数学中，过程开始时就存在的值或设置
senses.example: You can restore the program to its initial settings.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以把程序恢复到初始设置。
senses.why: Modern technical use extends 'at the beginning' to a state before any change: initial conditions, initial settings. The word names the baseline from which a process runs.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术用法把“在开头”延伸到“任何改变之前的状态”：初始条件、初始设置。这个词命名的是一个过程启动时所依据的基线。

senses.title: The illuminated initial: a letter turned into a picture
senses.titleCN: 装饰首字母：被画成一幅画的那个字母
senses.definition: a large decorated letter at the start of a chapter in an old manuscript or printed book
senses.definitionCN: 古代手抄本或印本中，章节开头的大型装饰字母
senses.example: The illuminated initial shows a knight on horseback.
senses.exampleCN: 那个装饰首字母画着一位骑马的骑士。
senses.why: Medieval scribes enlarged the first letter of a chapter into a picture. The decorated initial is sense 02 given space and gold, marking where the text begins.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员把一章的第一个字母放大成一幅画。装饰首字母就是把第 2 义给了空间和金色，标记正文从哪里开始。

intro.en: Initial is built on the Latin verb inire 'to go into'. A beginning is literally a going in: one crosses a threshold, and the first letter of a word or name stands at that threshold.
intro.cn: initial 建在拉丁动词 inire“走进去”上。“开始”字面上就是“走进”：人跨过一道门槛，而单词或姓名的第一个字母就站在那道门槛上。

items.en: Inire meant 'to go into, enter upon, begin', from in- 'into' plus ire 'to go'. The deeper PIE root *ei- 'to go' is a reconstruction, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: inire 意为“走入、着手、开始”，由 in-“进入”加 ire“走”构成。更深的印欧语词根 *ei-“走”是重构形式，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning, a commencement; an entrance, a going in'. It is a noun use of the neuter past participle of inire, so the word carries the image of having stepped inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开始、开端；入口、一次走入”。它是 inire 中性过去分词的名词化用法，所以这个词自带“已经跨进去”的画面。

items.en: Initialis meant 'initial, incipient, of the beginning', derived from initium. Latin gave the adjective to French and to English.
items.cn: initialis 意为“开头的、初期的、属于开始的”，由 initium 派生。拉丁语把这个形容词传给了法语和英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded as 'of or pertaining to a beginning', borrowed from French initial or directly from Latin initialis.
items.cn: 形容词记录为“与开始有关的”，借自法语 initial，或直接来自拉丁语 initialis。

items.en: The noun appears as 'initial letter of a name or surname', from a specialized use of the adjective meaning 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.'
items.cn: 名词出现，意为“姓名或姓氏的首字母”，来自形容词“位于词、句开头”的专指用法。

items.en: The verb 'to mark or sign with initials' is recorded from 1837, formed from the noun. Related forms are initialed and initialing in American spelling.
items.cn: 动词“用首字母标记或签署”记录于 1837 年，由名词构成。美式拼写中相关形式为 initialed、initialing。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the ability to act first without being told. It is initi- plus -ative, from the same initium.
entries.definitionCN: 主动性；率先行动的能力。它是 initi- 加 -ative，同出 initium。

entries.definition: at first; at the beginning. It is initial plus -ly and differs only in the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 起初；最初。它是 initial 加 -ly，只差词尾。

entries.definition: to begin something or bring someone into a group. It swaps the -ial ending for -iate.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；使入门。它把 -ial 词尾换成 -iate。

entries.definition: coming before all others in time or order. It is the plain English word for initial.
entries.definitionCN: 第一的；最先的。它是 initial 的朴素英语说法。

entries.definition: the first part or beginning of something. It stresses the moment a thing opens.
entries.definitionCN: 开头；开端。它强调事物“打开”的那一刻。

entries.definition: existing from the beginning, or first in a line. It points to origin rather than mere order.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；原先的。它指向来源，而不只是顺序上的第一。

entries.definition: just beginning to appear or develop. It is more formal and often used of things not yet visible.
entries.definitionCN: 初期的；刚出现的。它更正式，常指尚未明显显现的事物。

entries.definition: done before the main event as preparation. It is initial in time, but serves something later.
entries.definitionCN: 初步的；预备的。它在时间上最前，但为后来的正事服务。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin inire 'to go in', initium 'a beginning', and the English family of initial, initiate, initiative.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 inire“走进”、initium“开始”，以及 initial、initiate、initiative 这一族英语词。

normal.en: initial = in- 'into' + ire 'to go': the first step is the one that goes in.
normal.cn: initial = in-“进入”+ ire“走”：第一步就是走进门的那一步。

normal.en: initium means 'a going in', so a beginning and an entrance are the same picture.
normal.cn: initium 意为“一次走入”，所以“开始”和“入口”是同一幅画。

normal.en: The initial letter stands at the doorway of a word, which is why the first letter is called an initial.
normal.cn: 首字母站在一个词的门槛上，所以第一个字母才叫 initial。

normal.en: Your initials are several doorways of your name compressed into one mark.
normal.cn: 你的姓名缩写，就是把你名字的几道门槛压成一个记号。

normal.en: initial settings are the values a program has before it has walked anywhere.
normal.cn: initial settings 是一个程序还没走到任何地方时的值。

abstract.en: The core is a threshold: whatever stands just inside the opening is initial.
abstract.cn: 核心是一道门槛：刚跨进门口的那一点，就是 initial。

abstract.en: The same word names a time, a letter, and a position, because all three are 'the front of something'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名时间、字母和位置，因为三者都是“某物的最前面”。

abstract.en: Beginning and entering are one idea here: to begin is to step through a door.
abstract.cn: 在这里，“开始”与“进入”是同一个念头：开始就是跨过一道门。

examples.en: The initial estimate was far too low.
examples.cn: 最初的估算远远偏低。

examples.en: Her initials are written in gold on the cover.
examples.cn: 她的姓名首字母用金色写在封面上。

examples.en: The initial stage of the project lasted six months.
examples.cn: 项目的初始阶段持续了六个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ it（go 走）——刚走进门口的那一步 → initial 最初的；首字母

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开始、进入”，由 inire“走进、开始”而来（in-“进入”+ ire“走”）；核心是“刚跨进门的那一步”，故引申为“最初的”与“首字母”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one threshold: the first moment, the first letter, the letters that sign a name, the front position, the early stage, and the baseline before any change.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建在一道门槛上：最初的时刻、第一个字母、签名字母、最前面的位置、早期阶段，以及任何改变之前的基线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold; whatever stands at the opening is initial.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门槛；站在门口的一切都是 initial。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOMENT: what happens at the beginning, and the early stage of an illness.
branches.cn: 最初的时刻：开头发生的事，以及疾病的早期阶段。

branches.en: THE FIRST LETTER: the opening letter of a word, and its decorated manuscript form.
branches.cn: 第一个字母：词的开头字母，以及它在手抄本里的装饰形态。

branches.en: THE COMPACT SIGNATURE: initials standing for a name, and the act of signing with them.
branches.cn: 紧凑的签名：代表姓名的首字母，以及用它们签署的动作。

branches.en: THE FRONT SLOT: a letter at the start of a word or sentence, and the initial sound of a syllable.
branches.cn: 最前面的位置：词或句首的字母，以及音节的词首音。

branches.en: THE STARTING STATE: the default value or condition before a process changes it.
branches.cn: 起始状态：过程改变它之前的默认值或条件。

intro.en: Initial is in- plus it- plus -ial. Its family shows the prefix in-, the root it- from ire 'to go', and the suffixes -ial, -ly, -iate, -ion, -ive, -or, -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: initial 是 in- 加 it- 再加 -ial。它的词族展示前缀 in-，来自 ire“走”的词根 it-，以及后缀 -ial、-ly、-iate、-ion、-ive、-or、-ism、-ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire 'to go into' gives initium 'a beginning' and initialis 'of the beginning'. The same root produces initiate, initiation and initiative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inire“走入”给出 initium“开始”和 initialis“属于开始的”。同一个词根产生 initiate、initiation、initiative。

items.meaning: of the beginning; the first letter
items.meaningCN: 最初的；首字母（走进门的那一步）
items.example: Our initial plan was too ambitious.
items.exampleCN: 我们最初的计划过于宏大。

items.meaning: at first
items.meaningCN: 起初；最初（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: Initially, no one believed the story.
items.exampleCN: 起初没有人相信这个故事。

items.meaning: to begin; to bring someone into a practice
items.meaningCN: 开始；使入门（-iate 动词后缀）
items.example: They initiated a new health program.
items.exampleCN: 他们发起了一项新的健康计划。

items.meaning: the act of beginning or admitting a member
items.meaningCN: 开始；入会仪式（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The club's initiation includes a short test.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部的入会仪式包括一项小测试。

items.meaning: the power to act first; a new plan
items.meaningCN: 主动性；倡议（-ative 后缀）
items.example: She took the initiative and called the client.
items.exampleCN: 她主动打电话给了客户。

items.meaning: a person who starts something
items.meaningCN: 发起人（-or 表人）
items.example: He was the initiator of the reform.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场改革的发起人。

items.meaning: a word formed from first letters, each sounded separately
items.meaningCN: 首字母缩略词（如 FBI）
items.example: FBI is an initialism, not an acronym.
items.exampleCN: FBI 是首字母缩略词，不是首字母拼音词。

items.meaning: to set a device or program to its starting state
items.meaningCN: 初始化（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: The system initializes the drive on startup.
items.exampleCN: 系统在启动时会初始化该驱动器。

items.meaning: serving as an introduction or first rite
items.meaningCN: 入门的；起始的（-atory 形容词后缀）
items.example: The initiatory rite lasted three days.
items.exampleCN: 入门仪式持续了三天。

items.meaning: not yet introduced to a group or body of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 未入门的；外行的（un- 否定 + -ed）
items.example: The lecture assumed no knowledge, so the uninitiated could follow.
items.exampleCN: 这场讲座假定听众零基础，所以外行也能听懂。

latinEntries.meaning: to go into, enter upon, begin

definition_zh: 开始；发起；创始；使入门；接纳（入会）；（被）接纳者
definition_en: to begin something or set it going, or to bring someone into a practice or group
core_image: 一个人站在门槛上，被人牵着手跨进去；门里是一套他还不懂的秘密
scene: The CEO opens the meeting: We will initiate a review of the entire supply chain next week.
sceneCN: 这里 initiate 是「发起、启动」（第 2 个义项：正式让一项行动开始运转）；句意：我们下周将启动对整个供应链的审查。画面里有会议室、投影上的流程图和举手的经理。

pos.zh: 开始；发起；创始；使入门；接纳
新入会者；入门者
已入门的；受过传授的（古）

senses.title: To begin: step through the threshold
senses.titleCN: 开始、着手：跨过那道门槛
senses.definition: to begin an action or process
senses.definitionCN: 开始一项行动或过程
senses.example: The two countries initiated talks on a new trade deal.
senses.exampleCN: 两国就一项新的贸易协定开始了谈判。
senses.why: The verb is recorded c. 1600 as 'begin, set going', from Late Latin initiare 'to begin'. Behind it is initium 'a going in' — to begin is to step through a threshold.
senses.whyCN: 动词约在 1600 年记录为“开始、使运转”，来自晚期拉丁语 initiare“开始”。它背后是 initium“一次走入”——开始就是跨过一道门槛。

senses.title: To launch: be the first mover
senses.titleCN: 发起、创始：做第一个推动的人
senses.definition: to start a plan, movement, or institution, often as its first promoter
senses.definitionCN: 发起一项计划、运动或机构，常作为最初的推动者
senses.example: A group of parents initiated the campaign for a new library.
senses.exampleCN: 一群家长发起了争取新图书馆的运动。
senses.why: Because initiare also meant 'originate', the verb took on the role of naming the first mover. The one who initiates stands at the door and opens it for others.
senses.whyCN: 因为 initiare 也有“创始”之意，这个动词就承担了命名“第一个推动者”的角色。发起的人站在门口，替别人把门打开。

senses.title: To introduce: lead someone into a practice
senses.titleCN: 使入门：把一个人领进一门手艺
senses.definition: to introduce someone to a skill, subject, or practice
senses.definitionCN: 引导某人初次接触某项技能、学科或实践
senses.example: The course initiates students into the methods of field research.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把学生引入田野研究的方法。
senses.why: C. 1600 the word also meant 'introduce to some practice or system'. Classical Latin initiare meant 'to instruct in mysteries' — teaching was the first form of leading someone in.
senses.whyCN: 约 1600 年，这个词也指“引入某种实践或体系”。古典拉丁语 initiare 意为“传授秘仪”——教书就是把人领进门的第一种形式。

senses.title: To admit: bring a candidate inside the circle
senses.titleCN: 接纳加入：把候选人带进圈子
senses.definition: to admit someone into a group or secret society with a formal ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式仪式接纳某人进入团体或秘密会社
senses.example: The society initiates new members every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个会社每年春天接纳新成员。
senses.why: In classical Latin initiare meant 'to instruct in sacred knowledge' and to admit to the mysteries. The ceremony re-enacts the threshold: the candidate is brought from outside to inside.
senses.whyCN: 古典拉丁语 initiare 意为“传授神圣知识”，也指接纳进入秘仪。仪式重演那道门槛：候选人被从外面带到里面。

senses.title: The initiate: one who is already inside
senses.titleCN: 入门者：已经站在门里的人
senses.definition: a person who has been initiated into a group or body of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 已被接纳进入某团体或某知识体系的人
senses.example: Only the initiates were allowed to see the inner room.
senses.exampleCN: 只有入门者才被允许进入内室。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from 1732 as 'one who has been initiated'. It turns the past participle into a person: someone who has already crossed the threshold.
senses.whyCN: 名词记录于 1732 年，意为“已被接纳的人”。它把过去分词变成一个人：一个已经跨过门槛的人。

senses.title: Initiated: marked by what was taught
senses.titleCN: 已入门的：被所授之物标记过
senses.definition: having been instructed in secret or special knowledge; initiated
senses.definitionCN: 受过秘密或特殊知识传授的；已入门的
senses.example: The initiate priest alone knew the words of the rite.
senses.exampleCN: 只有那位已入门的祭司知道仪式的词句。
senses.why: An archaic past-participle adjective from c. 1600, from Latin initiatus. It describes the state left by the act: the person now stands inside, marked by what he was taught.
senses.whyCN: 这是约 1600 年出现的古旧过去分词形容词，来自拉丁语 initiatus。它描述动作留下的状态：此人如今站在门内，被所受的传授打了标记。

senses.title: To put forward: place a proposal at the door
senses.titleCN: 提出、引入：把议案放到门口
senses.definition: to formally put forward a proposal, measure, or legislation
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出提案、措施或立法
senses.example: The committee initiated a bill to regulate drone flights.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出了一项规范无人机飞行的法案。
senses.why: A proposal is the first step of a procedure, so the verb that means 'set going' naturally names the formal opening move. To initiate a bill is to place it on the threshold of becoming law.
senses.whyCN: 提案是程序的第一步，所以意为“使运转”的动词自然命名这个正式的开场动作。提出一项法案，就是把它放到“成为法律”的门槛上。

senses.title: To start a system: the on-switch
senses.titleCN: 启动系统：按下开关
senses.definition: to cause a device, program, or process to start operating
senses.definitionCN: 使设备、程序或过程开始运行
senses.example: The software initiates a backup every night at two.
senses.exampleCN: 软件每晚两点启动一次备份。
senses.why: Technical English keeps the oldest structure: a process stands waiting, and an initiating signal makes it step into motion. The threshold becomes an on-switch.
senses.whyCN: 技术英语保留了最古老的结构：一个过程站在那里等待，一个启动信号让它迈入运动。门槛在这里变成了开关。

senses.title: To trigger: the first link of a chain
senses.titleCN: 引发：链条上的第一环
senses.definition: to set off a chemical, physical, or biological process
senses.definitionCN: 引发化学、物理或生物过程
senses.example: The enzyme initiates the breakdown of starch.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶引发淀粉的分解。
senses.why: In science the first mover is a molecule or signal that opens a chain. Initiate marks the trigger event, the exact point where a dormant process enters its course.
senses.whyCN: 在科学里，第一推动者是一个打开链条的分子或信号。initiate 标记的是触发事件，即一个休眠过程进入轨道的那个准确点。

intro.en: Initiate and initial are siblings, both from Latin initium 'a beginning', literally 'a going in'. The religious sense 'instruct in the mysteries' came first in classical Latin, and 'begin' grew out of it in Late Latin.
intro.cn: initiate 与 initial 是同族词，都来自拉丁语 initium“开始”，字面是“一次走入”。古典拉丁语里先有宗教义“传授秘仪”，晚期拉丁语才从中长出“开始”。

items.en: Inire meant 'to go into, enter upon, begin', from in- 'into' plus ire 'to go'. The PIE root *ei- 'to go' is reconstructed, so the step below it is source uncertain.
items.cn: inire 意为“走入、着手、开始”，由 in-“进入”加 ire“走”构成。印欧语词根 *ei-“走”是重构形式，因此它下面的一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning; an entrance'. Its plural initia could mean 'constituent parts' or 'sacred mysteries', which prepared the religious sense of the verb.
items.cn: initium 意为“开始；入口”。它的复数 initia 可指“构成部分”或“神圣秘仪”，为动词的宗教义埋下伏笔。

items.en: In classical Latin initiare meant only 'to instruct in mysteries or sacred knowledge', to admit a person to secret rites. The everyday sense 'to begin' was not yet current.
items.cn: 在古典拉丁语里，initiare 只指“传授秘仪或神圣知识”，即接纳某人进入秘密仪式；“开始”这个日常义当时还未通行。

items.en: Late Latin initiare widened to 'to begin, originate'. The threshold image survived: to start anything is still to enter upon it.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 initiare 扩大到“开始、创始”。门槛意象仍在：开始任何事，仍然是“踏入”它。

items.en: Initiation is recorded from the 1580s, from French or Latin. The verb initiate appears c. 1600 with both 'introduce to a practice' and 'begin, set going'; some senses are back-formed from initiation.
items.cn: initiation 记录于 16 世纪 80 年代，来自法语或拉丁语。动词 initiate 约在 1600 年出现，兼有“引入某种实践”和“开始、使运转”两义；部分义项是由 initiation 逆构而成。

items.en: The noun initiate, 'one who has been initiated', is recorded from 1732, from an older past-participle adjective meaning 'instructed in secret knowledge'.
items.cn: 名词 initiate“已被接纳者”记录于 1732 年，来自更早的过去分词形容词“受过秘密知识传授的”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: of the beginning; the first letter. It is initi- plus -ial, the adjective beside the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；首字母。它是 initi- 加 -ial，是动词旁边的形容词。

entries.definition: the ability to act first, or a new proposal. It swaps -iate for -ative.
entries.definitionCN: 主动性；倡议。它把 -iate 换成 -ative。

entries.definition: the act of beginning something or admitting a new member. It is initiate plus -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；入会。它是 initiate 加 -ion。

entries.definition: to start doing or being something. It is the everyday word where initiate is formal.
entries.definitionCN: 开始。它是日常说法，而 initiate 更正式。

entries.definition: to start a major activity or put a product on the market. It stresses a public send-off.
entries.definitionCN: 发起；推出。它强调公开地“送出去”。

entries.definition: to begin, especially in formal or legal contexts. It shares the Latin initiare root through Vulgar Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 开始，尤用于正式或法律语境。它经通俗拉丁语与 initiare 同源。

entries.definition: to bring a person or thing into a place or subject for the first time. It matches the 'make familiar' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍；引入。它对应 initiate 的“使熟悉、使入门”义。

entries.definition: to admit someone formally into a group, office, or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 正式接纳……加入；就职。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin inire 'to go in', initium 'a beginning', initiare 'to instruct in mysteries', and the English family of initial, initiate, initiative.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 inire“走进”、initium“开始”、initiare“传授秘仪”，以及 initial、initiate、initiative 这一族英语词。

normal.en: initiate = in- 'into' + ire 'to go' + -ate: to go into something, hence to begin it.
normal.cn: initiate = in-“进入”+ ire“走”+ -ate：走进某事，因此就是开始它。

normal.en: The same initium gives initial and initiative: the first step, and the will to take it.
normal.cn: 同一个 initium 给出 initial 与 initiative：第一步，以及迈出第一步的意愿。

normal.en: The oldest sense was religious: to initiate was to lead a newcomer into the secret rites.
normal.cn: 最古老的一义是宗教的：initiate 就是把新人领进秘密仪式。

normal.en: To initiate a project is to open its door; the project then walks in.
normal.cn: 发起一个项目，就是替它开门；然后项目自己走进去。

normal.en: An initiate is someone who has already crossed the threshold and cannot be called an outsider.
normal.cn: an initiate 是已经跨过门槛的人，不能再算门外汉。

abstract.en: The core is a threshold crossed: beginning and being admitted are the same movement.
abstract.cn: 核心是跨过一道门槛：开始与被接纳是同一个动作。

abstract.en: The word moves from rite to project: first a secret ceremony, then any act of setting something going.
abstract.cn: 这个词从仪式走到项目：先是一场秘密仪式，再是任何让事情运转起来的行为。

abstract.en: Every sense has a first mover and a thing brought inside, whether a candidate, a bill, or a chemical reaction.
abstract.cn: 每个义项里都有一个第一推动者和一个被带进来的东西，无论那是候选人、法案还是化学反应。

examples.en: They plan to initiate a new training program in January.
examples.cn: 他们计划在一月启动一项新的培训计划。

examples.en: New members are initiated in a closed ceremony.
examples.cn: 新成员在一场不公开的仪式中正式入会。

examples.en: Scientists initiated the reaction by adding a catalyst.
examples.cn: 科学家通过加入催化剂引发了该反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ it（go 走）+ iate —— 走进门槛、把事情开头 → initiate 发起；使入门

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开始、进入”，来自 inire（in-“进入”+ ire“走”）；initiare 在古典拉丁语里专指“传授秘仪、引介入门”，因此兼有“开始”与“使入门”两义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses around one threshold: beginning, launching, teaching a newcomer, admitting a member, and the person or proposal that has crossed over. Technical use adds starting a system and triggering a chain.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕一道门槛：开始、发起、教新人、接纳成员，以及已经跨过去的人或议案。技术用法再加上“启动系统”和“引发链条”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold; someone or something is brought from outside to inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门槛；某人或某物被从外面带到里面。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOVE: beginning an action, and formally placing a proposal on the agenda.
branches.cn: 第一个动作：开始一项行动，以及正式把提案放上议程。

branches.en: THE FIRST PROMOTER: starting a plan or institution as its earliest backer.
branches.cn: 第一个推动者：作为最早的推动人发起计划或机构。

branches.en: LEARNING FROM INSIDE: teaching a practice, and the person who has already been taught.
branches.cn: 门内之学：传授一门实践，以及已经受过传授的人。

branches.en: THE RITE AND ITS MARK: admission by ceremony, and the state of being initiated.
branches.cn: 仪式与印记：通过仪式接纳，以及已入门的状态。

branches.en: THE TRIGGER: starting a system or process by an initiating signal.
branches.cn: 触发：用启动信号让系统或过程开始。

intro.en: Initiate is in- plus it- plus -iate. Its family shows the root it- from ire 'to go', the prefix in-, and the suffixes -ion, -ive, -or, -ory, -and and -ed.
intro.cn: initiate 是 in- 加 it- 再加 -iate。它的词族展示来自 ire“走”的词根 it-、前缀 in-，以及后缀 -ion、-ive、-or、-ory、-and、-ed。

latinIntro.en: Latin initiare 'to instruct in mysteries, begin' comes from initium 'a beginning', itself from inire 'to go into'. The family includes initiation, initiative and initiator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 initiare“传授秘仪、开始”来自 initium“开始”，而 initium 又来自 inire“走入”。这一族包括 initiation、initiative、initiator。

items.meaning: to begin; to admit into a practice
items.meaningCN: 开始；使入门（走进门）
items.example: The company initiated a review of its safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 公司启动了对安全规定的审查。

items.meaning: the act of beginning or admitting
items.meaningCN: 开始；入会仪式（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Her initiation into the lab took a full week.
items.exampleCN: 她进入实验室的入门培训花了整整一周。

items.meaning: the power to act first; a new plan
items.meaningCN: 主动性；倡议（-ative 后缀）
items.example: The mayor announced a housing initiative.
items.exampleCN: 市长宣布了一项住房倡议。

items.meaning: of the beginning; first
items.meaningCN: 最初的（同根形容词）
items.example: Their initial response was cautious.
items.exampleCN: 他们最初的反应很谨慎。

items.meaning: at first
items.meaningCN: 起初（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: Initially, the plan seemed too costly.
items.exampleCN: 起初，这个计划看起来太贵了。

items.meaning: one who starts something
items.meaningCN: 发起人（-or 表人）
items.example: She was the initiator of the school garden.
items.exampleCN: 她是学校菜园的发起人。

items.meaning: serving as an introduction
items.meaningCN: 入门的；起始的（-atory 后缀）
items.example: The initiatory steps are simple but slow.
items.exampleCN: 入门的步骤简单但缓慢。

items.meaning: a person about to be initiated
items.meaningCN: 即将入门的人（-and 表将要被……者）
items.example: Each initiand waited outside the door.
items.exampleCN: 每个即将入门的人都在门外等候。

items.meaning: not yet introduced to a group or subject
items.meaningCN: 未入门的；外行的
items.example: The film explains the jargon to the uninitiated.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片向外行解释了那些行话。

items.meaning: a set of first letters pronounced one by one
items.meaningCN: 首字母缩略词（同根）
items.example: UN is an initialism, not an acronym.
items.exampleCN: UN 是首字母缩略词，不是首字母拼音词。

latinEntries.meaning: to instruct in mysteries; to begin

definition_zh: 创新；革新；新事物；新方法；新发明
definition_en: the act of bringing something new into use, or the new thing itself
core_image: 一间老作坊的墙上被凿开一扇新窗，光从没见过的方向照进来
scene: An engineer holds a prototype and says: The real innovation is not the chip but the way it saves power.
sceneCN: 这里 innovation 是「创新（新做法/新事物）」（第 2 个义项：被引入的新东西本身）；句意：真正的创新不是芯片，而是它省电的方式。画面里有原型机、测试台和写满数据的白板。

pos.zh: 创新；革新；新事物；新方法

senses.title: Bringing in the new: the process
senses.titleCN: 引入新事物：作为一个过程
senses.definition: the act or process of introducing something new into an established system
senses.definitionCN: 把新东西引入既有体系的行为或过程
senses.example: Innovation requires both new ideas and the will to test them.
senses.exampleCN: 创新既需要新点子，也需要去检验它们的意愿。
senses.why: Recorded mid-15c. as 'restoration, renewal', from Late Latin innovare 'to change, renew' (in- 'into' + novus 'new'). The word first meant making something new again; the modern 'bringing in something new' keeps the same movement.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期记录为“恢复、更新”，来自晚期拉丁语 innovare“改变、使新”（in-“进入”+ novus“新”）。这个词最初指“让某物重新变新”；现代“引入新东西”的义项保留了同一个动作。

senses.title: The new thing: what has been brought in
senses.titleCN: 新事物：被带进来的那个东西
senses.definition: a new thing, method, or device that has been introduced
senses.definitionCN: 已被引入的新东西、新方法或新装置
senses.example: The electric bus was a genuine innovation in city transport.
senses.exampleCN: 电动公交车是城市交通中一项真正的创新。
senses.why: From the 1540s the noun also meant 'a new thing introduced in an established arrangement'. The act leaves behind an object, and the object takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 40 年代起，名词也指“被引入既有格局的新东西”。动作留下了一个物件，这个物件就继承了同一个名字。

senses.title: Reform: the system itself is changed
senses.titleCN: 革新：被改动的是整个制度
senses.definition: a change in institutions, customs, or systems, often one that departs from tradition
senses.definitionCN: 制度、习俗或体系上的改变，常指偏离传统
senses.example: The reform brought several innovations to the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革给税制带来了好几项革新。
senses.why: Because innovare meant 'to change', the word can name reform of a whole arrangement, not only a gadget. Anything that alters an old order by introducing something new qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 因为 innovare 意为“改变”，这个词可以命名整个格局的改革，而不只是一个小装置。任何通过引入新东西来改动旧秩序的事物都算。

senses.title: Renewal: the oldest sense, making new again
senses.titleCN: 更新、复兴：最古老的一义，让旧的重新变新
senses.definition: the renewal or restoration of something old, the word's earliest sense
senses.definitionCN: 对旧事物的更新或恢复，这是该词最早的义项
senses.example: The monastery's innovation of the old rite surprised the bishops.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院对古老仪式的更新让主教们感到意外。
senses.why: Mid-15c. innovacion meant 'restoration, renewal'. The prefix in- was read as 'into' and novus as 'new': to make new again. The older layer survives in religious and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期的 innovacion 意为“恢复、更新”。前缀 in- 被理解为“进入”，novus 为“新”：让旧的重新变新。这一旧义仍活在宗教与历史写作中。

senses.title: Technology: the new machine or method
senses.titleCN: 技术创新：新机器或新方法
senses.definition: a new technology or a new way of applying technical knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 新技术，或应用技术知识的新方式
senses.example: Solar cells were once a laboratory innovation and are now routine.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能电池曾是实验室里的创新，如今已是常规。
senses.why: Modern usage narrows the general sense to machines and methods. When the new thing is technical, English simply puts technology beside the word; innovation itself already carries the idea of a new application.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把一般义收窄到机器与方法。当新东西是技术性的，英语只需在词前加 technology；innovation 本身已带着“新应用”的意思。

senses.title: A new way of doing: the experimental variation
senses.titleCN: 新做法：一次实验性的变化
senses.definition: a novel change or experimental variation in how something is done
senses.definitionCN: 做事方式上新颖的改变或实验性变化
senses.example: The teacher's innovation was to let students choose their own reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师的创新是让学生自己选择读物。
senses.why: The 1540s sense includes 'experimental variation'. An innovation need not be a product; it can be a different way of doing an old task, tried out to see whether it works.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 40 年代的义项包含“实验性变化”。创新不必是一件产品；它可以是把旧任务换一种做法，试一下看行不行。

senses.title: The idea: newness before it is built
senses.titleCN: 新点子：尚未落地的新意
senses.definition: a new idea or fresh approach, especially one with practical promise
senses.definitionCN: 新想法或新思路，尤指有实际前景的
senses.example: Her innovation was to turn the empty lot into a community garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新点子是把那块空地变成社区花园。
senses.why: An idea is the first form a new thing takes. Before it is built or adopted, the innovation exists in the mind as a proposal — the seed of the introduced change.
senses.whyCN: 想法是新事物采取的第一种形态。在被造出或采纳之前，创新以提案的形式存在于脑中——它是那次引入的种子。

senses.title: Newness as a quality: how far it departs
senses.titleCN: 创新性：偏离旧路有多远
senses.definition: the quality of being new or original in approach
senses.definitionCN: 在做法上新颖、原创的特质
senses.example: Critics praised the film's innovation rather than its budget.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞的是这部影片的创新性，而不是它的预算。
senses.why: Abstract nouns often grow from countable ones: innovation as a thing becomes innovation as a quality. The word then measures how far a work departs from what already exists.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词常从可数名词长出来：作为“事物”的 innovation 变成作为“性质”的 innovation。于是这个词开始衡量一件作品偏离既有之物有多远。

senses.title: The introduction: the moment of entry
senses.titleCN: 引入：新东西跨进门的那一刻
senses.definition: the introduction or adoption of something new, considered as an event
senses.definitionCN: 把新事物引入或采纳，被视为一个事件
senses.example: The innovation of remote voting changed turnout in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 远程投票的引入改变了农村地区的投票率。
senses.why: Here the noun names the moment of bringing in. The same -ation ending that marks an action in Latin marks the crossing of the new thing into use.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名的是“带进来”的那一刻。拉丁语里标记动作的同一个 -ation 词尾，标记了新事物跨入使用的那一步。

intro.en: Innovation is built on Latin novus 'new'. Its first English sense was 'renewal', and only later did it mean a new thing brought into an old arrangement.
intro.cn: innovation 建在拉丁语 novus“新”上。它最早的英语义是“更新”，后来才指被带进旧格局的新事物。

items.en: The root *newo- 'new' is reconstructed from many daughter languages, but it is not written anywhere; as a reconstruction its status is source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *newo-“新”是从众多子语言中重构出来的，但没有任何书面记载；作为重构形式，它的地位标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Novus meant 'new'. From it came the verb novare 'to make new, renew', the base of the whole family.
items.cn: novus 意为“新的”。由它产生动词 novare“使新、更新”，成为整个词族的基础。

items.en: Innovare meant 'to change; to renew', built from in- 'into' plus novare 'to make new'. The sense 'bring in something new' grew from 'make new'.
items.cn: innovare 意为“改变；更新”，由 in-“进入”加 novare“使新”构成。“引入新事物”的义项是从“使新”长出来的。

items.en: Innovatio (stem innovation-) was the noun of action from innovare, naming the act of renewing or changing.
items.cn: innovatio（词干 innovation-）是 innovare 的动作名词，命名更新或改变的行为。

items.en: The noun enters English as innovacion, 'restoration, renewal'. The modern meaning was not yet present.
items.cn: 名词以 innovacion 进入英语，意为“恢复、更新”。现代义当时尚未出现。

items.en: The sense 'a novel change, experimental variation, new thing introduced in an established arrangement' is recorded from the 1540s and becomes the dominant modern meaning.
items.cn: “新颖的改变、实验性变化、被引入既有格局的新事物”这一义项记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，并成为现代主要含义。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the repair and renewal of a building. It swaps in- for re- and keeps the -novation ending.
entries.definitionCN: 翻新；整修。它把 in- 换成 re-，保留 -novation 词尾。

entries.definition: introducing new ideas or methods. It is innovation turned into an adjective with -ive.
entries.definitionCN: 创新的；有新意的。它是 innovation 加 -ive 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a person who introduces new methods or ideas. It adds -or to the verb innovate.
entries.definitionCN: 创新者。它是动词 innovate 加 -or 表人。

entries.definition: the creation of something that did not exist before. It names the making; innovation names the bringing into use.
entries.definitionCN: 发明；创造。它命名“造出”，而 innovation 命名“引入使用”。

entries.definition: the quality of being new, or a new and unusual thing. It stresses freshness more than practical adoption.
entries.definitionCN: 新颖；新奇事物。它更强调新鲜感，而非实际采纳。

entries.definition: a change made to improve an institution or system. It overlaps innovation as institutional change.
entries.definitionCN: 改革。它与 innovation 的“制度革新”义重叠。

entries.definition: an important discovery that removes a barrier. It is a sudden innovation, not a gradual one.
entries.definitionCN: 突破。它是突然的创新，而不是渐进的。

entries.definition: the act of making something exist. It is broader than innovation, which implies an existing setting.
entries.definitionCN: 创造。它比 innovation 更宽，后者隐含一个既有的环境。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin novus 'new', novare 'to renew', Late Latin innovare, and the English words novel, novelty, renovate.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 novus“新”、novare“更新”、晚期拉丁语 innovare，以及英语 novel、novelty、renovate。

normal.en: innovation = in- 'into' + novus 'new' + -ation: a new thing brought in.
normal.cn: innovation = in-“进入”+ novus“新”+ -ation：把新东西带进来。

normal.en: novus is everywhere: novel, novelty, renovate and novice all carry the same 'new'.
normal.cn: novus 无处不在：novel、novelty、renovate、novice 都带着同一个“新”。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was 'renewal' — to make the old new again.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义是“更新”——让旧的重新变新。

normal.en: An innovator is literally one who puts newness into an existing arrangement.
normal.cn: innovator 字面上就是把“新”放进既有格局的人。

normal.en: technological innovation is a new method entering an old workshop.
normal.cn: technological innovation 就是一种新方法走进老作坊。

abstract.en: The core is a new window cut into an old wall: the light comes from an unfamiliar direction.
abstract.cn: 核心是在老墙上凿出一扇新窗：光从陌生的方向照进来。

abstract.en: The word moves from act to object to quality: introducing, the new thing, its newness.
abstract.cn: 这个词从动作走到对象，再走到性质：引入、新事物、它的新。

abstract.en: Renovation and innovation share novus; one makes the old new again, the other brings the new in.
abstract.cn: renovation 与 innovation 共享 novus；一个让旧的重新变新，一个把新的带进来。

examples.en: The company owes its success to constant innovation.
examples.cn: 这家公司的成功归功于持续创新。

examples.en: Free public transport was an innovation the city soon copied.
examples.cn: 免费公共交通是一项创新，很快被其他城市效仿。

examples.en: Her innovation was to use waste heat to warm the greenhouse.
examples.cn: 她的创新之处是用废热来给温室供暖。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ nov（new 新）+ ation —— 把新东西搬进老体系 → innovation 创新

root: 源自拉丁语 novus“新”，经 novare“使新”、晚期拉丁语 innovare“更新、改变”与 innovatio 进入英语；核心是“把新的东西带进原有的秩序”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses around one new thing entering an old order: the act, the thing itself, the reform of a system, the renewal of something old, a new method, a new idea, and the quality of newness.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕“新东西进入旧秩序”：行为、事物本身、制度革新、旧物的更新、新方法、新点子，以及“新”这种性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something new is brought through the wall of an established order.
core.cn: 核心意象：某种新东西被带过既有秩序的那堵墙。

branches.en: THE ACT OF BRINGING IN: the process of innovation, and its moment of entry.
branches.cn: 引入之举：创新的过程，以及它跨进门的那一刻。

branches.en: THE NEW THING: the introduced object, and the idea before it is built.
branches.cn: 新事物：被引入的物件，以及它被造出之前的点子。

branches.en: CHANGING THE ARRANGEMENT: reform of a system, and an experimental new way of doing a task.
branches.cn: 改动格局：制度的革新，以及做同一件事的实验性新做法。

branches.en: MAKING THE OLD NEW AGAIN: the earliest sense, restoration and renewal.
branches.cn: 让旧的重新变新：最早的义项，恢复与更新。

branches.en: TECHNOLOGY AND ITS NEWNESS: a new technical method, and the quality of departing from the old.
branches.cn: 技术与其新意：新的技术方法，以及偏离旧路的那种性质。

intro.en: Innovation is in- plus nov- plus -ation. Its family shows the prefix in- and re-, the root nov- 'new', and the suffixes -ate, -ive, -or, -ly, -el, -ty and -ice.
intro.cn: innovation 是 in- 加 nov- 再加 -ation。它的词族展示前缀 in-、re-，词根 nov-“新”，以及后缀 -ate、-ive、-or、-ly、-el、-ty、-ice。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus 'new' gives novare 'to make new' and Late Latin innovare 'to change, renew'. The same root yields novel, novelty, renovate and novice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus“新”给出 novare“使新”和晚期拉丁语 innovare“改变、更新”。同一词根还给出 novel、novelty、renovate、novice。

items.meaning: the act of bringing in something new
items.meaningCN: 创新；新事物（把新带入）
items.example: The firm invests heavily in innovation.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在创新上投入很大。

items.meaning: to introduce new methods or ideas
items.meaningCN: 创新；革新（-ate 动词后缀）
items.example: Small teams often innovate faster than large ones.
items.exampleCN: 小团队往往比大团队创新更快。

items.meaning: introducing or using new ideas
items.meaningCN: 创新的；有新意的（-ive 形容词后缀）
items.example: They designed an innovative cooling system.
items.exampleCN: 他们设计了一套创新的冷却系统。

items.meaning: a person who introduces new things
items.meaningCN: 创新者（-or 表人）
items.example: She is regarded as an innovator in textile design.
items.exampleCN: 她被视为纺织品设计领域的创新者。

items.meaning: in a new and original way
items.meaningCN: 创新地（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: The space is used innovatively as a classroom.
items.exampleCN: 这个空间被创造性地用作教室。

items.meaning: new and unusual; also a long story
items.meaningCN: 新奇的；小说（同根）
items.example: The team tried a novel approach to the old problem.
items.exampleCN: 团队对这个老问题尝试了一种新方法。

items.meaning: the quality of being new; a new thing
items.meaningCN: 新颖；新奇事物（-ty 名词后缀）
items.example: The novelty of the game faded after a week.
items.exampleCN: 这个游戏的新鲜感一周后就消退了。

items.meaning: to make an old building new again
items.meaningCN: 翻新；整修（re- 再 + 使新）
items.example: They renovated the school library last summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年夏天翻新了学校图书馆。

items.meaning: a person new to a field
items.meaningCN: 新手；初学者（同根“新”）
items.example: As a novice, he asked a lot of questions.
items.exampleCN: 作为新手，他问了很多问题。

items.meaning: having the nature of an innovation
items.meaningCN: 创新的；革新的（-ory 形容词后缀）
items.example: The plan had an innovatory character from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划从一开始就带有革新性质。

definition_zh: 输入；投入；输入的数据；意见；进言
definition_en: something put in, such as data, money, energy, or advice, or the act of putting it in
core_image: 一只手把原料从入口倒进机器，机器才开始转动
scene: A manager looks at the survey and says: We need input from the staff before we change the schedule.
sceneCN: 这里 input 是「意见、建议」（第 4 个义项：为决策提供的看法与信息）；句意：改排班之前我们需要员工的意见。画面里有问卷、会议室和写满便签的白板。

pos.zh: 输入；投入；输入数据；意见；输入端
输入（数据）；进言；提供（意见）

senses.title: Data in: what the machine is fed
senses.titleCN: 数据输入：喂给机器的东西
senses.definition: data or signals fed into a computer or program
senses.definitionCN: 送入计算机或程序的数据或信号
senses.example: The program crashed because of a corrupt input.
senses.exampleCN: 程序因一条损坏的输入数据而崩溃。
senses.why: The computing sense 'data fed into a machine' is recorded from 1948, perhaps from the verb. The image is the old one: something is put in at the opening so the machine can work.
senses.whyCN: 计算机义“送入机器的数据”记录于 1948 年，可能来自动词。意象仍是旧的那个：从入口放进东西，机器才能工作。

senses.title: To key in: put the data in yourself
senses.titleCN: 输入动作：亲手把数据放进去
senses.definition: to enter data or text into a computer or device
senses.definitionCN: 把数据或文字录入计算机或设备
senses.example: Please input your student number and press enter.
senses.exampleCN: 请输入你的学号，然后按回车。
senses.why: The modern verb 'feed data into a machine' is from 1946, a new formation from in + put. The very old verb meant 'put on, impose'; the machine merely gave the old act a new object.
senses.whyCN: 现代动词“把数据送入机器”记录于 1946 年，是 in + put 的新组合。这个很老的动词本指“放在……上、施加”；机器只是给这个旧动作换了一个新对象。

senses.title: Money and effort: what a project is fed
senses.titleCN: 资金与力气：喂给项目的投入
senses.definition: money, materials, or effort put into a project to make it work
senses.definitionCN: 为使项目运转而投入的资金、物资或人力
senses.example: The farm needs a large input of water before the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 农场在收获前需要大量灌溉用水。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from 1753 as 'a sum of cash put in, a contribution'. Whatever is poured in at the start — cash, fuel, labor — is an input.
senses.whyCN: 名词记录于 1753 年，意为“投入的一笔钱、一份贡献”。开始时倒进去的任何东西——现金、燃料、劳力——都是 input。

senses.title: Advice in: what people put into a decision
senses.titleCN: 意见输入：人们放进决策里的看法
senses.definition: advice, comments, or information that people provide to improve a plan or decision
senses.definitionCN: 人们为改进计划或决策而提供的建议、评论或信息
senses.example: The committee asked for input from local residents.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会向当地居民征求意见。
senses.why: Once input means anything contributed, opinions become a contribution too. What people put in at a meeting is information the decision can use.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 input 泛指任何被贡献的东西，意见也就成了一种贡献。人们在会上放进去的，正是决策可以使用的信息。

senses.title: Contribution: the oldest noun sense
senses.titleCN: 贡献：名词最古老的一义
senses.definition: a contribution or share that someone puts into a joint effort
senses.definitionCN: 某人为共同事业投入的一份贡献或份额
senses.example: Every member's input made the report stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 每位成员的贡献都让这份报告更有力。
senses.why: 1753 'a sharing, contribution' is the word's first noun sense, from the phrase put in. To contribute is literally to put something into the common store.
senses.whyCN: 1753 年的“分享、贡献”是这个词最早的名词义，来自短语 put in。贡献，字面上就是往公共的仓库里放东西。

senses.title: Power in: energy supplied to a machine
senses.titleCN: 能量输入：供给机器的动力
senses.definition: the energy or power supplied to a machine or system
senses.definitionCN: 供给机器或系统的能量或功率
senses.example: The motor's power input is measured in watts.
senses.exampleCN: 这台电机的输入功率以瓦特计。
senses.why: The sense 'energy supplied to a device or machine' is dated to 1902, before electronics. A machine cannot produce work without something flowing in at its inlet.
senses.whyCN: “供给装置或机器的能量”这一义项可追溯到 1902 年，早于电子时代。没有东西从入口流进来，机器就无法做功。

senses.title: The port: where the putting-in happens
senses.titleCN: 输入端：放东西进去的那个口
senses.definition: the terminal, port, or channel through which something enters a device
senses.definitionCN: 某物进入设备的接线端、端口或通道
senses.example: Plug the microphone into the audio input.
senses.exampleCN: 把麦克风插到音频输入端。
senses.why: By naming the place rather than the thing, English makes input a doorway. The port is where the put-in happens, so it takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 英语用这个名字指地方而不是东西，于是 input 成了一道门。端口正是“放进去”发生的地方，所以就继承了动作的名字。

senses.title: Signal in: the entering side of a circuit
senses.titleCN: 输入信号：电路进门的一侧
senses.definition: a signal or information entering an electronic system
senses.definitionCN: 进入电子系统的信号或信息
senses.example: The sensor sends a weak input to the amplifier.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器向放大器发送一个微弱的输入信号。
senses.why: Electronics splits a system into an entering side and a leaving side: input and output. The input is the signal at the gate, before the circuit transforms it.
senses.whyCN: 电子学把一个系统分成进门的一侧和出门的一侧：input 与 output。输入就是门前的信号，尚未被电路改变。

senses.title: To offer a view: put words into a discussion
senses.titleCN: 进言：把话放进讨论里
senses.definition: to offer advice or information for a decision
senses.definitionCN: 为决策提供建议或信息
senses.example: The engineers input their concerns before the design was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们在设计定稿前提出了他们的顾虑。
senses.why: The verb extends from putting data into a machine to putting views into a discussion. In both cases someone places something into a system that will act on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从“把数据放进机器”延伸到“把看法放进讨论”。两种情况下，都是有人把东西放进一个会据此行动的系统。

intro.en: Input is not a Latin word. It is a native compound of in and put, first naming money put into a common fund, then energy into a machine, and only in the 1940s data into a computer.
intro.cn: input 不是拉丁词，而是 in 与 put 的本地复合词。它先指放进公共钱袋的钱，再指供给机器的能量，直到 20 世纪 40 年代才指送进计算机的数据。

items.en: Put comes from a Germanic stem meaning 'to thrust, push, place', seen in Danish putte and Middle Dutch poten. Its deeper origin is not established, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: put 来自一个意为“推、戳、放置”的日耳曼语词干，见于丹麦语 putte、中古荷兰语 poten。它更深的来源未被确立，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: In and inne meant 'in, into, within', from Proto-Germanic *in and PIE *en 'in'. The two forms merged in Middle English.
items.cn: in 与 inne 意为“在内、进入、在……之中”，来自原始日耳曼语 *in 与印欧语 *en“在内”。两种形式在中古英语中合并。

items.en: The verb input is recorded as 'put on, impose', a plain combination of in plus put. It had nothing to do with machines.
items.cn: 动词 input 记录为“放在……上、施加”，只是 in 加 put 的朴素组合，与机器毫无关系。

items.en: The noun input appears as 'a sum of cash put in, a sharing, contribution'. This is the source of the modern senses of money and effort.
items.cn: 名词 input 出现，意为“投入的一笔钱、一份分享、一份贡献”。现代“资金与人力投入”的义项就源于此。

items.en: The meaning 'energy supplied to a device or machine' is recorded from 1902, later applied to electronic devices.
items.cn: “供给装置或机器的能量”这一义项记录于 1902 年，后来应用到电子设备上。

items.en: The verb 'feed data into a machine' is recorded from 1946; the noun's computing sense 'data fed into a machine' from 1948. The old compound simply gained a new object.
items.cn: 动词“把数据送入机器”记录于 1946 年；名词的计算机义“送入机器的数据”记录于 1948 年。这个老复合词只是换了一个新对象。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: what a machine or system produces. It swaps in- for out- and keeps the -put.
entries.definitionCN: 输出；产量。它把 in- 换成 out-，保留 -put。

entries.definition: the amount taken in, as of food or air. It is in- plus take, the same shape as input.
entries.definitionCN: 摄入量；吸纳量。它是 in- 加 take，与 input 同构。

entries.definition: a small opening through which liquid or air enters. It is literally a letting-in place.
entries.definitionCN: 进水口；入口。它字面上就是“让……进来”的地方。

entries.definition: something given to a common effort. It is the oldest sense of input, widened to any gift.
entries.definitionCN: 贡献；捐助。它是 input 最古老的义项，扩大到任何给予。

entries.definition: comments about how well something worked, used to improve it. It is input about the output.
entries.definitionCN: 反馈。它是针对输出所给的输入。

entries.definition: money or resources put into something for a future return. It matches input as financial contribution.
entries.definitionCN: 投资。它对应 input 的“资金投入”义。

entries.definition: an opinion offered to help someone decide. It matches the 'input from staff' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 建议。它对应“员工的意见”这一义项。

entries.definition: facts or figures that a system can process. It is the content of a computing input.
entries.definitionCN: 数据。它是计算机输入的内容。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: input is the native compound in + put, and the same pattern gives output, throughput, intake and inlet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：input 是本地复合词 in + put，同样的结构给出 output、throughput、intake、inlet。

normal.en: input = in + put: put something in.
normal.cn: input = in + put：把东西放进去。

normal.en: output is its mirror image: out + put, what is put out.
normal.cn: output 是它的镜像：out + put，被放出来的东西。

normal.en: throughput is through + put: what passes through a system.
normal.cn: throughput 是 through + put：穿过系统的量。

normal.en: The noun began as money put in, not as data; the computer sense is only from 1948.
normal.cn: 这个名词最初指放进去的钱，而不是数据；计算机义直到 1948 年才有。

normal.en: An input port is simply the place where the putting-in happens.
normal.cn: input port 就是“放进去”这件事发生的地方。

abstract.en: The core is an inlet: an opening through which something enters a system.
abstract.cn: 核心是一个入口：某物由此进入一个系统。

abstract.en: One word names both the act and the thing: the putting in and what is put in.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名动作也命名事物：放进去，以及被放进去的东西。

abstract.en: Data, money, energy and advice are all the same move: something placed into a system that will act on it.
abstract.cn: 数据、金钱、能量和意见都是同一个动作：把某物放进一个会据此行动的系统。

examples.en: The model needs more input from real patients.
examples.cn: 这个模型需要更多来自真实病人的数据。

examples.en: Farmers must balance their inputs of water and fertilizer.
examples.cn: 农民必须平衡水和肥料的投入。

examples.en: All data is input through a single terminal.
examples.cn: 所有数据都通过一个终端输入。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ put（放）——把东西放进去 → input 输入；投入；意见

root: 由日耳曼语 in“进入”与 put“放置”复合而成，字面是“把东西放进去”；1753 年先指“投入的钱/贡献”，20 世纪才转为“输入的数据、能量与意见”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one opening: data into a computer, money and energy into a machine, advice into a decision, and the port where all of it enters.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项建在同一个入口上：数据进入计算机、资金与能量进入机器、意见进入决策，以及所有这些进入时所经过的端口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an opening through which something is put into a system.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个入口，某物由此被放进系统。

branches.en: DATA AND SIGNAL: what a computer is fed, and the entering side of a circuit.
branches.cn: 数据与信号：喂给计算机的东西，以及电路进门的一侧。

branches.en: THE ACT OF PUTTING IN: keying data, and offering a view to a discussion.
branches.cn: 放入的动作：录入数据，以及把看法放进讨论。

branches.en: MONEY AND ENERGY: resources fed to a project, and power fed to a machine.
branches.cn: 资金与能量：投给项目的资源，以及供给机器的动力。

branches.en: ADVICE AND CONTRIBUTION: opinions offered, and the oldest sense of a share put in.
branches.cn: 意见与贡献：提供的看法，以及最古老的“投入一份”之义。

branches.en: THE PORT: the place where the putting-in happens.
branches.cn: 端口：放入这件事发生的地点。

intro.en: Input is in plus put, a native compound rather than a prefixed Latin root. Its family shows the prefixes in- and out-, the root put, and the suffixes -ing and -er.
intro.cn: input 是 in 加 put，是本地复合词，而不是拉丁词根加前缀。它的词族展示前缀 in-、out-，词根 put，以及后缀 -ing、-er。

latinIntro.en: Input has no Latin ancestry: both in and put are Germanic. Latin offers only a comparison, in- plus ponere 'to place', seen in imponere 'to put in, impose'; this is an analogue, not the source.
latinIntro.cn: input 没有拉丁语血统：in 与 put 都属日耳曼语。拉丁语只能作对照：in- 加 ponere“放置”，见于 imponere“放入、施加”；那是类比，不是它的来源。

items.meaning: to put data or resources in; what is put in
items.meaningCN: 输入；投入（把东西放进去）
items.example: They input the figures into the shared sheet.
items.exampleCN: 他们把数字输入共享表格。

items.meaning: what is produced or sent out
items.meaningCN: 输出；产量（放出来的东西）
items.example: The factory doubled its output in two years.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂两年内产量翻了一番。

items.meaning: the amount passing through a system in a given time
items.meaningCN: 吞吐量；处理量（穿过并放出）
items.example: The new port has a higher throughput.
items.exampleCN: 新港口的吞吐量更高。

items.meaning: to place or thrust something somewhere
items.meaningCN: 放；置（本词的词根）
items.example: Put the box on the table.
items.exampleCN: 把箱子放在桌上。

items.meaning: the amount taken in
items.meaningCN: 摄入量；吸纳（in + 取）
items.example: Reduce your intake of sugar.
items.exampleCN: 减少糖的摄入量。

items.meaning: an opening that lets liquid or air in
items.meaningCN: 入口；进水口（in + 让）
items.example: The lake has a narrow inlet from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这个湖有一条通向海的狭窄入口。

items.meaning: a movement of liquid, money, or people into somewhere
items.meaningCN: 流入（in + 流）
items.example: The dam controls the inflow to the reservoir.
items.exampleCN: 大坝控制着流入水库的水量。

items.meaning: present from birth
items.meaningCN: 天生的（in + 出生）
items.example: She has an inborn sense of rhythm.
items.exampleCN: 她有一种天生的节奏感。

items.meaning: the activity of entering data
items.meaningCN: 输入过程（-ing 动名词）
items.example: Manual inputting is slow and error-prone.
items.exampleCN: 手工输入既慢又容易出错。

items.meaning: a person who enters data
items.meaningCN: 录入员（-er 表人）
items.example: The inputter checks each record before saving it.
items.exampleCN: 录入员在保存前核对每条记录。

definition_zh: 插入；嵌入；植入；登载（文字）；插入物；夹页广告
definition_en: to put or place something inside another thing, or a thing so placed, especially a printed sheet enclosed in a publication
core_image: 一只手把一张薄片对准已经排好的一行缝隙，把它稳稳塞进中间，让原来的顺序多出一个位置
scene: A technician holds a memory card above a laptop and says: Insert the card into the slot until it clicks.
sceneCN: 这里 insert 是「插入、放入」（第 1 个义项：把一件东西放进另一件东西内部的空位）；句意：把存储卡插入卡槽，直到咔哒一声。画面里有存储卡、卡槽和指示灯。

pos.zh: 插入；放入；植入；登载；介入
插入物；夹页；插页广告；插入镜头

senses.title: Put one thing inside another
senses.titleCN: 插入：把一件东西放进另一件东西内部
senses.definition: to put or place something into a space or opening inside something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放进另一物体内部的空位或开口中
senses.example: Insert the key into the lock and turn it clockwise.
senses.exampleCN: 把钥匙插进锁里，然后顺时针转动。
senses.why: Insert is recorded in the 1520s from Latin inserere, in- 'in' plus serere 'to join, arrange in a row'. The earliest image is not simply pushing, but placing something into an ordered line or gap.
senses.whyCN: insert 于 16 世纪 20 年代记录，来自拉丁语 inserere，即 in-“向内”加 serere“连接、排成一行”。最早的形象不只是推入，而是把东西放进一个有秩序的队列或缝隙里。

senses.title: Graft or implant living tissue
senses.titleCN: 植入；嫁接：把活的组织接到另一处
senses.definition: to graft a shoot or implant tissue, a gene, or a device into a living body or plant
senses.definitionCN: 把枝条嫁接，或把组织、基因、器械植入活的植物或身体中
senses.example: Scientists inserted a drought-resistant gene into the rice plant.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把一段抗旱基因植入水稻植株。
senses.why: Latin inserere was used for grafting a shoot into a stock, literally joining one living line to another. The agricultural image of grafting survives in modern medical and genetic uses of insert.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inserere 本就用于把枝条嫁接到砧木上，字面是把一条活的东西接到另一条上。嫁接的农业形象留在现代医学与基因学的 insert 用法里。

senses.title: Add words into a text
senses.titleCN: 增补文字：在一行字里加进词句
senses.definition: to add a word, sentence, or paragraph to a piece of writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 在书面或口头表达中加入词、句或段落
senses.example: The editor inserted a short explanation after the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在第一段后面加了一段简短说明。
senses.why: Writing is imagined as a line or row, which is exactly what serere means. To insert a sentence is to make it join the existing row of words, not to replace the row.
senses.whyCN: 写作被想象成一条线或一行，而 serere 的意思正是“排成一行”。插入一句话，就是让它加入原有的词行，而不是替换整行。

senses.title: Place an advertisement in media
senses.titleCN: 插播广告：把广告塞进媒体内容里
senses.definition: to place an advertisement or announcement within a newspaper, magazine, broadcast, or web page
senses.definitionCN: 把广告或通告放进报纸、杂志、广播或网页的内容中
senses.example: The agency inserted a thirty-second spot into the evening news.
senses.exampleCN: 广告公司在晚间新闻中插播了一段三十秒的广告。
senses.why: Once insert named the act of placing a sheet among printed pages, it was natural to insert an advertisement among them. The 1893 noun insert, 'something inserted', fixed the media sense.
senses.whyCN: 当 insert 已经指把一张纸放进印刷页面之间，把广告插进其中就顺理成章。1893 年的名词 insert“被插入之物”固定了这层媒体义。

senses.title: The inserted sheet itself
senses.titleCN: 夹页；插页：被塞进去的那张纸
senses.definition: a printed sheet, card, or advertisement placed inside a newspaper, magazine, or book
senses.definitionCN: 夹在报纸、杂志或书中的印刷页、卡片或广告
senses.example: The Sunday paper came with a colorful grocery insert.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的报纸里夹着一份色彩鲜艳的超市促销页。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from 1893 as 'something inserted', especially a paper placed among the pages of a newspaper or magazine. English often turns an action verb into a noun for the object produced by the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词自 1893 年起记录为“被插入之物”，尤指夹在报纸或杂志页面间的纸页。英语常把动作动词转成名词，指动作产生的那件东西。

senses.title: Place a device or instrument inside
senses.titleCN: 置入器械：把工具或导管放进体内或机器内
senses.definition: to place a tube, needle, probe, or other instrument into a body, machine, or opening
senses.definitionCN: 把导管、针头、探头等器械放入身体、机器或开口中
senses.example: The nurse inserted the catheter with steady hands.
senses.exampleCN: 护士稳稳地把导管置入。
senses.why: This is sense 01 narrowed by technical context: the thing placed is an instrument, and the opening is a body or a port. No new root meaning is added, only precision.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 1 义在技术语境中的收窄：被放进去的是器械，开口是身体或接口。词根意义没有新增，只是更精确。

senses.title: Push oneself into others' affairs
senses.titleCN: 介入；插手：把自己塞进别人的事情里
senses.definition: to involve oneself in a situation or conversation where one is not wanted or expected
senses.definitionCN: 介入自己不被需要或不被期待的情境或谈话
senses.example: He tried to insert himself into the negotiation at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图在最后一刻插进这场谈判。
senses.why: Insert oneself turns the physical placing into a social one: the person becomes the object pushed into a space already occupied by others. The awkwardness is part of the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: insert oneself 把物理放置变成社会性放置：人成了被推进一个已被他人占据的空间的对象。那种不请自来的尴尬正是这个隐喻的一部分。

senses.title: Write a clause into a document
senses.titleCN: 写入条款：把条件加进合同或法律
senses.definition: to add a clause, condition, or provision to a contract, law, or formal document
senses.definitionCN: 在合同、法律或正式文件中加入条款、条件或规定
senses.example: The parties inserted a confidentiality clause before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在签署前加入了一条保密条款。
senses.why: A contract is a row of clauses; inserting one is the same gesture as inserting a sentence. The legal sense is a precise social application of the root image of joining a line.
senses.whyCN: 合同是一行条款；加入一条与插入一句话是同一个动作。法律义是“加入一行”这一词根形象在社会领域中的精确应用。

senses.title: Slot an extra piece into a performance
senses.titleCN: 穿插：在表演或节目中加入一段
senses.definition: to add an extra scene, song, or segment between existing parts of a performance or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在表演或序列的既有部分之间加入额外的场景、歌曲或段落
senses.example: The director inserted a short comic scene between the two acts.
senses.exampleCN: 导演在两幕之间穿插了一段简短的喜剧场景。
senses.why: A performance is also a sequence, a row of parts in time. Inserting a scene means placing it between two existing pieces, proving how easily the spatial root extends to time and narrative.
senses.whyCN: 表演也是一条序列，是时间中的一行部件。插入一个场景，就是把它放在两个既有片段之间，说明这个空间词根多么容易延伸到时间与叙事。

intro.en: Insert is Latin 'to join in a row'. Its root serere, 'to join, arrange', first described grafting a shoot into a stock, then any placing of one thing into an ordered line, and finally the printed sheet slipped among newspaper pages.
intro.cn: insert 是拉丁语“接入一行”。词根 serere 意为“连接、排列”，先指把枝条接进砧木，再指把一物放进有秩序的队列，最后指夹进报纸页面之间的印刷页。

items.en: The root *ser- 'to line up' is reconstructed, not written. No text records it, so this deepest step is source uncertain; it is inferred from words such as Latin series and serere.
items.cn: 词根 *ser-“排成一行”是构拟形式，没有书面记录。因此最深的这一步是“来源不确定”，只能从拉丁语 series、serere 等词推断。

items.en: Serere meant 'to join together, arrange, put in a row'. It supplied series 'a row, chain' and the compound inserere.
items.cn: serere 意为“连接、排列、排成一行”。它给出了 series“行、链”以及复合词 inserere。

items.en: Inserere, from in- 'in' plus serere, meant 'to graft, implant, put in'. The grafting image is the ancestor of all later uses.
items.cn: inserere 由 in-“向内”加 serere 构成，意为“嫁接、植入、放入”。嫁接的形象是后来所有用法的祖先。

items.en: Middle English inseren is recorded as 'to set in place, to graft, to introduce into the mind', borrowed directly from the Latin verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 inseren 记录为“放置到位、嫁接、引入心中”，直接借自拉丁语动词。

items.en: The modern verb insert is recorded from the 1520s as 'to set in, put or place in'. The spelling and pronunciation were reshaped after Latin.
items.cn: 现代动词 insert 于 16 世纪 20 年代记录为“放入、置于其中”。拼写和读音依照拉丁语被重新塑造。

items.en: The noun insert appears in 1893 as 'something inserted', especially a paper placed among the pages of a newspaper or magazine.
items.cn: 名词 insert 于 1893 年出现，意为“被插入之物”，尤指夹在报纸或杂志页面间的纸页。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a small six-legged animal. It shares the in- opening but ends in -sect, from secare 'to cut'.
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫。它同样以 in- 开头，但结尾是 -sect，来自 secare“切”。

entries.definition: to demand or maintain something firmly. Its root is sistere 'to stand', not serere.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持；坚决要求。它的词根是 sistere“站立”，不是 serere。

entries.definition: to state a fact or claim confidently. It comes from ad- plus serere, the same joining root as insert.
entries.definitionCN: 断言；主张。它来自 ad- 加 serere，与 insert 同出“连接”词根。

entries.definition: to abandon someone or a duty. It comes from de- plus serere, literally to unjoin.
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃；擅离。它来自 de- 加 serere，字面是“解开连接”。

entries.definition: to force a liquid or substance into something with pressure. It stresses pressure, while insert stresses placement.
entries.definitionCN: 注入；注射。它强调压力，而 insert 强调放置。

entries.definition: to fix something firmly and deeply inside a surrounding mass. It suggests the surrounding material closes around it.
entries.definitionCN: 嵌入；深植。它暗示周围材料把该物包住。

entries.definition: to place tissue or a device surgically into a body. It is the medical cousin of insert sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 植入。它是 insert 第 2 义在医学上的近亲。

entries.definition: to insert words or material into a text or sequence, often to alter it. It is more technical than insert.
entries.definitionCN: 插补；窜改插入。它比 insert 更技术化。

entries.definition: to place something between two things, or to intervene. It focuses on the between position.
entries.definitionCN: 使介于两者之间；干预。它着眼于“在中间”的位置。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin serere 'to join in a row', inserere 'to graft', the English insertion, and the newspaper insert.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 serere“排成一行”、inserere“嫁接”、英语 insertion，以及报纸夹页 insert。

normal.en: insert = in- 'in' + serere 'to join a row': put the new piece into the existing line.
normal.cn: insert = in-“向内”+ serere“接入一行”：把新部件放进已有的行列。

normal.en: The same root gives series: things inserted are joined into a series, one after another.
normal.cn: 同一个词根给出 series：被插入的东西接成一系列，一个接一个。
