normal.en: A graft is an insert: the gardener slips a shoot into the stock so the two join and grow as one.
normal.cn: 嫁接就是一种 insert：园丁把枝条塞进砧木，让两者接合并长成一株。

normal.en: An editor inserts a sentence exactly as a printer inserts a sheet: both add a piece between existing pages or lines.
normal.cn: 编辑插入一句话，正像印刷工插入一张纸：两者都在既有页面或行间加进一片。

normal.en: The noun insert is the paper that was slipped in; the action and its object share one word.
normal.cn: 名词 insert 就是被塞进去的那张纸；动作和动作的对象共用同一个词。

abstract.en: The core is controlled entry: something outside is guided into an opening that already has an order.
abstract.cn: 核心是有控制的进入：外面的东西被引导进一个已有秩序的开口。

abstract.en: The word moves from plant to page to body to society: graft, text, catheter, contract, conversation.
abstract.cn: 这个词从植物走到纸页，再走到身体与社会：嫁接、文本、导管、合同、谈话。

abstract.en: To insert is always to alter a sequence by adding a new position, never merely to touch a surface.
abstract.cn: 插入总是在序列中增加一个新位置，从而改变序列，而不只是碰到表面。

examples.en: Insert the coin into the slot and wait for the ticket.
examples.cn: 把硬币投入投币口，然后等票出来。

examples.en: She inserted a new paragraph between the introduction and the conclusion.
examples.cn: 她在引言和结论之间加了一段新文字。

examples.en: The magazine is full of glossy inserts for holiday sales.
examples.cn: 这本杂志里夹满了假日促销的光滑插页。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ sert（谐音“塞它”）——把它塞到里面去 → insert 插入

root: 源自拉丁语 serere“连接、排成一行”，加 in-“向内”构成 inserere“嫁接、植入”，16 世纪 20 年代进入英语，核心是“把东西接入既有的一行”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of insert, all built on one act of guided entry: a key into a lock, a shoot into a stock, a sentence into a page, an ad into a paper, a clause into a contract, and a scene into a performance.
sensesIntro.cn: insert 的九个义项都建在同一次有引导的进入上：钥匙进锁、枝条进砧木、句子进页面、广告进报纸、条款进合同、场景进表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new piece guided into an ordered row or opening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个新部件被引导进一个有秩序的行列或开口。

branches.en: PHYSICAL ENTRY: a key, a card, or an instrument placed into an opening.
branches.cn: 物理进入：钥匙、卡片或器械被放进开口。

branches.en: LIVING AND VERBAL GRAFTS: tissue joined to tissue, words joined to words.
branches.cn: 生命与文字的嫁接：组织接到组织，词句接到词句。

branches.en: THE PRINTED INSERT: an advertisement placed in media, and the sheet itself.
branches.cn: 印刷插入物：放进媒体的广告，以及那张纸本身。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND LEGAL ENTRY: a person pushing into affairs, a clause written into a document.
branches.cn: 社会与法律的进入：人挤进他人的事务，条款写进文件。

branches.en: THE PERFORMANCE SLOT: an extra scene or song placed between existing parts.
branches.cn: 表演中的插位：额外场景或歌曲被放在既有片段之间。

intro.en: Insert is in- plus the root ser- 'join, arrange'. Its family shows the prefixes in-, ad-, de-, dis- and the suffixes -ion, -able, -er, -al.
intro.cn: insert 是 in- 加词根 ser-“连接、排列”。它的词族展示前缀 in-、ad-、de-、dis-，以及后缀 -ion、-able、-er、-al。

latinIntro.en: Latin serere 'to join, arrange in a row' is the base of series, insert, assert and desert; the same verb with different prefixes yields joining and unjoining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serere“连接、排成一行”是 series、insert、assert、desert 的基础；同一个动词配不同前缀，给出“接上”与“解开”。

items.meaning: to place something into another thing
items.meaningCN: 插入；放入（in- 向内 + 连接）
items.example: Insert the plug into the socket.
items.exampleCN: 把插头插进插座。

items.meaning: the act of putting something in
items.meaningCN: 插入；插入物（-ion 表动作或结果）
items.example: The insertion of the new clause took ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 加入新条款用了十分钟。

items.meaning: able to be inserted
items.meaningCN: 可插入的（-able 表能够）
items.example: The insertable tray fits any standard printer.
items.exampleCN: 这个可插入的托盘适合任何标准打印机。

items.meaning: a person or device that inserts
items.meaningCN: 插入者；插入器（-er 表人或工具）
items.example: The machine uses a robotic inserter for each card.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器用机械插入器处理每张卡片。

items.structure: Latin series, from serere (to join in a row)
items.meaning: a number of things joined in order
items.meaningCN: 系列；一连串（同出 serere 排成行）
items.example: The library holds a series of lectures on climate.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆举办一系列气候讲座。

items.meaning: arranged or happening in a series
items.meaningCN: 连续的；连载的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The novel was first published in serial form.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说最初以连载形式发表。

items.meaning: to claim or state firmly
items.meaningCN: 断言；主张（把主张接到自己这边）
items.example: She asserted that the data were reliable.
items.exampleCN: 她断言这些数据是可靠的。

items.meaning: to abandon, literally to unjoin
items.meaningCN: 抛弃；擅离（de- 离开 + 连接 → 解开）
items.example: He deserted his post during the storm.
items.exampleCN: 他在暴风雨中擅离职守。

items.meaning: a long formal written discussion
items.meaningCN: 学位论文（把材料分开排列、反复论述）
items.example: She is writing her dissertation on urban birds.
items.exampleCN: 她正在写关于城市鸟类的学位论文。

latinEntries.meaning: to join together, arrange in a row

definition_zh: 洞察力；深刻理解；顿悟；见解；内视
definition_en: a deep and accurate understanding of the hidden nature of something, or the sudden moment when such understanding arrives
core_image: 一束光不照表面，而是直接穿过外壳，把里面原本看不见的结构照亮
scene: A manager reads a customer survey and says: This gives us real insight into why people leave.
sceneCN: 这里 insight 是「洞察、深刻理解」（第 1 个义项：看穿表面、理解事物内里的能力或所得）；句意：这让我们真正看清了人们为什么会离开。画面里有问卷、数据图和若有所悟的经理。

pos.zh: 洞察力；深刻理解；顿悟；见解；内视

collocations.zh: 深入了解；获得对……的洞察

derivatives.zh: 富有洞察力的；见解深刻的

senses.title: Deep understanding of what is hidden
senses.titleCN: 洞察力：看穿表面、理解内里的能力
senses.definition: the ability to understand the true nature of a person, situation, or problem, especially what is not obvious
senses.definitionCN: 理解人、情境或问题真实本质的能力，尤指看见不明显之处
senses.example: Her insight into human motivation made her an excellent negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 她对人类动机的洞察使她成为出色的谈判者。
senses.why: Insight began about 1200 as 'sight with the eyes of the mind'. By the 1580s it had shifted to 'penetrating understanding into character or hidden nature': the inner eye looks through the surface.
senses.whyCN: insight 约在 1200 年指“用心灵之眼看见”。到 16 世纪 80 年代，它转为“对性格或隐藏本质的穿透性理解”：内在的眼睛看穿表面。

senses.title: The sudden moment of seeing
senses.titleCN: 顿悟：忽然看明白的那一刻
senses.definition: a sudden clear understanding of something that was previously confusing or unknown
senses.definitionCN: 对先前困惑或未知之事突然产生的清晰理解
senses.example: Halfway through the experiment, she had an insight that explained all the odd results.
senses.exampleCN: 实验进行到一半，她突然顿悟，解释了所有异常结果。
senses.why: The noun names not only a lasting capacity but a single event of inner sight. English commonly uses insight for the flash itself, because the word already contains the image of a moment of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只命名一种持久能力，也命名一次内在看见的事件。英语常用 insight 指那道闪光本身，因为词里本就含着“看见的一刻”的形象。

senses.title: Sight with the eyes of the mind
senses.titleCN: 内视：用心灵之眼看见
senses.definition: the old sense of mental vision or inward seeing, rather than sight with the physical eyes
senses.definitionCN: 古义：心灵视觉或向内看见，而非肉眼看物
senses.example: In the old poem, the prophet's insight comes in a dream, not through his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首古老的诗里，先知的洞见来自梦境，而非肉眼。
senses.why: The earliest recorded form, c. 1200 innsihht, meant 'sight with the eyes of the mind, mental vision, understanding from within'. The modern word still carries that inward eye beneath its analytical uses.
senses.whyCN: 最早记录形式约 1200 年的 innsihht 意为“用心灵之眼看见、心灵视觉、从内部理解”。现代词的分析用法之下，仍带着这只向内的眼睛。

senses.title: A particular view or opinion
senses.titleCN: 见解：关于某事的一个深刻看法
senses.definition: a particular understanding or opinion about something, often one that is unusually clear or useful
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的一种理解或看法，通常清晰或有用得不同寻常
senses.example: The book offers fresh insights into how language shapes thought.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书就语言如何塑造思维提供了新鲜见解。
senses.why: Once insight means inward seeing, the content seen can be spoken of as an insight. The countable plural insights names the separate products of that seeing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 insight 指“向内看见”，所看见的内容就可以被称为一个 insight。可数复数 insights 命名那次看见所产出的各个成果。

senses.title: Penetrating understanding of character
senses.titleCN: 看穿人心：对性格或隐秘本质的理解
senses.definition: the power of understanding a person's character or hidden motives accurately
senses.definitionCN: 准确理解一个人性格或隐秘动机的能力
senses.example: The novel shows an unusual insight into grief and family loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说对悲伤与家族忠诚表现出不同寻常的洞察。
senses.why: The 1580s sense is specifically 'penetrating understanding into character or hidden nature'. Here insight is aimed at people, and the metaphor is a look that goes inside rather than a look that stays outside.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 80 年代的义项具体是“对性格或隐藏本质的穿透性理解”。这里 insight 对准人，隐喻是看进去，而不是停留在外面。

senses.title: Understanding one's own mind
senses.titleCN: 自我认识：看清自己的内心
senses.definition: a clear understanding of one's own feelings, motives, or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 对自己情感、动机或行为的清晰理解
senses.example: Therapy helped him gain insight into his fear of failure.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗帮助他看清自己对失败的恐惧。
senses.why: When the inner eye is turned toward the self, insight becomes self-knowledge. The same word covers both looking into another person and looking into one's own mind.
senses.whyCN: 当内在的眼睛转向自我，insight 就成了自我认识。同一个词既覆盖看进他人，也覆盖看进自己的心。

senses.title: Professional or market insight
senses.titleCN: 专业洞见：商业与研究中的可用理解
senses.definition: actionable understanding of customers, data, or a field, used to guide decisions
senses.definitionCN: 对客户、数据或某一领域的可行动理解，用来指导决策
senses.example: The team used consumer insight to redesign the app's first screen.
senses.exampleCN: 团队利用消费者洞察重新设计了应用的首屏。
senses.why: Modern business turns insight into a countable resource: a finding that lets a company see what customers cannot say directly. The old inward sight becomes practical knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业把 insight 变成一种可数资源：一条让公司看见顾客说不出口之事的发现。古老的内视变成了实用知识。

senses.title: The content seen: a revelation
senses.titleCN: 启示：被看出来的那个道理
senses.definition: the idea or realization that results from a period of deep thinking or study
senses.definitionCN: 经过深入思考或研究后产生的想法或领悟
senses.example: The central insight of the paper is that trust lowers the cost of trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文的核心洞见是：信任降低了交易成本。
senses.why: Here the word points to the thing seen rather than the seeing. The metaphor of sight allows the object of insight to be presented almost like an object revealed by light.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指向被看见的东西，而不是看见的动作。视觉隐喻让洞见的对象几乎像被光照出来的物品一样呈现。

senses.title: Therapeutic insight: seeing the pattern
senses.titleCN: 心理领悟：看清自己的行为模式
senses.definition: in psychology, the understanding of one's own unconscious patterns that helps change behavior
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中对自己无意识模式的领会，有助于改变行为
senses.example: The patient reached an insight about how childhood fear shaped his reactions.
senses.exampleCN: 病人领悟到童年恐惧如何塑造了他的反应。
senses.why: Psychology gave the inward eye a technical task: not just seeing oneself, but seeing the recurring pattern behind one's actions. The word's old meaning of inner vision is used as a clinical tool.
senses.whyCN: 心理学给这只内在的眼睛一项技术任务：不只是看见自己，而是看见行为背后反复出现的模式。词旧的“内视”义被用作临床工具。

intro.en: Insight is a native English compound: in plus sight. It began as sight with the eyes of the mind, then narrowed into penetrating understanding of hidden character, and later widened into the modern business and psychological uses.
intro.cn: insight 是英语本土复合词：in 加 sight。它起初指用心灵之眼看见，后来收窄为对隐藏性格的穿透性理解，再扩展出现代的商业与心理学用法。

items.en: Sight comes from Old English gesiht, sihth, 'sight, something seen'. The noun already joined the act of seeing with the thing seen.
items.cn: sight 来自古英语 gesiht、sihth，意为“视觉、所见之物”。这个名词本就把“看见的动作”与“看见的东西”连在一起。

items.en: Innsihht is recorded as 'sight with the eyes of the mind, mental vision, understanding from within', formed from in plus sight.
items.cn: innsihht 记录为“用心灵之眼看见、心灵视觉、从内部理解”，由 in 加 sight 构成。

items.en: The meaning shifted to 'penetrating understanding into character or hidden nature'. The inner eye now looks through appearances.
items.cn: 词义转为“对性格或隐藏本质的穿透性理解”。内在的眼睛此时看穿表象。

items.en: Insightful is recorded in 1881, formed from insight plus -ful. Earlier alternatives were insighted and inseeing.
items.cn: insightful 于 1881 年记录，由 insight 加 -ful 构成。更早的替代说法是 insighted 与 inseeing。

items.en: Modern English turns insight into a countable professional asset: consumer insight, market insight, and clinical insight.
items.cn: 现代英语把 insight 变成一种可数的专业资产：消费者洞察、市场洞察、临床领悟。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to stir up or encourage violent or unlawful action. It sounds almost like insight but comes from citare 'to set in motion'.
entries.definitionCN: 煽动；激起。它听起来几乎和 insight 一样，但来自 citare“使动起来”。

entries.definition: the inner part or position within something. It shares the in- opening and the sound of sight.
entries.definitionCN: 内部；在里面。它同样以 in- 开头，且与 sight 音近。

entries.definition: located at the place where work or an event happens. It swaps in- for on-.
entries.definitionCN: 现场的；在场所内。它把 in- 换成了 on-。

entries.definition: the ability to see, or something seen. It is the second half of insight.
entries.definitionCN: 视力；景象。它是 insight 的后半部分。

entries.definition: the way one notices or understands something. It is broader and less penetrating than insight.
entries.definitionCN: 感知；看法。它比 insight 更宽，也少一些穿透力。

entries.definition: knowing something immediately without conscious reasoning. It arrives like insight but without the analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 直觉。它像 insight 一样突然到来，但不经过分析。

entries.definition: the ability to judge well and see differences clearly. It stresses discrimination between things.
entries.definitionCN: 洞察力；辨识力。它强调分辨事物之间的差异。

entries.definition: knowledge of a subject or a sympathetic grasp of someone's feelings. It is wider and calmer than insight.
entries.definitionCN: 理解；谅解。它比 insight 更宽、更平和。

entries.definition: knowledge that something exists or is happening. It is the first step before insight.
entries.definitionCN: 意识；察觉。它是形成洞察之前的第一步。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the English compound in + sight, the c. 1200 form innsihht, and the 1580s shift to understanding hidden character.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：英语复合词 in + sight、约 1200 年的 innsihht，以及 16 世纪 80 年代转向“理解隐藏性格”。

normal.en: insight = in + sight: sight turned inward, seeing inside rather than just looking at the surface.
normal.cn: insight = in + sight：向内的视觉，看见里面，而不只是看表面。

normal.en: The oldest form innsihht literally meant sight with the eyes of the mind.
normal.cn: 最古老的形式 innsihht 字面就是“用心灵之眼看见”。

normal.en: An insight is not more information; it is a look that passes through the information to the pattern beneath.
normal.cn: insight 不是更多信息，而是一种穿过信息、看见底下模式的目光。

normal.en: Foresight, hindsight and oversight all use sight as a direction: before, behind, and above.
normal.cn: foresight、hindsight、oversight 都用 sight 表方向：在前、在后、在上。

normal.en: Insightful is simply full of that inward sight, which is why it praises the person, not the amount of data.
normal.cn: insightful 就是“充满这种内在视觉”，所以它赞美的是人，而不是数据量。

abstract.en: The core is penetration: the eye does not stop at the surface but enters the hidden structure.
abstract.cn: 核心是穿透：眼睛不在表面停下，而是进入隐藏的结构。

abstract.en: The word moves from mystic inner vision to clinical self-knowledge to commercial strategy, keeping the same inward look.
abstract.cn: 这个词从神秘的内视走到临床的自我认识，再走到商业策略，始终保留同一种向内看。

abstract.en: So insight is both the act of seeing and the thing seen, which is why one can have an insight and also be known for insight.
abstract.cn: 所以 insight 既是看见的动作，也是看见的东西；这就是为什么人既可以“有一个顿悟”，也可以“以洞察力著称”。

examples.en: The study gives us new insight into how children learn languages.
examples.cn: 这项研究让我们对儿童如何学习语言有了新的认识。

examples.en: He had a sudden insight while walking home from the lab.
examples.cn: 他从实验室走回家的路上突然顿悟。

examples.en: Her insights into the market helped the company avoid a costly mistake.
examples.cn: 她对市场的洞察帮助公司避免了一次代价高昂的错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ sight（看）——往里面看，看见别人看不见的东西 → insight 洞察力

root: 英语本土复合词，由 in“向内”加 sight“看”构成，约 1200 年作 innsihht“心灵之眼所见”，16 世纪 80 年代转为“对隐藏本质的穿透性理解”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of insight, all built on one inward look: the mind's eye, a sudden flash of understanding, a penetrating reading of character, a professional finding, and a clinical pattern seen at last.
sensesIntro.cn: insight 的九个义项都建在同一次向内看：心灵之眼、突然的理解闪光、对性格的穿透性解读、专业发现，以及终于看清的临床模式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inward eye that sees through the surface to the hidden structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只向内的眼睛，穿过表面看见隐藏结构。

branches.en: THE PENETRATING EYE: deep understanding of hidden nature and of character.
branches.cn: 穿透之眼：对隐藏本质与性格的深刻理解。

branches.en: THE FLASH AND THE FINDING: a sudden moment of seeing, and the idea it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 闪光与所得：突然看见的一刻，以及它留下的想法。

branches.en: THE INWARD TURN: sight with the mind's eye, and the same eye turned on the self.
branches.cn: 向内转：心灵之眼的看见，以及同一只眼转向自我。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN VIEW: a particular insight shared with others, and professional market insight.
branches.cn: 说出的看法：与他人分享的具体见解，以及专业的市场洞察。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL PATTERN: insight used to see one's recurring unconscious behavior.
branches.cn: 临床模式：用洞察看见自己反复出现的无意识行为。

intro.en: Insight is in- plus sight. Its family shows the prefixes in-, fore-, hind-, over-, and eye-, the base sight, and the suffixes -ful, -fully, -less.
intro.cn: insight 是 in- 加 sight。它的词族展示前缀 in-、fore-、hind-、over-、eye-，基础词 sight，以及后缀 -ful、-fully、-less。

latinIntro.en: Insight has no Latin root: it is a native English compound of in and sight, and its relatives are other English compounds built on sight.
latinIntro.cn: insight 没有拉丁词根：它是 in 与 sight 的英语本土复合词，其亲属是其他以 sight 构成的英语复合词。

items.meaning: inward seeing; deep understanding
items.meaningCN: 洞察；内视（向内 + 看见）
items.example: The interview gave me insight into her daily life.
items.exampleCN: 这次采访让我了解了她的日常生活。

items.meaning: full of insight; perceptive
items.meaningCN: 富有洞察力的（-ful 表充满）
items.example: She asked an insightful question about the data.
items.exampleCN: 她就数据问了一个很有洞察力的问题。

items.meaning: in a perceptive way
items.meaningCN: 富有洞察力地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He wrote insightfully about the causes of the strike.
items.exampleCN: 他就罢工的原因写得很有见地。

items.meaning: the ability to see or what is seen
items.meaningCN: 视力；景象（古英语“看见”名词）
items.example: The ship was soon out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 船很快就不见了。

items.meaning: the ability to see what may happen
items.meaningCN: 先见之明（fore- 在前 + 看见）
items.example: With foresight, they stored food before the winter.
items.exampleCN: 凭着先见之明，他们在冬天前储好了食物。

items.meaning: understanding of an event after it has happened
items.meaningCN: 事后聪明；后见之明（hind- 在后）
items.example: In hindsight, we should have left earlier.
items.exampleCN: 事后看来，我们本该早点走。

items.meaning: supervision, or a careless failure to notice
items.meaningCN: 监督；疏漏（over- 在上 + 看）
items.example: The error was due to an oversight in the review.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误源于审查中的一处疏漏。

items.meaning: the power of seeing with the eyes
items.meaningCN: 视力（eye 眼 + sight 视觉）
items.example: Reading in dim light can strain your eyesight.
items.exampleCN: 在昏暗光线下阅读会损害视力。

items.meaning: unable to see; blind
items.meaningCN: 失明的（-less 表没有）
items.example: The sightless man navigated the street with a cane.
items.exampleCN: 那位失明的男子拄着手杖在街上行走。

items.meaning: visiting places of interest
items.meaningCN: 观光（看景物 + 看）
items.example: We spent the afternoon sightseeing along the river.
items.exampleCN: 我们下午沿河观光。

definition_zh: 检查；视察；检阅；查验；审查；审视
definition_en: to look at something closely and carefully in order to judge its condition, quality, or correctness
core_image: 一个人俯下身，把灯凑近机器的接缝，眼睛沿着每一道纹路慢慢扫过去，不放过任何一处
scene: A safety officer walks along the factory line and says: I need to inspect every machine before it restarts.
sceneCN: 这里 inspect 是「检查、检验」（第 1 个义项：仔细查看以判断状况或是否合格）；句意：每台机器重启前我都需要检查。画面里有安全员、记录板和生产线。

pos.zh: 检查；视察；检阅；查验；审视

collocations.zh: 检查某物是否有某问题

senses.title: Look closely at details
senses.titleCN: 仔细检查：贴近看每一个细节
senses.definition: to examine something closely and carefully, usually to find problems or judge condition
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，通常为了发现问题或判断状况
senses.example: The mechanic inspected the engine for signs of wear.
senses.exampleCN: 机械师仔细检查发动机是否有磨损迹象。
senses.why: Inspect is recorded in the 1620s from Latin inspicere, in- 'into' plus specere 'to look'. The prefix makes the looking directional: not a glance at, but a look into the thing.
senses.whyCN: inspect 于 16 世纪 20 年代记录，来自拉丁语 inspicere，即 in-“向内”加 specere“看”。前缀让“看”有了方向：不是瞥一眼，而是看进去。

senses.title: Visit an institution officially
senses.titleCN: 视察：以官方身份到机构查看
senses.definition: to make an official visit to a school, factory, prison, or other institution in order to check how it is run
senses.definitionCN: 以官方身份到学校、工厂、监狱等机构查看其运作情况
senses.example: Government officials will inspect the school next week.
senses.exampleCN: 政府官员下周将视察这所学校。
senses.why: The same close look becomes an official act when the viewer has authority. The 19c growth of public administration turned inspect into a routine verb of oversight, and the visit itself became an inspection.
senses.whyCN: 当查看者拥有权力，同样的仔细看就变成官方行为。19 世纪公共行政的扩张使 inspect 成为例行监督动词，而这次到访本身就成了 inspection。

senses.title: Review troops on parade
senses.titleCN: 检阅：在列队中查看部队
senses.definition: to walk past soldiers on parade and examine their order, equipment, and appearance
senses.definitionCN: 走过列队的士兵，检查其队形、装备与仪容
senses.example: The general inspected the troops before the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 将军在仪式前检阅了部队。
senses.why: Military inspection is the oldest public ritual of the word: an officer's eye moves along a line of men just as it moves along a machine. The rows of soldiers make the 'looking into order' image visible.
senses.whyCN: 军事检阅是这个词最古老的公开仪式：军官的目光沿着一排人移动，正如沿着一台机器移动。士兵的队列让“看进秩序”这一形象变得可见。

senses.title: Search baggage or goods
senses.titleCN: 查验：搜查行李或货物
senses.definition: to examine luggage, cargo, or containers for prohibited or undeclared items
senses.definitionCN: 检查行李、货物或集装箱是否有违禁或未申报物品
senses.example: Customs officers inspected every bag at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 海关官员在边境检查了每一个包。
senses.why: A customs inspection is sense 01 with legal force: the close look is not optional, and its purpose is to find what is hidden. The eye becomes a search.
senses.whyCN: 海关查验是带法律强制力的第 1 义：这种仔细查看不可拒绝，目的是找出隐藏之物。眼睛于是变成一次搜查。

senses.title: Check quality or safety
senses.titleCN: 检验：查质量或安全是否达标
senses.definition: to test or check a product, building, or system against a standard
senses.definitionCN: 按标准测试或检查产品、建筑或系统
senses.example: Every bridge is inspected for cracks once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每座桥每年都要检查一次是否有裂缝。
senses.why: The word's close look is easily directed at a standard: not just seeing what is there, but seeing whether it meets a required condition. This is inspection as quality control.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的仔细看很容易对准一个标准：不只是看见有什么，而是看见它是否达到要求的状态。这就是作为质量控制的检验。

senses.title: Audit accounts or documents
senses.titleCN: 审查：核对账目或文件
senses.definition: to examine records, accounts, or documents officially to check that they are correct
senses.definitionCN: 以官方身份检查记录、账目或文件是否正确
senses.example: The auditor inspected the company's accounts line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员逐行审查了公司的账目。
senses.why: Paper has its own rows and lines, and the inspecting eye follows them one by one. The root specere 'to look' extends from objects to records without changing its basic motion.
senses.whyCN: 纸面也有自己的行与列，检查的眼睛逐行跟随。词根 specere“看”从物体延伸到记录，基本动作并未改变。

senses.title: Look someone up and down
senses.titleCN: 打量；审视：从头到脚看一个人
senses.definition: to look at a person closely and critically, often in a way that makes them uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 仔细而挑剔地看一个人，常令对方不自在
senses.example: The interviewer inspected him from head to toe before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官在开口前把他从头到脚打量了一番。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the same careful look can feel like judgment. The word keeps its neutral surface but the social effect is often evaluation, even suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是人，同样的仔细看可能像一种评判。这个词表面仍中立，但社会效果常是评价，甚至怀疑。

senses.title: Survey a place on the ground
senses.titleCN: 勘察：到现场查看地形或工程
senses.definition: to visit and examine a site, building, or area before work or after damage
senses.definitionCN: 在工作开始前或受损后到现场查看地点、建筑或区域
senses.example: Engineers inspected the site before the foundation was poured.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在地基浇筑前勘察了现场。
senses.why: Here inspect means a look that requires going to the place, because the information is in the ground itself. The word's 'look into' becomes physical entry into a site.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 inspect 指必须到现场才能完成的查看，因为信息就在地里。词的“看进去”变成了亲身进入一个场地。

senses.title: Check code, data, or a system
senses.titleCN: 检查代码、数据或系统
senses.definition: to review code, data, or a technical system for errors, security issues, or correct behavior
senses.definitionCN: 检查代码、数据或技术系统是否有错误、安全问题或行为是否正确
senses.example: The team inspected the logs after the server crashed.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器崩溃后，团队检查了日志。
senses.why: Modern technical English reuses the old verb for invisible structures: code and logs are examined as closely as a machine. The eye still goes 'into' the system to find what is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术英语把这个旧动词用于看不见的结构：代码和日志被像机器一样仔细检查。眼睛仍然“进入”系统，找出哪里出了问题。

intro.en: Inspect is Latin 'to look into'. It joins in- 'into' with specere 'to look', the same root that gives spectator, prospect, and perspective. English borrowed the verb in the 1620s.
intro.cn: inspect 是拉丁语“看进去”。它把 in-“向内”与 specere“看”结合，同一词根还给出 spectator、prospect、perspective。英语在 16 世纪 20 年代借入这个动词。

items.en: The root *spek- 'to observe' is reconstructed, not written. No text records it, so this deepest step is source uncertain; it is inferred from Latin specere and Greek skopein.
items.cn: 词根 *spek-“观察”是构拟形式，没有书面记录。因此最深的这一步是“来源不确定”，只能从拉丁语 specere 与希腊语 skopein 推断。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, look at, observe'. It is the base of many Latin looking words and of English spectator, spectacle, and suspect.
items.cn: specere 意为“看、观看、观察”。它是许多拉丁语“看”类词的基础，也是英语 spectator、spectacle、suspect 的来源。

items.en: Inspicere, from in- 'into' plus specere, meant 'to look at, observe, view; look into, inspect, examine'. The prefix turns a look into an examination.
items.cn: inspicere 由 in-“向内”加 specere 构成，意为“看、观察、观看；看进去、检查、审查”。前缀把一次看变成一次检查。

items.en: Inspectus is the past participle of inspicere. English took this stem, not the present form, which is why the modern verb ends in -spect.
items.cn: inspectus 是 inspicere 的过去分词。英语取的是这个词干，而不是现在时形式，所以现代动词以 -spect 结尾。

items.en: Inspect is recorded in the 1620s with the meaning 'to look at closely, examine'. The noun inspection is from the 1590s and helped prepare the verb's place in English.
items.cn: inspect 于 16 世纪 20 年代记录，意为“仔细看、检查”。名词 inspection 来自 16 世纪 90 年代，为动词在英语中的位置作了准备。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a particular part or feature of a situation. It comes from ad- plus specere, a look in one direction.
entries.definitionCN: 方面；外观。它来自 ad- 加 specere，即朝一个方向看。

entries.definition: to think that something will happen. It comes from ex- 'out' plus spectare, to look out for.
entries.definitionCN: 期待；预料。它来自 ex-“向外”加 spectare，即向外张望。

entries.definition: to admire or regard someone highly. It comes from re- 'back' plus specere, to look back at.
entries.definitionCN: 尊敬；尊重。它来自 re-“回”加 specere，即回头看。

entries.definition: to believe someone may be guilty without proof. It comes from sub- 'under' plus specere, to look up at from below.
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑。它来自 sub-“在下”加 specere，即从下往上看。

entries.definition: to look at something in detail in order to learn about it or judge it. It is the closest general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 检查；审查。它是最接近的一般同义词。

entries.definition: to examine something very carefully and critically. It is stronger and more suspicious than inspect.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细审查。它比 inspect 更强，也更多疑。

entries.definition: to look at or examine the whole of something, often a place. It is wider than inspect.
entries.definitionCN: 勘测；巡视。它比 inspect 视野更宽。

entries.definition: to look at something quickly to make sure it is correct or safe. It is lighter and faster than inspect.
entries.definitionCN: 核对；检查。它比 inspect 更轻、更快。

entries.definition: to examine accounts or records officially. It matches inspect sense 06.
entries.definitionCN: 审计；查账。它对应 inspect 第 6 义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin specere 'to look', inspicere 'to look into', and the English family spectator, prospect, and perspective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 specere“看”、inspicere“看进去”，以及英语词族 spectator、prospect、perspective。

normal.en: inspect = in- 'into' + spect 'look': to look into a thing, not merely at it.
normal.cn: inspect = in-“向内”+ spect“看”：看进一个东西，而不只是看它。

normal.en: The same spect gives spectator, prospect and perspective: all are ways of looking.
normal.cn: 同一个 spect 给出 spectator、prospect、perspective：全都是“看”的方式。

normal.en: An inspector is literally a looker-into: the job is to put the eye inside the system.
normal.cn: inspector 字面就是“看进去的人”：这份工作就是把眼睛放进系统内部。

normal.en: Inspection day at a school is the same gesture as a customs check: authority looks closely and records what it finds.
normal.cn: 学校的视察日与海关查验是同一个动作：权力仔细看，并记录所见。

normal.en: To inspect troops is to run the eye along a line, exactly as one runs it along a machine's seams.
normal.cn: 检阅部队就是让目光沿一条队列移动，正如沿机器的接缝移动。

abstract.en: The core is directional attention: the look is aimed into a bounded object and moves through its parts.
abstract.cn: 核心是有方向的注意：目光射入一个有边界的对象，并穿过它的各部分。

abstract.en: The word moves from eyes to authority to records: a close look becomes an official act, then a bureaucratic routine.
abstract.cn: 这个词从眼睛走到权力，再走到记录：仔细看变成官方行为，再变成官僚程序。

abstract.en: So inspect always implies a standard: even a neutral look is measuring something against what it ought to be.
abstract.cn: 所以 inspect 总暗含一个标准：即使中立的查看，也在拿某物与它应有的样子作比较。

examples.en: The teacher inspected our homework for spelling mistakes.
examples.cn: 老师检查我们的作业有没有拼写错误。

examples.en: Health inspectors visit the restaurant twice a year.
examples.cn: 卫生检查员每年到这家餐厅检查两次。

examples.en: The officer inspected the troops in silence.
examples.cn: 军官默默地检阅了部队。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ spect（看）——把眼睛伸到里面去看 → inspect 检查

root: 源自拉丁语 specere“看”，加 in-“向内”构成 inspicere“看进去、检查”，过去分词 inspectus 于 17 世纪 20 年代进入英语，核心是“把目光投进内部”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of inspect, all built on one directed look: into an engine, into a school, along a parade, through baggage, across accounts, over a site, and into code.
sensesIntro.cn: inspect 的九个义项都建在同一次有方向的看：看进发动机、看进学校、沿队列看、翻查行李、核对账目、巡视现场、看进代码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a close, directed look into a bounded thing in order to judge it.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光有方向地看进一个有边界的事物，以便评判它。

branches.en: THE CLOSE LOOK: examining details of an object, and checking it against a quality standard.
branches.cn: 仔细看：检查物体的细节，并按质量标准检验它。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL VISIT: inspecting an institution, and surveying a site on the ground.
branches.cn: 官方到访：视察机构，以及到现场勘察。

branches.en: THE SEARCHING LINE: troops on parade, and baggage opened for concealed goods.
branches.cn: 搜查的队列：列队受阅的部队，以及为查隐藏物品而打开的行李。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE SYSTEM: accounts read line by line, and code or logs reviewed for faults.
branches.cn: 记录与系统：逐行核对账目，以及检查代码或日志的故障。

branches.en: THE JUDGING EYE: a person looked up and down, and silently evaluated.
branches.cn: 评判之眼：一个人被从头到脚打量，并被默默评价。

intro.en: Inspect is in- plus the root spect- 'look'. Its family shows the prefixes in-, intro-, retro-, pro-, per- and the suffixes -ion, -or, -ive, -acle, -ate.
intro.cn: inspect 是 in- 加词根 spect-“看”。它的词族展示前缀 in-、intro-、retro-、pro-、per-，以及后缀 -ion、-or、-ive、-acle、-ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look' is the base of inspect, spectator, prospect and perspective; the same root appears in suspicion and spectacle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere“看”是 inspect、spectator、prospect、perspective 的基础；同一词根也出现在 suspicion 与 spectacle 中。

items.meaning: to look into; examine closely
items.meaningCN: 检查；视察（in- 向内 + 看）
items.example: They inspected the roof after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨后他们检查了屋顶。

items.meaning: the act of examining closely
items.meaningCN: 检查；视察（-ion 表动作）
items.example: The annual inspection found no safety problems.
items.exampleCN: 年度检查没有发现安全问题。

items.meaning: a person who inspects
items.meaningCN: 检查员；督察（-or 表人）
items.example: A health inspector closed the kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 一名卫生检查员关闭了这间厨房。

items.meaning: a body of inspectors
items.meaningCN: 检查机构；督察部门（-ate 表机构）
items.example: The inspectorate published its annual report.
items.exampleCN: 督察部门发布了年度报告。

items.meaning: to look into one's own mind
items.meaningCN: 内省（intro- 向内 + 看）
items.example: She introspected after the argument.
items.exampleCN: 争吵之后她作了内省。

items.meaning: to look back on the past
items.meaningCN: 回顾（retro- 向后 + 看）
items.example: In retrospect, the decision was wise.
items.exampleCN: 回顾起来，那个决定是明智的。

items.meaning: a view ahead; a future possibility
items.meaningCN: 前景；可能性（pro- 向前 + 看）
items.example: The prospect of a long trip excited them.
items.exampleCN: 长途旅行的前景让他们兴奋。

items.meaning: a way of seeing things through a particular position
items.meaningCN: 视角；透视（per- 穿过 + 看 + -ive）
items.example: Travel gave her a new perspective on home.
items.exampleCN: 旅行让她对家有了新的视角。

items.meaning: a striking public sight
items.meaningCN: 景象；壮观场面（spectare 观看 + -acle）
items.example: The fireworks were a magnificent spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 烟花是一场景象壮丽的表演。

items.meaning: to form a guess by looking out for signs
items.meaningCN: 推测（源自瞭望塔，向外观察）
items.example: Reporters speculated about the cause of the fire.
items.exampleCN: 记者们推测火灾的原因。

definition_zh: 实例；例子；事例；场合；诉讼程序；请求；援引为例
definition_en: a single case or example of something, or the particular occasion on which something happens
core_image: 一排相同的样本摆在桌上，手指点住其中一只：就用这一个来说明整类东西是什么样
scene: A teacher points to a chart and says: For instance, this one student missed class for a week and still caught up.
sceneCN: 这里 instance 是「例子」（第 1 个义项：用单个事例说明一般情况）；句意：比如，这名学生缺课一周，仍然赶上了。画面里有图表、教师和一名被点到的学生。

pos.zh: 实例；例子；事例；场合；诉讼程序
援引为例；举……为例

collocations.zh: 在这种情况下；在此例中

senses.title: A single example of a general thing
senses.titleCN: 实例：用单个事例说明一般情况
senses.definition: a single fact, event, or case that shows what a general type or rule is like
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某一普遍类型或规则是怎样的单个事实、事件或案例
senses.example: The report cites several instances of waste in the building program.
senses.exampleCN: 报告举出了该建筑项目中的几个浪费实例。
senses.why: The logical sense 'a fact, a case, an example' appears in English in the early 15c. from Medieval Latin instantia, which translated Greek enstasis. The word moved from urgency to a case that presses a general claim.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑义“事实、案例、例子”在 15 世纪初出现于英语，来自中世纪拉丁语 instantia，后者翻译了希腊语 enstasis。这个词从“紧急”转成“支撑普遍主张的个案”。

senses.title: An occurrence that actually happened
senses.titleCN: 事例：真实发生的一起事件
senses.definition: a particular occurrence or occasion, especially one that can be counted or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 特定的一起发生或场合，尤指可计数或记录者
senses.example: There have been three instances of theft in the dormitory this term.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期宿舍里发生了三起盗窃事件。
senses.why: Once instance means a case, it can name any bounded happening. The word counts events the way a hand counts separate objects, each one standing apart from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 instance 指一个案例，它就能命名任何有边界的事件。这个词像手指数东西一样数事件，每一件都与其他件分开。

senses.title: For instance: here is one case
senses.titleCN: 例如：就拿这一个例子来说
senses.definition: used in the phrase for instance to introduce a single example of a wider statement
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 for instance，引出对更宽泛陈述的一个具体例子
senses.example: Some languages, for instance Japanese, mark politeness in grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言，例如日语，会在语法中标记礼貌。
senses.why: For instance is recorded from the 1650s. The phrase asks the listener to stand on one instance, one case, and see the general rule through it; the older noun phrase give someone a for instance dates from 1953.
senses.whyCN: for instance 自 16 世纪 50 年代起记录。这个短语请听者站在一个 instance、一个案例上，透过它看见普遍规则；更早的名词短语 give someone a for instance 可追溯到 1953 年。

senses.title: In this particular case
senses.titleCN: 在此情况下：就这一个具体场合而言
senses.definition: the particular situation or occasion being considered, as in in this instance
senses.definitionCN: 正在被考虑的具体情境或场合，如 in this instance
senses.example: In this instance, the committee decided to waive the fee.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种情况下，委员会决定免除费用。
senses.why: Instance can mean the occasion itself, not an example of a type. The shift is small: one case is both an example and the particular situation in which a decision is made.
senses.whyCN: instance 可以指场合本身，而不是某一类型的例子。这个转变很小：一个案例既是一个例子，也是作出决定时所处的具体情境。

senses.title: A stage in legal proceedings
senses.titleCN: 诉讼程序：司法过程中的一个审级或程序
senses.definition: a particular stage or proceeding in a court case, as in a court of first instance
senses.definitionCN: 案件中的一个特定审级或程序，如初审法院
senses.example: The case was heard at first instance in a local court.
senses.exampleCN: 该案先在当地法院进行初审。
senses.why: Legal Latin used instantia for a pressing matter, and court procedure gave it a technical sense: the instance is the stage at which a case is actually pressed. A court of first instance is where the case is first heard.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语用 instantia 指紧迫事务，法庭程序又给它技术义：instance 是案件真正被推进的审级。court of first instance 就是案件首次受审的法院。

senses.title: Urgency or insistence, the oldest sense
senses.titleCN: 紧急；坚持：最古老的一层意思
senses.definition: urgency, insistence, or earnest pressure, a sense now archaic
senses.definitionCN: 紧迫、坚持或恳切催促，现为古旧义
senses.example: In the old play, the messenger speaks with great instance about the approaching army.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部古老的戏剧里，信使极为急切地谈到逼近的军队。
senses.why: The noun enters English in the late 14c. as 'urgency, insistence', from Old French instance 'effort, application; urgency, eagerness'. This is the oldest layer, before the word came to mean a case.
senses.whyCN: 名词在 14 世纪后期进入英语，意为“紧迫、坚持”，来自古法语 instance“努力、专注；紧迫、急切”。这是最古老的一层，在“案例”义之前。

senses.title: At someone's request or urging
senses.titleCN: 应某人之请：因某人的敦促而做
senses.definition: used in at the instance of to mean at the request or urging of someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于 at the instance of，意为应某人的请求或敦促
senses.example: The inquiry was opened at the instance of the victims' families.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查是应受害者家属的请求而启动的。
senses.why: The old sense of urgent pressure survives in at the instance of. Here instance is the force of someone's insistence, not an example; the preposition shows the social direction of that pressure.
senses.whyCN: “紧迫压力”的旧义保存在 at the instance of 中。这里的 instance 是某人坚持的力量，而非例子；介词显示这种压力的社会方向。

senses.title: To cite as an example
senses.titleCN: 援引为例：把某事举出来作证
senses.definition: to cite or mention something as an example or proof
senses.definitionCN: 把某事引用或提出来作为例子或证据
senses.example: The author instanced the fall of Rome as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 作者以罗马的衰亡为例提出警告。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from c. 1600 as 'cite as an instance'. Middle English had instauncen 'to plead with, urge and entreat', showing again how the old pressure and the new example senses sit side by side.
senses.whyCN: 动词自约 1600 年记录为“援引为例”。中古英语有 instauncen“恳求、敦促”，再次显示旧的“压力”义与新的“例子”义并排存在。

senses.title: One running copy in computing
senses.titleCN: 实例：计算机中运行的一个具体对象
senses.definition: in computing, a single running copy of a program, class, or database
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中程序、类或数据库的一个正在运行的具体副本
senses.example: The server runs three instances of the same application.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器运行着同一个应用的三个实例。
senses.why: Computer science borrows the logical sense and makes it technical: a class is the general type, an instance is one concrete case of it. The old example relation becomes an exact technical relation.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学借走逻辑义并使之技术化：类是普遍类型，instance 是它的一个具体案例。旧的“例子”关系变成了精确的技术关系。

intro.en: Instance is Latin 'a standing near'. It began as urgency and insistence, then became a case that presses a claim, then a single example, and finally a technical legal and computing unit.
intro.cn: instance 是拉丁语“站在附近”。它起初指紧迫与坚持，后来指支撑主张的案例，再指单个例子，最后成为法律与计算机中的技术单位。

items.en: The root *sta- 'to stand' is reconstructed, not written. No text records it, so this deepest step is source uncertain; it is inferred from Latin stare and English stand.
items.cn: 词根 *sta-“站立”是构拟形式，没有书面记录。因此最深的这一步是“来源不确定”，只能从拉丁语 stare 与英语 stand 推断。

items.en: Stare meant 'to stand'. With the prefix in-, it formed instare 'to stand upon, press upon, be present or urgent'.
items.cn: stare 意为“站立”。加前缀 in- 构成 instare“站在上面、压在上面、在场或紧迫”。

items.en: Instantia meant 'presence, effort, intention; earnestness, urgency', literally 'a standing near'. The pressure in the word is still physical.
items.cn: instantia 意为“在场、努力、意图；恳切、紧迫”，字面是“站在附近”。词里的压力仍是物理性的。

items.en: Old French instance meant 'effort, application; urgency, eagerness, anxiety', carrying the Latin sense of pressing nearness.
items.cn: 古法语 instance 意为“努力、专注；紧迫、急切、焦虑”，带着拉丁语“逼近的压力”之意。

items.en: English instance is first recorded as 'urgency, insistence', a sense now archaic. The word still meant pressure, not example.
items.cn: 英语 instance 最早记录为“紧迫、坚持”，此义今已古旧。这个词当时仍指压力，而非例子。

items.en: The logical sense 'a fact, a case, an example' appears in the early 15c. from Medieval Latin instantia, which translated Greek enstasis. For instance follows in the 1650s.
items.cn: 逻辑义“事实、案例、例子”于 15 世纪初出现，来自中世纪拉丁语 instantia，后者翻译了希腊语 enstasis。for instance 随后在 16 世纪 50 年代出现。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a very short moment, or happening immediately. It is the present-participle form of the same Latin verb, literally 'standing near'.
entries.definitionCN: 瞬间；立即的。它是同一个拉丁动词的现在分词形式，字面是“站在附近”。

entries.definition: the space between two points. It comes from dis- 'apart' plus stare 'to stand'.
entries.definitionCN: 距离。它来自 dis-“分开”加 stare“站立”。

entries.definition: the material or essential quality of something. It comes from sub- 'under' plus stare, what stands beneath.
entries.definitionCN: 物质；实质。它来自 sub-“在下”加 stare，即站在下面的东西。

entries.definition: a way of standing, or an stated attitude. It is the bare root noun behind instance.
entries.definitionCN: 站姿；立场。它是 instance 背后裸露的词根名词。

entries.definition: a thing that shows what a general rule or type is like. It is the closest everyday synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 例子；榜样。它是最接近的日常同义词。

entries.definition: a particular situation, occurrence, or legal matter. It is broader and more neutral than instance.
entries.definitionCN: 情况；案例；案件。它比 instance 更宽、更中性。

entries.definition: something that happens. It fits instance sense 02, a recorded event.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的事件。它对应 instance 第 2 义，即被记录的事件。

entries.definition: an example or picture used to explain something. It stresses the explaining function.
entries.definitionCN: 例证；插图。它强调解释功能。

entries.definition: a single sample used to represent a whole group. It is more physical than instance.
entries.definitionCN: 样本；标本。它比 instance 更具体。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin stare 'to stand', instare 'to stand upon', instantia 'a standing near', and the English phrase for instance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 stare“站立”、instare“站在上面”、instantia“站在附近”，以及英语短语 for instance。

normal.en: instance comes from a 'standing near': a case stands beside a general rule as its witness.
normal.cn: instance 来自“站在附近”：一个案例站在普遍规则旁边，作它的见证。

normal.en: For instance means: let one case stand here so that we can see the rule in it.
normal.cn: for instance 意为：让一个案例站在这里，好让我们在其中看见规则。

normal.en: At the instance of someone is the old sense of pressure: that person's insistence stands behind the act.
normal.cn: at the instance of someone 是旧的“压力”义：那个人的坚持站在行为背后。

normal.en: A court of first instance is where the case first stands before a judge.
normal.cn: court of first instance 就是案件第一次站到法官面前的法院。

normal.en: In computing, a class is the pattern and an instance is one copy standing on its own.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，类是模式，instance 是独立站出来的一个副本。

abstract.en: The core is a single case standing beside a general type, close enough to be pointed at.
abstract.cn: 核心是一个个案站在普遍类型旁边，近到可以用手指出来。

abstract.en: The word moves from pressure to proof: insistence becomes the case that insists on a conclusion.
abstract.cn: 这个词从压力走到证据：坚持变成那个“坚持指向结论”的案例。

abstract.en: So example, occasion, lawsuit and software object are one thing seen at four levels of abstraction.
abstract.cn: 所以例子、场合、诉讼与软件对象，是同一个东西在四种抽象层级上的样子。

examples.en: This is one instance of a problem that appears across the country.
examples.cn: 这是全国范围内都存在的一个问题的一个实例。

examples.en: For instance, a small change in temperature can alter the result.
examples.cn: 例如，温度的微小变化就能改变结果。

examples.en: The court of first instance refused to hear the new evidence.
examples.cn: 初审法院拒绝听取新证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ stance（站立）——规则里面站着的那个具体个案 → instance 实例

root: 源自拉丁语 stare“站立”，加 in- 构成 instare“站在上面、逼近”，名词 instantia 字面为“站在附近、在场、紧迫”，14 世纪后期进入英语，由“坚持”转为“个案、实例”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of instance, all built on one case standing near: an example of a type, a happening, the phrase for instance, a situation, a legal stage, an old urgency, a request, a cited proof, and a running copy in software.
sensesIntro.cn: instance 的九个义项都建在同一个“站在附近的案例”上：类型的例子、发生的事件、for instance、具体情境、法律审级、古老的紧迫、请求、被援引的证据，以及软件中运行的副本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one case standing beside a general rule, close enough to be pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个个案站在普遍规则旁边，近到可以用手指出来。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: a single case that illustrates a type, and the phrase that introduces it.
branches.cn: 例子：说明一个类型的单个案例，以及引出它的短语。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: an event that happened, and the particular situation under discussion.
branches.cn: 场合：真实发生的事件，以及正在讨论的具体情境。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL UNIT: a stage in court, and one running copy in computing.
branches.cn: 技术单位：法庭中的一个审级，以及计算机中一个运行副本。

branches.en: THE OLD PRESSURE: urgency or insistence, and the request that carries it.
branches.cn: 旧的压力：紧迫或坚持，以及承载它的请求。

branches.en: THE CITED PROOF: the verb that holds an example up as evidence.
branches.cn: 被援引的证据：把例子举起来作证的动词。

intro.en: Instance is in- plus the root st- 'stand' plus -ance. Its family shows the prefixes in-, con-, sub-, circum-, dis- and the suffixes -ance, -ant, -ly, -aneous, -ate, -ion.
intro.cn: instance 是 in- 加词根 st-“站立”再加 -ance。它的词族展示前缀 in-、con-、sub-、circum-、dis-，以及后缀 -ance、-ant、-ly、-aneous、-ate、-ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'to stand' is the base of instance, instant, constant, substance and distance; the same verb with different prefixes describes where something stands.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare“站立”是 instance、instant、constant、substance、distance 的基础；同一个动词配不同前缀，描述某物站在何处。

items.meaning: a case standing near; an example
items.meaningCN: 实例；例子（站在附近 + -ance）
items.example: This is a clear instance of poor planning.
items.exampleCN: 这是规划不善的一个明显例子。

items.meaning: a moment; immediate
items.meaningCN: 瞬间；立即的（站到眼前的一刻）
items.example: The reply came in an instant.
items.exampleCN: 回复瞬间就来了。

items.meaning: immediately
items.meaningCN: 立即地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She recognized him instantly.
items.exampleCN: 她立刻认出了他。

items.meaning: happening in an instant
items.meaningCN: 瞬间发生的（-aneous 形容词后缀）
items.example: The reaction was almost instantaneous.
items.exampleCN: 反应几乎是瞬间的。

items.meaning: to represent by a concrete instance
items.meaningCN: 实例化；用实例表示（-ate 动词后缀）
items.example: The program instantiates a new object each time.
items.exampleCN: 程序每次都会实例化一个新对象。

items.meaning: the act of making a concrete instance
items.meaningCN: 实例化（-ion 表动作）
items.example: Each instantiation of the class uses its own memory.
items.exampleCN: 该类的每个实例都使用自己的内存。

items.meaning: standing firm; unchanging
items.meaningCN: 不变的；持续的（共同站稳 + -ant）
items.example: The temperature remained constant all night.
items.exampleCN: 温度整夜保持不变。

items.meaning: what stands under; material or essence
items.meaningCN: 物质；实质（站在下面 + -ance）
items.example: The substance felt like wax.
items.exampleCN: 这种物质摸起来像蜡。

items.meaning: the conditions standing around an event
items.meaningCN: 环境；情况（站在周围 + -ance）
items.example: Under no circumstances should you open the door.
items.exampleCN: 在任何情况下你都不该开门。

items.meaning: the space standing between two points
items.meaningCN: 距离（分开站立 + -ance）
items.example: The distance between the two towns is ten miles.
items.exampleCN: 两镇之间的距离是十英里。
