senses.title: An organization set up for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 机构：为特定目的设立的组织
senses.definition: an organization founded to promote a particular activity, especially education, science, or the arts
senses.definitionCN: 为促进某项活动而设立的组织，尤指教育、科学或艺术领域
senses.example: The institute offers free training to young researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家机构为年轻研究人员提供免费培训。
senses.why: The noun institute is recorded in the 1510s as 'purpose, design', from Latin institutum 'thing set up'. The 1828 sense 'organization devoted to specific work' came through French, especially the Institut national des Sciences et des Arts.
senses.whyCN: 名词 institute 于 16 世纪 10 年代记录为“目的、设计”，来自拉丁语 institutum“被设立之物”。1828 年的“从事特定工作的组织”义经法语而来，尤其是 Institut national des Sciences et des Arts。

senses.title: A research institute
senses.titleCN: 研究所：以研究为专职的机构
senses.definition: a body of scholars or scientists organized to carry out research in a field
senses.definitionCN: 为在某一领域开展研究而组织起来的学者或科学家团体
senses.example: The institute publishes an annual report on climate data.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究所发布气候数据年度报告。
senses.why: Once the 1828 sense named an organization for specific work, the most natural specialization was research. The word's origin as a 'thing set up' is still visible: the institute is a standing arrangement for producing knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 1828 年的义项命名了从事特定工作的组织，最自然的 specialization 就是研究。词源“被设立之物”仍可见：研究所是一种为生产知识而稳稳立住的安排。

senses.title: A technical or specialized school
senses.titleCN: 学院：以专门技艺为课程的学校
senses.definition: a school or college devoted to a particular subject or technical training
senses.definitionCN: 专攻某一学科或技术训练的学校或学院
senses.example: She studied fashion design at a small institute in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她在城里一所小型学院学习时装设计。
senses.why: An institute can also be an educational body, because teaching was one of the things Latin instituere named. The modern school sense is the older 'establish and instruct' meaning carried by an organization.
senses.whyCN: institute 也可以指教育机构，因为教学本是拉丁语 instituere 命名的事项之一。现代学校义是更古老的“设立并教导”之意，由机构承载下来。

senses.title: To establish or found
senses.titleCN: 建立；设立：让一个组织正式立起来
senses.definition: to formally set up an organization, system, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 正式建立组织、制度或安排
senses.example: The university was instituted in 1890 with private funds.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学于 1890 年由私人资金建立。
senses.why: The verb is recorded in early 14c. as 'to establish in office, appoint', and the general sense 'set up, found, introduce' appears in the late 15c. Latin instituere is in- plus statuere 'cause to stand': founding is making something stand.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 14 世纪初记录为“任命、使就职”，一般义“建立、设立、引入”出现在 15 世纪后期。拉丁语 instituere 是 in- 加 statuere“使站立”：创立就是让某物立住。

senses.title: To put a system or rule in force
senses.titleCN: 制定；实行：让制度或规则开始生效
senses.definition: to establish a rule, policy, reform, or practice and begin to use it
senses.definitionCN: 确立并开始实行一项规则、政策、改革或做法
senses.example: The city instituted a ban on single-use plastics.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市开始实行一次性塑料禁令。
senses.why: A rule is also something that must be made to stand. Latin statuere meant 'cause to stand, establish', so instituting a policy is literally giving it a standing place in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 规则也是一种必须被立起来的东西。拉丁语 statuere 意为“使站立、设立”，所以制定政策字面上就是给它一个在日常生活中的站立位置。

senses.title: To bring a legal action
senses.titleCN: 提起：正式启动诉讼或程序
senses.definition: to begin legal proceedings or an official inquiry against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人正式启动法律程序或官方调查
senses.example: The company instituted legal proceedings against its former supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司对前供应商提起了法律诉讼。
senses.why: Legal English speaks of instituting proceedings because a case must be formally set up before a court. The verb's 'cause to stand' image fits: the action is placed on the court's standing docket.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语说 instituting proceedings，因为案件必须先正式设立于法庭。动词“使站立”的形象正好合适：诉讼被放到法庭的日程上立住。

senses.title: To appoint or install someone
senses.titleCN: 任命；授予圣职：把人正式安置到职位上
senses.definition: to appoint someone to an office, especially a religious position, and formally install them
senses.definitionCN: 任命某人担任职位，尤指宗教职位，并正式使其就职
senses.example: The bishop instituted the new priest in a small ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 主教在一场小型仪式上授予新神父圣职。
senses.why: This is the verb's oldest English sense, 'to establish in office, appoint' (early 14c.). A person is made to stand in a post, so the same root that means 'cause to stand' also means 'install'.
senses.whyCN: 这是动词最古老的英语义“任命、使就职”（14 世纪初）。人被使站立在一个职位上，所以意为“使站立”的同一词根也意为“安置就职”。

senses.title: An established law or custom
senses.titleCN: 制度；法规：已经立住的惯例或法律
senses.definition: an established law, custom, or principle, a now archaic or formal sense of the noun
senses.definitionCN: 已确立的法律、惯例或原则，名词的古旧或正式义
senses.example: The old institute of common grazing survived for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 公共放牧的古老惯例延续了几个世纪。
senses.why: The noun's 1540s sense is 'an established law'. Latin institutum meant 'an ordinance, a custom'. A custom is a practice that has been made to stand, which is exactly what the root says.
senses.whyCN: 名词 16 世纪 40 年代的义项是“已确立的法律”。拉丁语 institutum 意为“法令、惯例”。惯例就是一种被立起来的做法，正合词根所说。

senses.title: To initiate a practice or precedent
senses.titleCN: 开创：让一项做法或先例第一次立起来
senses.definition: to begin or set in motion a practice, tradition, or precedent
senses.definitionCN: 开始或启动一项做法、传统或先例
senses.example: The school instituted a tradition of morning reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校开创了晨读传统。
senses.why: When the thing established is not an organization but a practice, institute means 'initiate'. The metaphor is still spatial: the practice is given a standing place from which later examples can follow.
senses.whyCN: 当被设立的不是组织而是做法时，institute 意为“开创”。隐喻仍是空间的：这项做法被给了一个站立的位置，后来的例子可以从那里跟着来。

intro.en: Institute is Latin 'to cause to stand'. It joins in- with statuere, from stare 'to stand'. It is not related to instruct, which comes from struere 'to pile up, build'. The two English words look alike but stand on different roots.
intro.cn: institute 是拉丁语“使站立”。它由 in- 与 statuere 结合，而 statuere 来自 stare“站立”。它与 instruct 无关，后者来自 struere“堆起、建造”。两个英语词形似，却站在不同词根上。

items.en: The root *sta- 'to stand, make firm' is reconstructed, not written. No text records it, so this deepest step is source uncertain; it is inferred from Latin stare and English stand.
items.cn: 词根 *sta-“站立、使稳固”是构拟形式，没有书面记录。因此最深的这一步是“来源不确定”，只能从拉丁语 stare 与英语 stand 推断。

items.en: Stare meant 'to stand'. Its causative partner statuere meant 'to cause to stand, set up, establish'.
items.cn: stare 意为“站立”。它的使动对应词 statuere 意为“使站立、设立、建立”。

items.en: Instituere, from in- plus statuere, meant 'to set up, put in place; arrange; found, establish; appoint; teach'. The 'teach' branch is a use of the verb, not a different root.
items.cn: instituere 由 in- 加 statuere 构成，意为“设立、放置到位；安排；创立、建立；任命；教导”。其中“教导”是这一动词的用法分支，不是另一个词根。

items.en: The English verb is first recorded as 'to establish in office, appoint'. The general sense 'set up, found, introduce' appears in the late 15c.
items.cn: 英语动词最早记录为“任命、使就职”。一般义“建立、设立、引入”出现在 15 世纪后期。

items.en: The noun appears in the 1510s as 'purpose, design', from Latin institutum 'thing set up'. By the 1540s it also means 'an established law'.
items.cn: 名词于 16 世纪 10 年代出现，意为“目的、设计”，来自拉丁语 institutum“被设立之物”。到 16 世纪 40 年代，它也指“已确立的法律”。

items.en: The sense 'organization devoted to specific work' is recorded from 1828, through French use in the Institut national des Sciences et des Arts. This produced the modern research institute.
items.cn: “从事特定工作的组织”义自 1828 年记录，经法语 Institut national des Sciences et des Arts 的用法而来。这产生了现代的研究所。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate. Note that instruct looks close but has a different root.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。注意 instruct 形似，但词根不同。

entries.definition: an established organization, law, or practice. It is the noun of action and result from institute.
entries.definitionCN: 机构；制度。它是 institute 的动作与结果名词。

entries.definition: to form or make up something. It uses the same statuere 'set up' root with con- 'together'.
entries.definitionCN: 构成；组成。它用同一个 statuere“设立”词根，加 con-“共同”。

entries.definition: to put one thing in place of another. It literally means to set something under or in place of.
entries.definitionCN: 代替；替换。它字面是把某物放在下面或放在原位置。

entries.definition: a carved or cast figure of a person or animal. It comes from statua, something set up standing.
entries.definitionCN: 雕像。它来自 statua，即被立起来的东西。

entries.definition: to teach or give directions. It looks like institute but comes from struere 'to build, pile up', not from stare.
entries.definitionCN: 教导；指示。它形似 institute，但来自 struere“建造、堆起”，而非 stare。

entries.definition: a group of people working together for a purpose. It is the broadest synonym for institute sense 01.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；机构。它是 institute 第 1 义最宽的同义词。

entries.definition: the act of founding something, or an organization so founded. It matches both the verb and noun sides.
entries.definitionCN: 建立；建立的机构。它同时对应动词与名词两侧。

entries.definition: an organization that funds research or charity, or the base on which something stands.
entries.definitionCN: 基金会；基础。它既指资助研究或慈善的组织，也指某物站立的基础。

entries.definition: a society of scholars or a specialized school. It often overlaps with institute sense 02 or 03.
entries.definitionCN: 学会；专门学院。它常与 institute 第 2 或第 3 义重叠。

entries.definition: to establish an organization or city. It is the plain verb behind institute sense 04.
entries.definitionCN: 创立；建立。它是 institute 第 4 义背后的朴素动词。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin stare 'to stand', statuere 'cause to stand', instituere 'set up', and the English family statue, statute, and substitute.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 stare“站立”、statuere“使站立”、instituere“设立”，以及英语词族 statue、statute、substitute。

normal.en: institute = in- + statuere 'cause to stand': to found something is to make it stand.
normal.cn: institute = in- + statuere“使站立”：创立某物就是让它立起来。

normal.en: Statue, statute, station and substitute all share the stand root: each is something placed or made to stand.
normal.cn: statue、statute、station、substitute 都共享“站立”词根：每一个都是被放置或立起来的东西。

normal.en: Do not confuse institute with instruct: instruct builds knowledge (struere, pile up), while institute makes an organization stand (stare).
normal.cn: 不要把 institute 与 instruct 混淆：instruct 建造知识（struere，堆起），institute 使机构站住（stare）。

normal.en: A research institute is a purpose made to stand: a group, a building, and a name fixed in place.
normal.cn: 研究所就是一个被立起来的目的：一群人、一栋楼、一个固定在此处的名字。

normal.en: To institute proceedings is to set a lawsuit on its feet before the court.
normal.cn: institute proceedings 就是让一场诉讼在法庭面前站起来。

abstract.en: The core is causing something to stand: an idea becomes real when it is given a fixed place among people and rules.
abstract.cn: 核心是使某物站立：一个想法在人、规则之间获得固定位置时，才成为现实。

abstract.en: The word moves from appointing a person to founding a body to establishing a practice: first a post, then a building, then a habit.
abstract.cn: 这个词从任命一个人走到创立一个机构，再走到确立一种做法：先是职位，再是建筑，再是习惯。

abstract.en: So institute is both the act of making something stand and the thing that stands: verb and noun are two sides of one gesture.
abstract.cn: 所以 institute 既是使某物站立的动作，也是站立起来的东西：动词与名词是同一个动作的两面。

examples.en: The institute was founded to study diseases of the eye.
examples.cn: 这家研究所是为研究眼部疾病而设立的。

examples.en: The government instituted new rules on data privacy last year.
examples.cn: 政府去年制定了新的数据隐私规则。

examples.en: They instituted proceedings against the contractor in March.
examples.cn: 他们在三月对承包商提起了诉讼。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ stitute（谐音“四提丢的”）——把四样东西提进来立住，组成一个机构 → institute 机构；建立

root: 源自拉丁语 stare“站立”，使动形式 statuere“使站立、设立”，加 in- 构成 instituere“设立、创立、任命”，14 世纪初进入英语；与来自 struere“堆建”的 instruct 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of institute, all built on one act of making something stand: a research body, a school, a law, a reform, a lawsuit, a priest in office, and a tradition begun.
sensesIntro.cn: institute 的九个义项都建在同一个“使某物站立”的动作上：研究机构、学院、法律、改革、诉讼、就职的神父，以及被开创的传统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is made to stand firm in a place, and people and rules gather around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被稳稳立在一个位置上，人与规则围绕它聚拢。

branches.en: THE STANDING BODY: an organization founded for a purpose, and a research institute in particular.
branches.cn: 立起来的机构：为某一目的设立的组织，尤指研究所。

branches.en: THE INSTALLED FORM: a specialized school, and a person formally placed in office.
branches.cn: 被安置的形式：专门学院，以及被正式安置到职位上的人。

branches.en: THE FOUNDING ACT: establishing an organization, and initiating a practice or tradition.
branches.cn: 创立的动作：建立组织，以及开创一项做法或传统。

branches.en: THE RULE THAT STANDS: a policy put in force, and an established law or custom.
branches.cn: 立住的规则：开始生效的政策，以及已确立的法律或惯例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL STANDING: a lawsuit formally set on its feet before a court.
branches.cn: 法律的站立：一场在法庭前被正式立起的诉讼。

intro.en: Institute is in- plus the root stat- 'stand, set up'. Its family shows the prefixes in-, con-, sub-, de- and the suffixes -ion, -al, -ize, -ute, -a.
intro.cn: institute 是 in- 加词根 stat-“站立、设立”。它的词族展示前缀 in-、con-、sub-、de-，以及后缀 -ion、-al、-ize、-ute、-a。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'to stand' and its causative statuere 'cause to stand' are the base of institute, statue, statute, constitute and substitute. The root is standing, not building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare“站立”及其使动形式 statuere“使站立”是 institute、statue、statute、constitute、substitute 的基础。词根是“站立”，不是“建造”。

items.meaning: to set up, found, establish
items.meaningCN: 建立；设立（使站立到位）
items.example: They instituted a scholarship for rural students.
items.exampleCN: 他们为农村学生设立了一项奖学金。

items.meaning: an established organization, law, or practice
items.meaningCN: 机构；制度（-ion 表动作与结果）
items.example: The university is one of the oldest institutions in the country.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学是该国最古老的机构之一。

items.meaning: relating to an institution
items.meaningCN: 机构的；制度性的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The report criticized institutional failures.
items.exampleCN: 报告批评了制度层面的失误。

items.meaning: to make something part of an institution or system
items.meaningCN: 使制度化；使机构化（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: They institutionalized the review process.
items.exampleCN: 他们使审查流程制度化。

items.meaning: to form or make up
items.meaningCN: 构成；组成（共同设立）
items.example: Ten members constitute the committee.
items.exampleCN: 十名成员组成该委员会。

items.meaning: the basic law or makeup of a body
items.meaningCN: 宪法；构成（-ion 名词后缀）
items.example: The constitution protects freedom of speech.
items.exampleCN: 宪法保护言论自由。

items.structure: sub- (under, in place of) + statuere (set up)
items.meaning: to put one thing in place of another
items.meaningCN: 代替；替换（在下面/原位设立）
items.example: You can substitute honey for sugar.
items.exampleCN: 你可以用蜂蜜代替糖。

items.meaning: a figure set up to stand in a place
items.meaningCN: 雕像（被立起来的东西）
items.example: A bronze statue stands in the square.
items.exampleCN: 广场上立着一尊青铜雕像。

items.meaning: extremely poor; literally left standing without support
items.meaningCN: 赤贫的（被丢下、无依无靠地站着）
items.example: The flood left hundreds of families destitute.
items.exampleCN: 洪水使数百个家庭一贫如洗。

items.meaning: a written law formally set up
items.meaningCN: 法规；成文法（被正式设立之物）
items.example: The statute limits the length of the working week.
items.exampleCN: 该法规限制了每周工作时长。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, set up, establish
to set up, found, appoint; teach

definition_zh: 教导；指导；命令；指示；正式告知；委托（律师）；向（陪审团）作法律指示
definition_en: to teach someone a subject or skill, or to give someone an authoritative direction, order, or piece of information
core_image: 把散落的木料一根根堆起、排成一条笔直的梁——先备齐材料，再让它们按次序站好
scene: The coach instructs the swimmers to keep their stroke long.
sceneCN: 这里 instruct 是「指导、指示」（第 02 个义项：用明确要求训练某人）；句意：教练指导队员保持划水幅度。画面里池边的教练举着秒表，水中的队员把手臂尽量拉长，动作被排成一条有序的线。

pos.zh: 教导；指导；命令；指示；告知；（法律）委托（律师）；向（陪审团）作法律指示

collocations.zh: 教某人某门学问或技能

derivatives.zh: 可教育的；能接受教导的（罕用）

senses.title: Teach a subject: build knowledge into a mind
senses.titleCN: 教授科目：把知识搭进脑子里
senses.definition: to teach someone a subject or skill, especially in a formal or organized way
senses.definitionCN: 以正规或有条理的方式教某人一门学科或技能
senses.example: The nurse instructed the new staff in infection control.
senses.exampleCN: 护士教新员工感染控制的知识。
senses.why: The verb appears in English early 15c. as 'to tell, inform, impart knowledge'. It comes from Latin instruere, literally 'to build, erect': knowledge is piled up in order inside a mind, the way timber is stacked into a beam.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在 15 世纪早期进入英语，意为“告知、传授知识”。它来自拉丁语 instruere，字面是“建造、竖立”：知识像木料被堆成一根梁那样，在头脑里被按次序搭起来。

senses.title: Coach by showing: set the body's movements in order
senses.titleCN: 示范训练：把身体的动作排成次序
senses.definition: to train or coach someone by giving precise directions and repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过精确要求和反复练习来训练或指导某人
senses.example: The coach instructed the swimmers to keep their stroke long.
senses.exampleCN: 教练指导游泳队员保持划水幅度。
senses.why: Instruere also meant 'arrange, set in order'. A coach does exactly that with limbs and timing: the body is arranged into a shape that works, then repeated until it holds.
senses.whyCN: instruere 也有“排列、使有序”的意思。教练对四肢和节奏做的正是这件事：把身体排成一个有效的形状，再反复练习直到它固定下来。

senses.title: Order: lay down what must be done
senses.titleCN: 命令：把必须做的事定下来
senses.definition: to give someone an order or authoritative direction to do something
senses.definitionCN: 向某人下达命令或权威性指示，要求其做某事
senses.example: The officer instructed us to stay behind the line.
senses.exampleCN: 军官命令我们待在界线后面。
senses.why: Early 15c. English already used instruct for 'furnish with authoritative directions'. Here the ordered structure is not built into a mind but imposed on someone else's action: a sequence handed down from above.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪早期的英语里，instruct 已经表示“给予权威性指示”。这时被排成次序的不是头脑中的知识，而是别人的行动：一串从上方交下来的步骤。

senses.title: Inform officially: pass the word down
senses.titleCN: 正式告知：把消息传下来
senses.definition: to inform someone officially or formally of a fact or decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方地告知某人某一事实或决定
senses.example: We have been instructed that the hearing is postponed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们已获正式通知，听证会延期。
senses.why: The earliest English sense is simply 'to tell, inform'. The authority of the teller is what makes it instruct rather than mention: the information is handed down as an arranged, settled statement.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义项就是“告知、通知”。说话者的权威使它成为 instruct 而不是随口一提：信息被作为一条排定好的说法传下来。

senses.title: Brief a lawyer: hand the case over in order
senses.titleCN: 委托律师：把案情有条理地交出去
senses.definition: in British legal usage, to employ a solicitor or barrister and give them the facts and directions of a case
senses.definitionCN: 在英国法律用语中，聘请事务律师或出庭律师并向其交代案情与指示
senses.example: She instructed her solicitor to prepare the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 她委托律师起草合同。
senses.why: A client does not merely talk to a lawyer; the client arranges the facts and the aim into a brief. The old 'authoritative directions' sense settles into a professional procedure: the case is set in order for someone else to act on.
senses.whyCN: 当事人不只是和律师说话，而是把事实与目标排成一份案情摘要。古老的“权威指示”义在这里落成一套职业程序：把案件整理有序，交给另一个人去办。

senses.title: Give the steps: tell exactly how to operate
senses.titleCN: 交代步骤：说明到底怎么操作
senses.definition: to give detailed directions for carrying out a task, using a device, or following a procedure
senses.definitionCN: 为完成一项任务、使用一台设备或遵循某个程序而给出详细做法
senses.example: The label instructs users to shake the bottle before opening.
senses.exampleCN: 标签说明要求用户开瓶前摇匀。
senses.why: An instruction is an ordered list: first this, then that. The same 'arrange in sequence' base shows through when instruct means 'tell someone the exact steps' rather than 'teach a whole subject'.
senses.whyCN: instruction 就是一张有序清单：先这样，再那样。当 instruct 表示“告诉人确切步骤”而不是“教一整门课”时，透出的仍是同一个“按顺序排列”的词基。

senses.title: Form a person: moral and religious teaching
senses.titleCN: 教化：道德与宗教上的训导
senses.definition: to teach someone moral or religious duties, especially over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 长期教导某人道德或宗教上的责任
senses.example: The elders instructed the young in the duties of the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 长辈教导年轻人秋收时该尽的责任。
senses.why: Latin instruere was used for teaching doctrine, and 'inform, teach' in English kept that weight. Moral instruction arranges a whole life, not just a lesson: duties are put in order so they can be lived.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instruere 曾用于传授教义，英语“告知、教导”义保留了这份分量。道德训导安排的是整个生活而不只是一堂课：责任被排好次序，以便人去践行。

senses.title: Charge the jury: the judge lays out the law
senses.titleCN: 指示陪审团：法官把法律摆清楚
senses.definition: of a judge, to explain the relevant law and give directions to a jury before it decides
senses.definitionCN: 指法官在陪审团裁决前解释相关法律并作出指示
senses.example: The judge instructed the jury to disregard the last remark.
senses.exampleCN: 法官指示陪审团不要考虑刚才那句话。
senses.why: This is the 'authoritative directions' sense in court. The judge sets the legal rules in order for the jury, just as a builder sets timbers in order: the same word, a different material.
senses.whyCN: 这是“权威指示”义在法庭上的样子。法官把法律规则按次序摆给陪审团，正如建造者把木料排好：同一个词，只是材料换了。

senses.title: Command a machine: issue a structured order
senses.titleCN: 给机器下指令：发出结构化命令
senses.definition: to give a coded or structured command to a device or program
senses.definitionCN: 向设备或程序发出编码的、结构化的命令
senses.example: The controller instructs the printer to switch to the backup tray.
senses.exampleCN: 控制器指示打印机切换到备用纸盒。
senses.why: In 20c. computing, a human order became a line of code. The receiver is no longer a mind that must understand, but a system that must execute; the direction is still arranged step by step.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪计算机用法里，人的命令变成了一行代码。接收者不再是要理解的头脑，而是必须执行的系统；指示依然按步骤排好。

intro.en: Instruct comes from Latin instruere 'arrange, prepare, set in order; inform, teach', literally 'to build, erect', from in- 'on, upon' and struere 'to pile, build'. The same struere gives structure and construct. English took the verb early 15c., keeping both halves: to teach and to order.
intro.cn: instruct 来自拉丁语 instruere“排列、准备、使有序；告知、教导”，字面是“建造、竖立”，由 in-“在上”与 struere“堆、建”构成。同一个 struere 也生出 structure 与 construct。英语在 15 世纪早期借入这个动词，并保留了两半意思：教与令。

items.en: Instruere joined in- 'on, upon' to struere 'to pile, build'. Its first image is physical: materials laid on top of one another until an ordered structure stands. It also meant 'draw up troops, equip, prepare'.
items.cn: instruere 把 in-“在上”接到 struere“堆、建”上。它最初的画面是物理的：材料一层层叠上去，直到一个有序的结构立起来。它也有“列队、装备、准备”的意思。

items.en: The physical image turned inward. Arranging facts or people in order became 'to inform, teach'; the past participle instructus carried both 'prepared' and 'taught'. The PIE root behind struere, *stere- 'to spread', is a reconstructed form with no written record, so its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 物理画面转向内里：把事实或人排好，变成了“告知、教导”；过去分词 instructus 同时带“准备好”和“被教过”两义。struere 背后的原始印欧词根 *stere-“铺开”是重构形式，没有书面记录，来源不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin instructor meant 'teacher' (in classical Latin, 'preparer'), and Old French passed instruction and instructor toward English. The teaching branch was now a settled school word.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 instructor 意为“教师”（古典拉丁语中为“准备者”），古法语把 instruction 与 instructor 传向英语。教学的这一支此时已是固定的学堂用语。

items.en: The verb enters English as 'to tell, inform, impart knowledge or information', and also 'furnish with authoritative directions'. Teaching and commanding arrive in the same word, because both are ways of putting something in order for someone.
items.cn: 动词在 15 世纪早期进入英语，意为“告知、通知、传授知识或信息”，同时也有“给予权威性指示”。教与令落在同一个词里，因为两者都是替别人把某事排好。

items.en: The noun instruction covers both 'teaching' and 'an order or direction', and instructor (mid-15c.) names the one who builds knowledge in others. Instructive appears in the 1610s; the older adjective instructing dates from the 1580s.
items.cn: 名词 instruction 同时覆盖“教学”与“命令、指示”，instructor（15 世纪中期）指在别人脑中搭建知识的人。instructive 出现于 17 世纪 10 年代；更早的形容词 instructing 可追溯到 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: Legal usage fixed 'instruct a solicitor' and 'instruct the jury'. In the later 20c. computing added 'instruct a device', where the order is coded rather than spoken. The old act of stacking in order survives in every branch.
items.cn: 法律用法固定了 instruct a solicitor（委托律师）与 instruct the jury（指示陪审团）。20 世纪后期计算机用法又添了“给设备下指令”，命令不再靠嘴说而是写成代码。那个“按次序堆叠”的老动作，在每一支里都还活着。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin struere base and therefore the -struct- shape; the second group shares one or another of instruct's meanings. Keep the spelling family and the sense family apart.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁语 struere 词基，因此都有 -struct- 的词形；第二组只与 instruct 的某一个义项相近。把“词形家族”和“词义家族”分开记。

entries.definition: to build or put something together from parts. It uses the same 'pile up' root, but the material is physical.
entries.definitionCN: 建造；构造。同样用“堆起来”的词根，但材料是实物。

entries.definition: to block a way or hold up a process by putting something in the way. Here the piling is against you.
entries.definitionCN: 阻挡；妨碍。这里的“堆”是堆在你要通过的路上。

entries.definition: the way parts are arranged into a whole, or the thing so arranged. It is the noun of the ordered stacking itself.
entries.definitionCN: 结构；构造物。它正是“有序堆叠”这件事的名词形式。

entries.definition: a tool or device used for a task. Latin instrumentum came from instruere 'equip, furnish', so it is a distant cousin of instruct.
entries.definitionCN: 工具；器械。拉丁语 instrumentum 来自 instruere“装备、备办”，因此是 instruct 的远亲。

entries.definition: to help someone learn a subject or skill. It matches instruct's teaching sense but carries no order or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 教；讲授。对应 instruct 的教学义，但不带命令或权威色彩。

entries.definition: to teach a skill through repeated practice. It matches instruct in the coaching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 训练；培训。对应 instruct 的教练、训练义。

entries.definition: to tell someone how to do something or where to go. It matches instruct's 'give directions' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指导；指挥。对应 instruct 的“给出做法、指明方向”义。

entries.definition: to tell someone firmly that they must do something. It matches instruct's command sense most closely.
entries.definitionCN: 命令；下令。与 instruct 的命令义最贴近。

entries.definition: to tell someone a fact. It matches instruct's formal 'notify' sense without the teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 告知；通知。对应 instruct 的正式“通知”义，但不含教学。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: struere 'build' behind structure, construct and destroy, the same in- prefix in instrument, and the double life of instruction as both a lesson and an order.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：structure、construct、destroy 背后的 struere“建造”，instrument 里同样的 in- 前缀，以及 instruction 同时是“课”又是“命令”的双重身份。

normal.en: instruct = in- 'on' + struere 'pile': you pile knowledge onto a learner until it stands as a structure.
normal.cn: instruct = in-“在上”+ struere“堆”：把知识一层层堆到学习者身上，直到它立成一个结构。

normal.en: construct and instruct are brothers: one piles bricks, the other piles ideas.
normal.cn: construct 与 instruct 是兄弟：一个堆砖，一个堆想法。

normal.en: An instruction sheet is a structure on paper: the steps are stacked in the only order that works.
normal.cn: 一张 instruction 说明就是纸上的结构：步骤被堆成唯一能奏效的那个次序。

normal.en: instructor: the person who builds the frame inside your head, then hands you the tools.
normal.cn: instructor：先在你脑袋里搭起框架、再把工具递给你的人。

normal.en: To instruct a lawyer is to stack the facts in order before the case can stand.
normal.cn: instruct a lawyer 就是先把事实按次序堆好，案子才立得起来。

abstract.en: Teaching and commanding share one word because both arrange another person's future: what they will know, or what they will do.
abstract.cn: 教与令共用一个词，因为两者都在安排别人的未来：他将知道什么，或将做什么。

abstract.en: A structure is stable only if every piece is in place; so an instruction is only clear when every step is in order.
abstract.cn: 结构只有每块都在位才稳；同样，指示只有每一步都在序才清楚。

abstract.en: The word prefers slow building to quick telling: to instruct is to make something hold, not merely to say it.
abstract.cn: 这个词偏爱缓慢搭建而非快速告知：instruct 是让某样东西立住，而不只是说出来。

examples.en: The teacher instructed the students in the use of the microscope.
examples.cn: 老师教学生使用显微镜。

examples.en: We were instructed to wait outside until our names were called.
examples.cn: 我们被告知在外面等候，直到叫到名字。

examples.en: She instructed her solicitor to prepare the contract before Friday.
examples.cn: 她委托律师在周五前起草合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬是拽课”——in（往里）+ struct（结构）：把知识一根根堆进脑子里的结构，就是教导、指示

root: 源自拉丁语 instruere“排列、准备、使有序；告知、教导”，字面“堆建、竖立”，由 in-“在上”+ struere“堆、建”构成；struere 上溯重构的原始印欧词根 *stere-“铺开”（重构形式，无书面记录，来源不确定）。15 世纪早期进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of instruct, all built on one Latin act: instruere, to pile material into an ordered structure. Teach, coach, order, inform, brief, and command are the same act aimed at different receivers — a mind, a body, a lawyer, a jury, a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: instruct 的九个义项都建立在同一个拉丁动作上：instruere，把材料堆成一个有序结构。教、练、令、告、委托、指挥，都是同一个动作对准不同的接收者——头脑、身体、律师、陪审团、机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose material stacked into an ordered structure, then that order placed into a mind or an action.
core.cn: 核心意象：把散乱材料堆成有序结构，再把这个次序放进一个头脑或一项行动里。

branches.en: BUILDING A MIND: a subject is taught, and a body is trained until the movement holds its shape.
branches.cn: 搭起一个头脑：既教一门学科，也训练一具身体，直到动作稳住它的形状。

branches.en: ORDERING AN ACTION: a command is laid down, and a procedure is spelled out step by step.
branches.cn: 安排一项行动：既下达命令，也把操作程序一步步说清。

branches.en: FORMAL DELIVERY: information is officially passed down, and a judge lays out the law for a jury.
branches.cn: 正式交付：信息被官方传下，法官把法律摆给陪审团。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONAL BRIEF: facts and aims are arranged and handed to a lawyer to act on.
branches.cn: 职业案情摘要：把事实与目标排好，交给律师去办。

branches.en: FORMING AND COMMANDING: moral teaching shapes a whole life, while code shapes a machine's next move.
branches.cn: 塑造与指挥：道德训导塑造整个生活，代码则规定机器的下一步。

intro.en: Instruct is built on Latin struere 'to pile, build': instruction, instructor and instructive grow from the verb, while construct, structure, obstruct, destroy and instrument share the same building base.
intro.cn: instruct 建立在拉丁语 struere“堆、建”上：instruction、instructor、instructive 由这个动词长出，而 construct、structure、obstruct、destroy、instrument 共用同一个“建造”词基。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere 'to pile, build' gives structura 'a building, arrangement' and instruere 'to build in, equip, teach'. The family is about putting separate pieces into a standing order, whether walls, troops, facts, or a case.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 struere“堆、建”生出 structura“建筑、安排”和 instruere“搭进去、装备、教导”。这个词族讲的是把分开的块放进一个立得住的次序里，不管是墙、队伍、事实还是一场官司。

items.meaning: to build knowledge or directions into someone
items.meaningCN: 教导；指示（in- 在上 + struere 堆建）
items.example: The tutor instructed her in Latin grammar.
items.exampleCN: 导师教她拉丁语语法。

items.meaning: the act of teaching, or an order / step to follow
items.meaningCN: 教学；指示；说明（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Read the instructions before using the machine.
items.exampleCN: 使用机器前请阅读说明。

items.meaning: one who teaches or trains
items.meaningCN: 教练；讲师（-or 表人）
items.example: The driving instructor stayed calm throughout.
items.exampleCN: 驾校教练全程都很镇定。

items.meaning: serving to teach or inform
items.meaningCN: 有教益的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The failure was instructive rather than embarrassing.
items.exampleCN: 这次失败给人教益，而不只是难堪。

items.meaning: capable of being taught
items.meaningCN: 可受教的（-ible 表“能被……的”）
items.example: A patient and instructible pupil learns fastest.
items.exampleCN: 有耐心又肯受教的学生学得最快。

items.meaning: to build by putting parts together
items.meaningCN: 建造；构造（con- 共同 + struere 建）
items.example: They constructed a shelter from driftwood.
items.exampleCN: 他们用浮木搭了一个避身处。

items.meaning: the arrangement of parts, or a built thing
items.meaningCN: 结构；建筑物（-ure 构成名词）
items.example: The bridge's steel structure is unusually light.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥的钢结构异常轻盈。

items.meaning: to pile something against; to block
items.meaningCN: 阻碍；阻塞（ob- 反向 + struere 堆）
items.example: Fallen rocks obstructed the mountain road.
items.exampleCN: 落石阻塞了山路。

items.meaning: to build down; to tear a structure apart
items.meaningCN: 毁坏；摧毁（de- 向下 + struere 建）
items.example: The flood destroyed the old mill.
items.exampleCN: 洪水摧毁了那座老磨坊。

items.meaning: a thing equipped for a task; a tool
items.meaningCN: 工具；器械（-mentum 表手段、工具）
items.example: The surgeon laid out the instruments in order.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生把器械按次序摆好。

latinEntries.meaning: to build in, equip, set in order, teach

definition_zh: 不可或缺的；完整的；固有的；整数的；积分；（古）正直的
definition_en: forming an essential part of a whole, or being whole and complete in itself; (n.) a mathematical integral, or a whole number
core_image: 一块拼图正好卡在整幅画的正中央——抽走它，画面就永远缺一角
scene: Trust is an integral part of any long partnership.
sceneCN: 这里 integral 是「不可或缺的」（第 01 个义项：作为整体必需的一部分）；句意：信任是任何长期伙伴关系中不可或缺的一部分。画面里那块拼图卡在中央，四周的图都靠它才连成一片。

pos.zh: 不可或缺的；完整的；固有的；整数的
积分；整体；整数

collocations.zh: 某事物不可或缺的一部分

senses.title: Essential part: the piece the whole needs
senses.titleCN: 不可或缺：整体少不得的那一块
senses.definition: necessary to make a whole complete; belonging to something as one of its essential parts
senses.definitionCN: 为使整体完整所必需的；作为本质组成部分属于某事物的
senses.example: Teamwork is an integral part of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 团队合作是这份工作不可或缺的一部分。
senses.why: Latin integralis meant 'forming a whole'. A part is integral when the whole would no longer be whole without it: the piece is not an extra but a condition of completeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 integralis 意为“构成一个整体”。当缺了它整体就不再完整时，这一部分就是 integral：它不是附加物，而是完整性的条件。

senses.title: Whole and complete: nothing missing
senses.titleCN: 完整：一样都不缺
senses.definition: whole, complete, and undivided; having all its parts present
senses.definitionCN: 完整的、齐全的、未被分割的；所有部分都在
senses.example: The archive holds an integral set of the letters, with none missing.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有这批信件完整的一套，一封不缺。
senses.why: English used integral in the Latin sense 'whole, entire' from about 1500. The base integer is literally 'untouched': a thing with no part taken away is a thing that is whole.
senses.whyCN: 大约从 1500 年起，英语就用 integral 表达拉丁语的“完整、全部”。词基 integer 字面是“未被碰过”：没有哪一部分被拿走的东西，就是完整的东西。

senses.title: Built in: intrinsic to the thing itself
senses.titleCN: 固有：本来就长在里面
senses.definition: belonging naturally to something as part of its own nature, not added from outside
senses.definitionCN: 作为某物本性的一部分天然属于它，而非从外部添加
senses.example: The lens is integral to the camera, not an accessory.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚镜头是相机固有的部分，不是配件。
senses.why: The late 15c. sense was 'intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole'. If a part belongs to the whole by nature, it is already inside the definition of the thing, not bolted on later.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪后期的义项是“内在的、作为一部分属于整体的”。如果一个部分天然属于整体，它就已经在这件事物的定义之内，而不是后来拧上去的。

senses.title: Calculus: the sum of infinitely many slices
senses.titleCN: 积分：把无穷多小片加起来
senses.definition: a mathematical quantity obtained by summing infinitely many infinitesimal parts; the result of integration
senses.definitionCN: 把无穷多个无穷小部分相加而得到的数学量；积分运算的结果
senses.example: She evaluated the integral from zero to one in a single step.
senses.exampleCN: 她一步就算出了从 0 到 1 的积分。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1610s, and calculus fixed it as the name of a total built from infinitesimal pieces. The mathematical operation is still 'making a whole' out of slices, so it keeps the oldest image.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 10 年代已有记录，微积分把它固定为“由无穷小片拼成的总量”的名称。这个运算仍然是把切片“做成整体”，所以保留着最古老的画面。

senses.title: Whole-number: values that do not split
senses.titleCN: 整数：不可再分的数值
senses.definition: in mathematics, involving or consisting of whole numbers rather than fractions
senses.definitionCN: 数学中涉及或由整数而非分数构成的
senses.example: The equation has an integral solution, x = 4.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个整数解 x = 4。
senses.why: Integer, 'a whole number', is recorded from the 1570s. An integral solution is one that lands exactly on a whole number, with no fraction left over: again the idea is a value that is complete in itself.
senses.whyCN: integer“整数”自 16 世纪 70 年代有记录。integral solution 指恰好落在一个整数上的解，不剩分数：仍然是“自身完整”的那个想法。

senses.title: Indivisible: one unit that cannot be split
senses.titleCN: 不可分割：拆开就失去它本身的一个单元
senses.definition: forming a single undivided unit whose parts cannot be separated without destroying it
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个不可分割的整体；各部分一旦分开，该整体就不复存在
senses.example: The two departments now operate as an integral unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个部门现在作为一个不可分割的整体运作。
senses.why: Integer literally means 'untouched, whole'. An integral unit is one whose parts have not been cut apart; to divide it is to stop it being what it is.
senses.whyCN: integer 字面是“未被触碰、完整”。an integral unit 就是各部分没有被切开的一个单元；把它分开，它就不再是原来的东西。

senses.title: Calculus: the branch that sums wholes
senses.titleCN: 积分学的：把无穷小片加回整体的那套运算
senses.definition: of or relating to mathematical integration, as in integral calculus
senses.definitionCN: 与数学积分有关的，如 integral calculus（积分学）
senses.example: She signed up for a course in integral calculus.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名了一门积分学课程。
senses.why: The noun integral (1610s) named a whole built by summing parts; the adjective then labelled the calculus that computes such wholes.
senses.whyCN: 名词 integral（17 世纪 10 年代）指把各部分加起来所得的整量；形容词随后用来标记计算这种整量的那门微积分。

senses.title: The whole itself: a complete entity
senses.titleCN: 整体本身：一个完整的存在
senses.definition: a whole considered as a single complete entity (now rare)
senses.definitionCN: 被视为单一完整实体的整体（今罕用）
senses.example: The essay treats the city as one integral rather than a set of districts.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把这座城市当作一个整体，而不是一组城区。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1610s as a use of the adjective: what is integral can be named as the integral, the whole thing itself. Modern English prefers whole in this sense, leaving integral mostly to mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 名词在 17 世纪 10 年代由形容词转用而来：完整的东西可以被叫作“那个整体”，即整体本身。现代英语在这个义项上更常用 whole，把 integral 大体留给了数学。

senses.title: Whole-making view: seeing the parts as one design
senses.titleCN: 整体化视角：把各部分看成一个设计
senses.definition: combining all parts into a single coherent view or design, rather than treating them separately
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分结合成一个连贯的视角或设计，而非分开处理
senses.example: The plan takes an integral view of transport, housing and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这个规划对交通、住房和学校采取整体化的视角。
senses.why: The modern 'integral approach' extends the old whole-making base from things to methods. When a way of thinking leaves nothing outside, the method itself becomes integral: it makes its object whole.
senses.whyCN: 现代的 integral approach 把古老的“使成整体”词基从事物扩展到方法。当一种思路不把任何东西留在外面，方法本身也就成了 integral：它在把对象做成整体。

intro.en: Integral comes from Medieval Latin integralis 'forming a whole', from Latin integer 'whole, complete', literally 'untouched' — in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'. Old French intégral passed it to English in the late 15c., first as an adjective, then as a noun in the 1610s.
intro.cn: integral 来自中世纪拉丁语 integralis“构成一个整体的”，再上溯拉丁语 integer“完整的、完全的”，字面“未被碰过”——in-“不”加上 tangere“触碰”的词根。古法语 intégral 在 15 世纪后期把它传给英语，先作形容词，17 世纪 10 年代再作名词。

items.en: Integer meant 'intact, whole, complete' and figuratively 'untainted, upright', literally 'untouched': in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'. The PIE root *tag- 'to touch, handle' behind tangere is a reconstructed form with no written record, so that deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: integer 意为“完好的、完整的、完全的”，比喻义为“未受污染的、正直的”，字面是“未被碰过”：in-“不”加上 tangere“触碰”的词根。tangere 背后的原始印欧词根 *tag-“触摸、把持”是重构形式，没有书面记录，因此更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Integralis 'forming a whole' was built on integer for scholastic and mathematical writing. The word names not just a whole thing but the quality of making or belonging to a whole.
items.cn: integralis“构成一个整体的”在中世纪拉丁语的经院与数学写作中由 integer 构成。这个词不只命名一个完整之物，也命名“构成整体”或“属于整体”的性质。

items.en: Old French intégral carried the adjective sense 'whole, complete'. French also gave English the noun integer through Latin, so the whole family arrived in two waves.
items.cn: 古法语 intégral 带有形容词义“完整的、完全的”。法语也通过拉丁语把名词 integer 给了英语，因此整个词族分两波到达。

items.en: English records integral as 'of or pertaining to a whole; intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole'. From the start it points two ways at once: the whole, and the part that the whole requires.
items.cn: 英语记录 integral 为“与整体有关的；内在的、作为一部分属于整体的”。它从一开始就同时指向两头：整体，以及整体所必需的那一部分。

items.en: The noun appears in the 1610s, formed from the adjective. In 17c. calculus the same word became the name of a total summed from infinitesimal parts; the exact first written date of that technical use is not recorded in the standard etymology.
items.cn: 名词在 17 世纪 10 年代由形容词构成。17 世纪微积分里，同一个词成为“由无穷小部分相加而成的总量”的名称；这一专科用法的确切最早书面年代，标准词源记录未载。

items.en: Modern usage settles into 'an integral part of' and 'integral to', and mathematical 'integral solution' draws on integer 'whole number' (1570s). The untouched whole and the necessary part now live in one word.
items.cn: 现代用法固定为 an integral part of 与 integral to；数学的 integral solution 则取自 integer“整数”（16 世纪 70 年代）。未受碰触的整体与必需的那一部分，如今住在同一个词里。

note.en: The first group is the integer family: same Latin base, different endings and meanings. The second group approaches integral from the side of meaning, where whole, essential and built-in overlap.
note.cn: 第一组是 integer 词族：同一个拉丁词基，不同的词尾与词义。第二组从词义一侧靠近 integral，在“完整、必需、内置”上交叠。

entries.definition: the state of being whole and unbroken, or the quality of being honest. It is the noun of the same 'untouched' base.
entries.definitionCN: 完整、未受损的状态，或诚实的品质。它是同一个“未被碰过”词基的名词。

entries.definition: a whole number, positive, negative, or zero, with no fractional part. It is the source word, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 整数（正、负或零，无小数部分）。它是源词，不是近义词。

entries.definition: to make whole by bringing parts together. It is the verb of the family, while integral is the state or the part.
entries.definitionCN: 整合；使成整体。它是这个词族的动词，而 integral 是状态或部分。

entries.definition: complete and not damaged. It shares the literal 'untouched' image with integer but entered English separately.
entries.definitionCN: 完好无损的。它与 integer 共用“未被碰过”的字面画面，但另走一路进入英语。

entries.definition: absolutely necessary; forming the basic nature of something. It matches integral in the 'indispensable' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；本质的。对应 integral 的“不可或缺”义。

entries.definition: complete, with every part present and nothing missing. It matches integral's 'complete' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；全部的。对应 integral 的“完整”义。

entries.definition: belonging to a thing by its own nature rather than by addition. It matches integral in the 'built-in' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 固有的；内在的。对应 integral 的“内置、本来就有”义。

entries.definition: too important to be without. It is the strongest near-match for 'an integral part'.
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的。它是“不可或缺的一部分”最强的近义表达。

entries.definition: having all necessary parts or elements. It matches integral in the 'whole' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；齐全的。对应 integral 的“整体”义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: in- 'not' plus tangere 'touch' behind integer, intact and contact, the 1570s integer 'whole number', and the calculus integral that sums slices into a whole.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：integer、intact、contact 背后 in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”，16 世纪 70 年代的 integer“整数”，以及把切片加成整体的微积分 integral。

normal.en: integral = in- 'not' + tang- 'touch': a thing nobody has broken off is still whole, and a part the whole cannot lose is integral.
normal.cn: integral = in-“不”+ tang-“碰”：没有谁把它掰掉一块的东西仍然完整，而整体丢不起的那一块就是 integral。

normal.en: integral and intact are the same picture: untouched, therefore undamaged.
normal.cn: integral 和 intact 是同一幅画：没被碰过，所以没有损伤。

normal.en: integer is a number that cannot be split without leaving the family; an integral part is a piece the whole cannot split off.
normal.cn: integer 是一旦拆开就不再是同类数的数；integral part 是整体一拆开就不复完整的那一块。

normal.en: integral and integrate are state and action: integrate makes it whole, integral says it is needed for the whole.
normal.cn: integral 与 integrate 是状态与动作：integrate 把它做成整体，integral 说它是整体所必需的。

normal.en: In calculus the integral is the whole rebuilt from thin slices, so even the math sense is 'make whole'.
normal.cn: 微积分里的 integral 是用薄片重新拼出的整体，所以连数学义也还是“使完整”。

abstract.en: The word's two faces are one: to be indispensable is to be the part without which the whole is no longer whole.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两副面孔其实是一副：不可或缺，就是缺了它整体便不再完整的那一部分。

abstract.en: Integrity of body and integrity of character use the same measure: nothing has been taken away or broken.
abstract.cn: 身体的完整与人格的正直用的是同一把尺：没有东西被拿走，也没有东西被折断。

abstract.en: An integral view is not a view of everything; it is a view in which nothing relevant is left outside.
abstract.cn: 整体化视角并不是把一切都收进来，而是不让任何相关的东西留在外面。

examples.en: Practice is integral to learning a language well.
examples.cn: 要学好一门语言，练习是不可或缺的。

examples.en: The two volumes form one integral work and should not be sold separately.
examples.cn: 这两卷构成一部完整的作品，不应分开出售。

examples.en: The integral of a positive function is the area under its curve.
examples.cn: 正函数的积分是其曲线下方的面积。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因特格柔”——in（不）+ teg（碰）：没被碰过的一块，才是完整、不可或缺的

root: 源自拉丁语 integer“完整的、未受碰触的”（in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”的词根），经中世纪拉丁语 integralis“构成整体的”与古法语 intégral 于 15 世纪后期进入英语；tangere 上溯重构的原始印欧词根 *tag-“触摸”（重构形式，无书面记录，来源不确定）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of integral, all held by one image: a thing untouched and therefore whole, and a part whose removal would break that wholeness. Mathematics adds the integral, the whole rebuilt from slices.
sensesIntro.cn: integral 的九个义项由一个画面托住：一件未被碰过因而完整的东西，以及拿掉就会破坏这份完整的那一部分。数学再加进“积分”——用切片重新拼出的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an untouched, unbroken whole — and the one piece whose loss would leave a hole in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被碰过、未曾断裂的整体——以及失去就会留下缺口的那一块。

branches.en: THE NEEDED PART: what is essential to the whole, and what belongs to it by nature rather than by addition.
branches.cn: 必需的那部分：整体少不得的东西，以及天然属于它而非外加的东西。

branches.en: THE UNBROKEN WHOLE: complete with every part present, and held together as one unit that cannot be split.
branches.cn: 未断的整体：所有部分都在的完整，以及作为一个不可拆分单元而保持一体。

branches.en: NUMBER AND CALCULUS: the integral sums infinitesimal slices, and an integral solution lands on a whole number.
branches.cn: 数与微积分：积分把无穷小切片相加，整数解则恰好落在整数上。

branches.en: CALCULUS AND THE WHOLE: the branch that sums infinitesimal slices, and the whole named as one entity.
branches.cn: 微积分与整体：把无穷小切片加总的那门运算，以及被命名为一个实体的整体。

branches.en: THE WHOLE-MAKING VIEW: a method that leaves no relevant part outside its design.
branches.cn: 使成整体的视角：一种不让任何相关部分落在设计之外的方法。

intro.en: Integral belongs to the Latin integer family: integrity, integrate and integration grow from the same base, while intact, tangible and contact share the 'touch' root that in- negates.
intro.cn: integral 属于拉丁语 integer 词族：integrity、integrate、integration 由同一词基长出，而 intact、tangible、contact 共用那个被 in- 否定的“触碰”词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer 'untouched, whole' gives integralis 'forming a whole' and integrare 'to make whole'. The root tangere 'to touch' also yields tangibilis 'touchable' and contingere 'to touch together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer“未被碰过、完整”生出 integralis“构成整体的”与 integrare“使完整”。词根 tangere“触碰”还生出 tangibilis“可触的”与 contingere“相触、接触”。

items.meaning: forming a whole; essential to a whole
items.meaningCN: 完整的；不可或缺的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Water is integral to every living cell.
items.exampleCN: 水对每一个活细胞都不可或缺。

items.meaning: the quality of being whole or essential
items.meaningCN: 完整性；不可或缺性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The integrality of the collection makes it unique.
items.exampleCN: 这套收藏的完整性使它独一无二。

items.meaning: in a way that forms part of a whole
items.meaningCN: 完整地；作为整体地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two systems are integrally connected.
items.exampleCN: 这两个系统作为一个整体相连。

items.meaning: wholeness; soundness of character
items.meaningCN: 完整；正直（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The integrity of the data must be protected.
items.exampleCN: 数据的完整性必须受到保护。

items.meaning: to make whole by joining parts
items.meaningCN: 整合；使成整体（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The school integrates art into every subject.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校把艺术融入每一门学科。

items.meaning: the act of making whole; also the math operation
items.meaningCN: 整合；一体化；积分（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Economic integration changed the border towns.
items.exampleCN: 经济一体化改变了这些边境城镇。

items.meaning: a whole number; literally an untouched whole
items.meaningCN: 整数（字面“未受碰触的完整之物”）
items.example: Five and minus three are both integers.
items.exampleCN: 5 和 -3 都是整数。

items.meaning: not touched; undamaged
items.meaningCN: 未受碰触的；完好无损的
items.example: The vase survived the move intact.
items.exampleCN: 这只花瓶搬动后仍完好无损。

items.meaning: able to be touched; concrete
items.meaningCN: 可触的；有形的（-ible 表“能被……的”）
items.example: The benefits were tangible, not just promised.
items.exampleCN: 好处是看得见摸得着的，不只是承诺。

items.meaning: the state of touching or communicating
items.meaningCN: 接触；联系（con- 共同 + tact 触碰）
items.example: The two wires must not make contact.
items.exampleCN: 这两根电线不得接触。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 未受碰触的；完整的；正直的

senses.title: Make whole: join the parts into one body
senses.titleCN: 使成整体：把各部分接成一个身子
senses.definition: to bring separate parts or elements together so that they form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部分或要素结合起来，使它们形成一个整体
senses.example: The plan integrates housing, transport and green space.
senses.exampleCN: 这个规划把住房、交通和绿地整合在一起。
senses.why: Integrate enters English in the 1630s meaning 'to render whole, bring together the parts of'. Latin integrare is 'make whole', from integer 'untouched, whole': the parts are not merely added, they are made into one body.
senses.whyCN: integrate 在 17 世纪 30 年代进入英语，意为“使完整、把各部分聚在一起”。拉丁语 integrare 就是“使完整”，来自 integer“未被碰过、完整”：各部分不只是相加，而是被做成一个身子。

senses.title: Fit in: become part of a group
senses.titleCN: 融入：成为群体的一部分
senses.definition: to become accepted as part of a group, community, or society
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个群体、社区或社会被接纳的一部分
senses.example: The new students soon integrated into the life of the college.
senses.exampleCN: 新生很快融入了学院生活。
senses.why: When the whole is a society, the part that joins it must change shape a little to fit. The transitive 'make whole' turns intransitive: the newcomer is the piece finding its place in the existing structure.
senses.whyCN: 当整体是一个社会时，加入其中的部分必须略改形状才能合上。及物的“使完整”于是变成不及物：新来者就是那块在既有结构里找到位置的材料。

senses.title: Merge: put two organizations under one roof
senses.titleCN: 合并：把两个机构放进同一个屋顶
senses.definition: to combine two or more organizations, services, or systems into a single one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多机构、服务或系统合并成一个
senses.example: The two schools were integrated into a single district.
senses.exampleCN: 这两所学校被合并成一个学区。
senses.why: From 'parts into a whole' it is a short step to institutions: separate budgets, staffs and buildings become one body. The 1802 sense 'put together parts or elements and combine them into a whole' made this administrative use natural.
senses.whyCN: 从“部分进入整体”到机构只有一步：分开的预算、人员和楼宇变成同一个身子。1802 年“把部分或要素放在一起合成整体”的义项，让这种行政用法显得自然。

senses.title: Desegregate: take down the racial line
senses.titleCN: 取消隔离：把种族的分界线拆掉
senses.definition: to open a school, neighborhood, or institution to all races and end segregation in it
senses.definitionCN: 向所有种族开放学校、社区或机构，结束其中的种族隔离
senses.example: Federal troops were sent to integrate the high school.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦军队被派去执行这所高中的种族融合。
senses.why: The racial sense dates from 1940 and is probably a back-formation from integration, whose anti-discrimination sense is recorded from 1934. Segregation kept parts apart; integrate makes them one body again.
senses.whyCN: 种族义可追溯到 1940 年，很可能是从 integration 逆构而来，而 integration 的反歧视义在 1934 年已有记录。segregation 把部分隔开，integrate 则把它们重新做成一个身子。

senses.title: Calculus: find the integral
senses.titleCN: 求积分：把切片加回整体
senses.definition: in mathematics, to calculate the integral of a function or equation
senses.definitionCN: 数学中计算一个函数或方程的积分
senses.example: We integrate the function over the interval from 0 to 2.
senses.exampleCN: 我们求这个函数在 0 到 2 区间上的积分。
senses.why: The mathematical verb grew in 19c. calculus from the noun integral: to integrate is to sum infinitely many thin slices back into a whole. The technical first date is not fixed in the standard etymology, but the image is exactly the word's oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 这个数学动词在 19 世纪微积分中由名词 integral 长出：integrate 就是把无穷多薄片加回一个整体。这一专科用法的最早书面年代，标准词源未明确，但画面正是这个词最古老的那个。

senses.title: Systems: make parts work as one
senses.titleCN: 系统集成：让各部分像一体那样运转
senses.definition: to combine hardware, software, or procedures so that they operate together as a single system
senses.definitionCN: 把硬件、软件或流程结合起来，使它们作为单一系统一起运转
senses.example: The app integrates with the company's payment system.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用与公司的支付系统整合在一起。
senses.why: In 20c. technology, integration is the test of whether parts truly form a whole: not just stored together, but able to pass data and act as one. The old whole-making sense becomes a practical engineering standard.
senses.whyCN: 在 20 世纪技术语境里，integration 成了检验各部分是否真成一个整体的标准：不只是存放在一起，还要能传数据、像一个那样动作。古老的“使完整”义变成了一条工程实践标准。

senses.title: Renew: make whole again
senses.titleCN: 复原：让完整重新回来
senses.definition: to restore something to wholeness or to a former sound condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某物恢复完整或回到原先完好的状态
senses.example: Therapy helped him integrate the scattered pieces of his life.
senses.exampleCN: 心理治疗帮助他把生活里散落的碎片重新整合起来。
senses.why: Latin integrare also meant 'renew, begin again'. Wholeness can be lost and then restored, so integrate carries a repairing edge: the pieces were once one, were broken apart, and are now put back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 integrare 也有“更新、重新开始”的意思。完整可以失去再被恢复，所以 integrate 带一层修复意味：这些部分原本是一体，被拆散了，如今又被放回去。

senses.title: Incorporate: take something inside a larger whole
senses.titleCN: 并入：把某物收进更大的整体
senses.definition: to absorb or incorporate something into a larger whole so that it becomes a part of it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物吸收或并入一个更大的整体，使其成为其中一部分
senses.example: The report integrates the survey data into its main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把调查数据并入其主要论证。
senses.why: Here the direction is inward: one thing is taken into another. The whole does not merely touch the part; it makes the part internal, so that the larger thing's identity now includes it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动向往里：一样东西被收进另一样东西。整体不只是挨着部分，而是把部分变成内部的，于是更大那件事的身份里现在包含了它。

senses.title: Psychology: gather the self into one
senses.titleCN: 人格整合：把自我收拢成一个
senses.definition: in psychology, to unify different parts of the personality or of experience into a coherent self
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指把人格或经验的不同部分统一成一个连贯的自我
senses.example: He worked for years to integrate the memories he had pushed away.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了多年时间，把那些被自己推开的记忆整合进来。
senses.why: Modern psychology extends the same structure inward: a person is a whole made of parts, and health means those parts are no longer split off. Integrate is still 'make one body', only the body is a self.
senses.whyCN: 现代心理学把同一个结构转向内里：人是由部分构成的整体，健康意味着这些部分不再被割裂在外。integrate 仍然是“做成一个身子”，只是这个身子是自我。

intro.en: Integrate comes from Latin integrare 'make whole, renew', from integer 'untouched, whole' (in- 'not' + the root of tangere 'to touch'). English took it in the 1630s as 'render whole'; the modern 'combine parts into a whole' is from 1802, the racial sense from 1940.
intro.cn: integrate 来自拉丁语 integrare“使完整、更新”，再上溯 integer“未被碰过、完整”（in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”的词根）。英语在 17 世纪 30 年代借入，意为“使完整”；现代“把部分合成整体”义始于 1802 年，种族义始于 1940 年。

items.en: Integer 'untouched, whole, complete' is in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'. The PIE root *tag- 'to touch' behind tangere is a reconstructed form with no written record, so the deepest origin is uncertain; the Latin compound itself is well attested.
items.cn: integer“未受碰触的、完整的、完全的”由 in-“不”加 tangere“触碰”的词根构成。tangere 背后的原始印欧词根 *tag-“触摸”是重构形式，没有书面记录，因此最深的来源不确定；但拉丁语这个复合词本身有充分书证。

items.en: Integrare meant 'make whole' and also 'renew, begin again', with the past participle integratus. The second sense matters: wholeness is something that can be lost and restored, not only built for the first time.
items.cn: integrare 意为“使完整”，也有“更新、重新开始”的意思，过去分词是 integratus。第二个义项很要紧：完整不只可以第一次造出来，也可以失去后再恢复。

items.en: The verb first appears as 'to render (something) whole, bring together the parts of'. The accent is on the result: the parts were apart, and now the thing is whole.
items.cn: 这个动词最早出现时意为“使某物完整、把它的各部分聚在一起”。重心在结果：部分原来是分开的，现在这个东西完整了。

items.en: A new transitive sense is recorded: 'put together parts or elements and combine them into a whole'. This is the modern everyday sense used for plans, systems, schools and data.
items.cn: 一个新的及物义项被记录：“把部分或要素放在一起，合成一个整体”。这就是今天用于规划、系统、学校和数据的日常义。

items.en: Calculus gives integrate the technical sense 'find the integral of a function'. Standard etymology records the noun integral from the 1610s but gives no exact date for this verb use, so its first written appearance is uncertain.
items.cn: 微积分给 integrate 添上专科义“求一个函数的积分”。标准词源记录名词 integral 始于 17 世纪 10 年代，却未给出这个动词用法的确切年代，因此它最早的书证时间不确定。

items.en: Integration takes on the anti-discrimination sense in 1934; integrate 'racially desegregate' follows in 1940, probably as a back-formation. Later 20c. systems talk extends the same word to hardware, software and data.
items.cn: integration 在 1934 年获得反歧视义；integrate 的“取消种族隔离”义在 1940 年跟上，很可能是逆构词。20 世纪后期的系统语境又把同一个词扩展到硬件、软件与数据。

note.en: The first group is spelling: all four words descend from integer but have split into different jobs. The second group is meaning: each verb joins things, but with a different degree of closeness.
note.cn: 第一组看拼写：四个词都出自 integer，却分成了不同的职务。第二组看词义：每个动词都在“连接”，只是紧密程度不同。

entries.definition: essential to a whole, or complete in itself. It is the adjective of the family, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的；完整的。它是这个词族的形容词，不是动作。

entries.definition: wholeness, or honesty of character. It names the state that integrate tries to produce.
entries.definitionCN: 完整；正直。它命名的是 integrate 想要造成的状态。

entries.definition: a whole number with no fractional part. It is the source noun, not a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 整数（无小数部分）。它是源名词，不是动词。

entries.definition: combined into a whole, or no longer separated by race. It is the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 整合成的；种族融合的。它是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: to join two or more things so that they are together. It is the broadest match and says nothing about becoming one body.
entries.definitionCN: 结合；联合。最宽泛的对应词，不强调变成一个身子。

entries.definition: to join two things so that the boundary between them disappears. It matches integrate's institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 合并；融合。对应 integrate 的机构合并义。

entries.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole. It matches integrate's 'absorb into' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 并入；包含。对应 integrate 的“吸收进来”义。

entries.definition: to absorb a person or group into the culture of a larger society. It matches integrate's social sense but stresses cultural change.
entries.definitionCN: 同化；融入。对应 integrate 的社会义，但更强调文化改变。

entries.definition: to join together for a common purpose or as a single unit. It matches the core 'make one' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 联合；团结。对应最核心的“使成为一个”义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the integer family behind integral and integrity, integrare 'make whole, renew', the 1940 civil-rights sense, and the calculus operation that sums slices back into a whole.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：integral、integrity 背后的 integer 词族，integrare“使完整、更新”，1940 年的民权义，以及把切片加回整体的微积分运算。

normal.en: integrate = in- 'not' + tang- 'touch' + -ate: to make something that had been broken into untouched, whole pieces again.
normal.cn: integrate = in-“不”+ tang-“碰”+ -ate：把曾被拆开的东西重新做成未被碰断的完整一件。

normal.en: integral is the state, integrate is the act, integration is the result: needed part, make whole, wholeness.
normal.cn: integral 是状态，integrate 是动作，integration 是结果：必需的部分、使完整、完整状态。

normal.en: A school that integrates is putting two student bodies into one building and one life.
normal.cn: 一所学校 integrate，就是把两群学生放进同一栋楼、同一种生活。

normal.en: In calculus, integrate is to add up the thin slices until the area stands as one number.
normal.cn: 微积分里，integrate 就是把薄片加起来，直到面积立成一个数。

normal.en: disintegrate is the mirror: take the in- away and the whole falls back into parts.
normal.cn: disintegrate 是镜子里的反影：把 in- 拿走，整体就散回成部分。

abstract.en: Integration does not erase the parts; it changes what counts as the boundary. The colors remain in the rope.
abstract.cn: 整合并不抹掉部分，它改变的是“边界”算在哪里。绳子里仍看得见原来的颜色。

abstract.en: A society integrates when a newcomer no longer has to stand at the edge to be counted.
abstract.cn: 一个社会真正完成融合，是在新来者不必站在边缘也能被算作一员的时候。

abstract.en: The word's oldest sense is repair as much as construction: what was whole can be made whole again.
abstract.cn: 这个词最老的义项既是建造，也是修补：曾经完整的东西可以再次被做成完整。

examples.en: The course integrates theory with hands-on laboratory work.
examples.cn: 这门课把理论与动手实验整合在一起。

examples.en: It took her a year to integrate into the local community.
examples.cn: 她花了一年时间融入当地社区。

examples.en: The software integrates easily with most existing databases.
examples.cn: 这款软件能轻松与大多数现有数据库整合。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因特格瑞特”——in（不）+ teg（碰）+ rate（做）：把被拆开的各部分重新做成没被碰断的一整件

root: 源自拉丁语 integrare“使完整、更新”，由 integer“未被碰过、完整的”构成（in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”的词根）；英语 17 世纪 30 年代借入为“使完整”，1802 年固定“合成整体”义，1940 年添“取消种族隔离”义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of integrate, all one movement: separate parts are brought inside a single boundary. The whole may be a plan, a society, a school district, a system, a self — or an area under a curve.
sensesIntro.cn: integrate 的九个义项都是同一个动作：把分开的部分收进同一条边界。这个整体可以是一项规划、一个社会、一个学区、一套系统、一个自我——也可以是一条曲线下的面积。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate strands twisted into one rope, each still visible, none able to pull away.
core.cn: 核心意象：几股分开的线被捻成一根绳，每一股仍看得见，却谁也拉不开。

branches.en: MAKING AND REMAKING: parts are joined into a whole, and a broken whole can be restored.
branches.cn: 造出与重修：把部分接成整体，也让破碎的整体复原。

branches.en: TAKING INSIDE: a newcomer fits into a group, and a thing is absorbed into a larger whole.
branches.cn: 收进内部：新来者合进群体，一样东西被吸进更大的整体。

branches.en: ONE ROOF: separate institutions, budgets, and staffs are merged into a single body.
branches.cn: 同一个屋顶：分开的机构、预算与人员被合并成一个身子。

branches.en: NO OLD LINE: the racial boundary is taken down and the separated parts become one society.
branches.cn: 拆掉旧线：种族边界被拆除，被隔开的部分成为一个社会。

branches.en: WORKING AS ONE: slices sum into a definite integral, systems pass data as one, and a self gathers its split parts.
branches.cn: 像一个那样运转：切片加成定积分，系统像一体那样传数据，自我把割裂的部分收拢。

intro.en: Integrate is the verb of the integer family: integration, integrated and integrative grow from it, while disintegrate and reintegrate add direction. Integral, integrity and integer share the same 'untouched whole' base.
intro.cn: integrate 是 integer 词族的动词：integration、integrated、integrative 由它长出，disintegrate 与 reintegrate 则添上方向。integral、integrity、integer 共用同一个“未受碰触的完整”词基。

latinIntro.en: Latin integrare 'make whole, renew' comes from integer 'untouched, whole', built on in- 'not' plus tangere 'to touch'. The family is about restoring a boundary that has been broken: whole, heal, begin again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integrare“使完整、更新”来自 integer“未被碰过、完整”，后者由 in-“不”加 tangere“触碰”构成。这个词族讲的是修复一条被破坏的边界：完整、愈合、重新开始。

items.meaning: to make whole by joining parts
items.meaningCN: 整合；使成整体（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The design integrates old brick with new steel.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计把旧砖与新钢整合在一起。

items.meaning: the act or result of making whole
items.meaningCN: 整合；一体化；积分（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Integration of the two teams took six months.
items.exampleCN: 两个团队的整合花了六个月。

items.meaning: made into one whole; desegregated
items.meaningCN: 整合的；种族融合的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The city runs an integrated bus and rail service.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市运营着一体化的公交与铁路服务。

items.meaning: tending to bring parts together
items.meaningCN: 有助于整合的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The clinic offers an integrative approach to care.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所提供综合性的照护方式。

items.meaning: one that integrates, or a device that integrates
items.meaningCN: 整合者；积分器（-or 表施动者）
items.example: She acted as the integrator between design and engineering.
items.exampleCN: 她担任设计与工程之间的整合者。

items.meaning: to fall apart into pieces
items.meaningCN: 瓦解；分裂（dis- 分开 + integrate）
items.example: The old wall disintegrated in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 那堵旧墙在雨中瓦解了。

items.meaning: to make whole again; to bring back into a group
items.meaningCN: 使重新融合；使复原（re- 再 + integrate）
items.example: The program helps veterans reintegrate into civilian work.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助退伍军人重新融入平民工作。

items.meaning: essential to, or forming, a whole
items.meaningCN: 不可或缺的；完整的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Soil is integral to any farm plan.
items.exampleCN: 土壤对任何农场规划都不可或缺。

items.meaning: wholeness; uprightness
items.meaningCN: 完整；正直（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: He defended the integrity of the archive.
items.exampleCN: 他维护了这批档案的完整性。

items.meaning: a whole number
items.meaningCN: 整数（字面“未受碰触的完整之物”）
items.example: Divide the total by an integer to keep it exact.
items.exampleCN: 用整数去除总数，以保持精确。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 未受碰触的；完整的；完全的

definition_zh: 智力的；脑力的；有才智的；需动脑的；知识分子的；知识界的
definition_en: relating to the mind and understanding rather than the senses or feelings; or a person who lives by ideas and serious thought
core_image: 一个人坐在灯下，把散乱的经验一层层拆开、比较、再合成一个判断——脸上是安静的专注
scene: Reading is an intellectual pleasure, not a fast one.
sceneCN: 这里 intellectual 是「需动脑的、智性上的」（第 03 个义项：诉诸心智而非感官）；句意：阅读是一种智性上的乐趣，不是求快的那种。画面里灯下的人把句子拆开再合拢，速度慢，却有东西在脑子里立起来。

pos.zh: 智力的；脑力的；有才智的；需动脑的
知识分子；脑力劳动者
