senses.title: Of the understanding: grasped by the mind, not the senses
senses.titleCN: 理解力的：靠头脑把握，而非靠感官
senses.definition: relating to the intellect or understanding, especially as distinct from the senses and the emotions
senses.definitionCN: 与智力或理解力有关的，尤指区别于感官与情感的
senses.example: Children need intellectual as well as physical stimulation.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子既需要身体上的刺激，也需要智力上的刺激。
senses.why: The adjective is recorded late 14c. as 'grasped by the understanding (rather than by the senses)'. It comes from Latin intellectus 'discernment, understanding', so its first job is to mark the line between what the mind holds and what the senses bring.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 14 世纪后期记录为“由理解力把握的（而非由感官）”。它来自拉丁语 intellectus“辨别、理解”，所以它最早的工作就是划出界线：哪些是头脑把握的，哪些是感官带来的。

senses.title: High-powered mind: marked by a great intellect
senses.titleCN: 才智出众：以强大的智力为特征
senses.definition: having or showing a high degree of intellect; unusually intelligent or thoughtful
senses.definitionCN: 具有或表现出高度智力的；格外聪明或深思的
senses.example: She was one of the most intellectual students in her year.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那届学生里最有才智的人之一。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from 1819: 'characterized by a high degree of intellect'. The word moves from naming a faculty to grading a person — the same shift that turns the adjective into a noun for the people who have it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从 1819 年有记录：“以高度智力为特征的”。这个词从命名一种官能，转为给人评级——正是同一个转变，让形容词后来变成指人的名词。

senses.title: Demanding thought: addressed to the mental powers
senses.titleCN: 费脑子：专门诉诸心智能力
senses.definition: appealing to or engaging the mental powers; requiring thought rather than mere sensation
senses.definitionCN: 诉诸或调动心智能力的；需要思考而非仅凭感觉的
senses.example: It is an intellectual film, slow but worth the effort.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一部费脑子的电影，节奏慢，但值得花力气。
senses.why: From 1834 the word means 'appealing to or engaging the mental powers'. A book or film can be intellectual in the same way a meal can be rich: what it offers is not comfort but work for the mind.
senses.whyCN: 从 1834 年起，这个词意为“诉诸或调动心智能力的”。一本书或一部电影可以很 intellectual，就像一顿饭可以很丰盛：它给的不是舒服，而是给头脑的活儿。

senses.title: The person: one who lives by ideas
senses.titleCN: 那个人：靠观念生活的人
senses.definition: a person who engages in serious thought and the life of ideas, often as a profession or public role
senses.definitionCN: 从事严肃思考、过观念生活的人，常以此为职业或公共身份
senses.example: The café was a meeting place for writers and intellectuals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆是作家和知识分子的聚会处。
senses.why: The noun appears in the 1590s meaning 'mind, intellect, intellectual powers'; 'an intellectual person' is recorded from the 1650s, faded in the 19c., and was re-coined about 1906. The abstract faculty became a social type.
senses.whyCN: 名词在 16 世纪 90 年代出现，意为“头脑、智力、智力官能”；“有智力的人”这一义在 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，19 世纪转淡，约 1906 年又被重新造出。抽象的官能变成了一个社会类型。

senses.title: The world of ideas: academic and cultural life
senses.titleCN: 观念的世界：学术与文化生活
senses.definition: belonging to or characteristic of the world of learning, letters, and serious ideas
senses.definitionCN: 属于或体现学问、文学与严肃观念世界的
senses.example: The magazine reports on the intellectual life of the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志报道首都的智识生活。
senses.why: Once the noun named a class of people, the adjective could describe their world: salons, journals, universities, debates. Intellectual life is the environment in which ideas are the main currency.
senses.whyCN: 一旦名词命名了一类人，形容词就能描述他们的世界：沙龙、刊物、大学、辩论。intellectual life 就是以观念为主要通货的环境。

senses.title: Abstract rather than personal: a clash of ideas
senses.titleCN: 抽象而非私人：观念层面的分歧
senses.definition: concerned with ideas and reasoning rather than with practical action or personal feeling
senses.definitionCN: 关心观念与推理，而非实际行动或私人感受的
senses.example: Their disagreement was intellectual, not personal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的分歧是观念上的，不是私人恩怨。
senses.why: Because the word marks the understanding as separate from the senses and emotions, it can oppose 'personal'. An intellectual disagreement stays on the plane of argument: the persons are not at stake, the ideas are.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词把理解力与感官、情感区分开，它就能与 personal 相对。intellectual 的分歧停留在论证层面：当事人不在场，观念才在。

senses.title: Rational: judgment over impulse
senses.titleCN: 理性的：判断压过冲动
senses.definition: guided by reason and thought rather than by instinct, impulse, or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 由理性与思考引导，而非由本能、冲动或情感引导的
senses.example: Fear can override intellectual judgment in an emergency.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急情况下，恐惧会压过理性的判断。
senses.why: Latin intelligere is 'to understand, discern' — to pick out between options. The adjective inherits that act: the intellectual response is the one that separates, compares, and chooses instead of reacting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intelligere 是“理解、辨别”——在选项之间挑出来。形容词继承了这一动作：intellectual 的反应，是先分开、比较、再选择，而不是直接反应。

senses.title: The mind itself: an old noun for the faculty
senses.titleCN: 心智本身：指官能的古名词义
senses.definition: in 16c-17c usage, the mind or intellect considered as a faculty (now archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 16 至 17 世纪用法中指作为官能的头脑或智力（今已古旧）
senses.example: The old doctors treated the intellectual as a faculty of the soul.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的学者把“智力”看作灵魂的一种官能。
senses.why: The 1590s noun first meant 'mind, intellect, intellectual powers', not 'a person'. The adjective had been turned back into a noun for the faculty itself; only later did it come to name the one who uses that faculty.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 90 年代的名词最初指“头脑、智力、智力官能”，而不是“一个人”。形容词被转回成名词，指官能本身；只是后来才用来指使用这个官能的人。

senses.title: Too much head: the over-cerebral caricature
senses.titleCN: 想得太多：过度用脑的讽刺画像
senses.definition: derogatorily, over-concerned with abstract reasoning and out of touch with ordinary life or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 贬义地指过分沉溺于抽象推理、脱离日常生活或情感的
senses.example: Don't be so intellectual about it — just taste the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 别把这事想得那么复杂——先尝尝这汤。
senses.why: Once a society has a word for people who live by ideas, it also gets a word for resenting them: anti-intellectual is recorded from 1821. The same adjective can therefore be a compliment or a complaint, depending on who is holding it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦社会有了一个词来指靠观念生活的人，也就有了一个词来表达对他们的不满：anti-intellectual 自 1821 年有记录。于是同一个形容词既可以是称赞，也可以是抱怨，取决于谁在用它。

intro.en: Intellectual comes from Latin intellectualis 'relating to the understanding', from intellectus 'discernment', the noun of intelligere 'to understand, discern'. That verb is inter 'between' plus legere 'choose, pick out, read'. Old French intellectuel passed it to English in the late 14c.
intro.cn: intellectual 来自拉丁语 intellectualis“与理解力有关的”，再上溯 intellectus“辨别、理解”，即 intelligere“理解、辨别”的名词。这个动词由 inter“在……之间”加 legere“挑选、读出”构成。古法语 intellectuel 在 14 世纪后期把它传给英语。

items.en: Intelligere joined inter 'between' to legere 'choose, pick out, read': to understand is to pick out what matters among many signs. Legere goes back to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather', a reconstructed root with no written record, so its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: intelligere 把 inter“在……之间”接到 legere“挑选、读出”上：理解就是在许多迹象之间挑出要紧的那个。legere 上溯原始印欧词根 *leg-“收集、聚拢”，这是重构词根，没有书面记录，因此更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Intellectus meant 'discernment, understanding, a perception', and intellectualis 'relating to the understanding'. The pair separates the faculty (intellectus) from the quality of belonging to it (intellectualis).
items.cn: intellectus 意为“辨别、理解、感知”，intellectualis 意为“与理解力有关的”。这一对词把官能（intellectus）与“属于该官能的性质”（intellectualis）分开。

items.en: Old French intellectuel carried the adjective into medieval learning. French was the road by which most Latin abstract vocabulary reached English in this period.
items.cn: 古法语 intellectuel 把这个形容词带进中世纪的学问。在这一时期，法语是大多数拉丁抽象词汇进入英语的通道。

items.en: English records the adjective as 'grasped by the understanding' rather than by the senses. This is a philosophical distinction before it is a compliment: it says which faculty does the grasping.
items.cn: 英语记录这个形容词为“由理解力把握的”，而非由感官。这先是哲学上的区分，而不是称赞：它说明是哪种官能在把握。

items.en: The noun first means 'mind, intellect, intellectual powers' in the 1590s. 'An intellectual person' is recorded from the 1650s, but the modern social sense was hardly used in the 19c. and was re-coined about 1906.
items.cn: 名词在 16 世纪 90 年代先指“头脑、智力、智力官能”。“有智力的人”自 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，但现代的社会义在 19 世纪几乎不用，约 1906 年又被重新造出。

items.en: New senses arrive quickly: 'characterized by a high degree of intellect' (1819), 'appealing to the mental powers' (1834), and intellectual property (1845). Anti-intellectual follows in 1821 as the resentment of the type.
items.cn: 新义项来得很快：“以高度智力为特征的”（1819）、“诉诸心智能力的”（1834），以及 intellectual property（1845）。anti-intellectual 在 1821 年跟上，表达对这一类型的不满。

note.en: The first group is the intelligere family: same 'pick out between' base, different endings and jobs. The second group is meaning: each word names a kind of mental or scholarly life.
note.cn: 第一组是 intelligere 词族：同一个“在之间挑出”的词基，不同的词尾与职务。第二组看词义：每个词都命名某种心智或学术生活。

entries.definition: able to learn, understand, and reason well. It describes capacity, while intellectual describes the life of ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 聪明的；有理解力的。它描述能力，而 intellectual 描述观念生活。

entries.definition: able to be understood; clear enough to grasp. It is about being understood, not about being clever.
entries.definitionCN: 可理解的；明白易懂的。它讲“能被理解”，不讲“聪明”。

entries.definition: the power of the mind to reason and understand. It is the faculty that intellectual describes.
entries.definitionCN: 智力；理解力。它正是 intellectual 所描述的官能。

entries.definition: the educated class who discuss and shape ideas. It is the collective noun for intellectuals.
entries.definitionCN: 知识界；知识分子阶层。它是知识分子的集合名词。

entries.definition: appealing to or requiring thought rather than feeling. It matches intellectual's 'demanding thought' sense and often sounds colder.
entries.definitionCN: 诉诸理智的；费脑的。对应 intellectual 的“需动脑”义，常显得更冷。

entries.definition: showing careful academic study and knowledge. It matches intellectual in the academic-life sense.
entries.definitionCN: 学术的；有学者风范的。对应 intellectual 的学术生活义。

entries.definition: relating to the mind or its processes. It matches the basic 'of the understanding' sense but is a plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 心理的；精神的。对应最基本的“理解力的”义，但更平实。

entries.definition: relating to education, research, or scholarly institutions. It matches intellectual's institutional side.
entries.definitionCN: 学术的；学院的。对应 intellectual 的机构性一面。

entries.definition: showing careful thinking and consideration for others. It matches the 'reflective' side of intellectual.
entries.definitionCN: 深思的；体贴的。对应 intellectual 中“善于思考”的一面。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: inter 'between' + legere 'pick out' behind intellect, intelligent and intelligible; the 1590s noun for the faculty; and the 1821 anti-intellectual backlash.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：intellect、intelligent、intelligible 背后 inter“在之间”+ legere“挑出”；16 世纪 90 年代指官能的名词；以及 1821 年的 anti-intellectual 反弹。

normal.en: intellectual = inter 'between' + legere 'pick out': the mind's job is to pick the right thing out of the many in front of it.
normal.cn: intellectual = inter“在之间”+ legere“挑出”：头脑的工作就是从眼前许多东西里挑出对的那个。

normal.en: intellect, intelligent and intelligible share one verb: to understand is to pick out, to be intelligent is to be able to pick, to be intelligible is to be pickable.
normal.cn: intellect、intelligent、intelligible 共用一个动词：理解是挑出，聪明是能挑，明白易懂是能被挑出来。

normal.en: An intellectual is not just a smart person; it is someone whose daily material is ideas.
normal.cn: intellectual 不只是聪明人；它指以观念为日常材料的人。

normal.en: intellectual property is the product of the mind treated as property — ideas with a fence around them.
normal.cn: intellectual property 是把头脑的产物当作财产——给观念围上一道篱笆。

normal.en: anti-intellectual appeared in 1821: as soon as there was a name for the type, there was a name for resenting it.
normal.cn: anti-intellectual 出现于 1821 年：一旦这一类型有了名字，不满它的名字也就有了。

abstract.en: The word's oldest distinction is not smart versus dull but mind versus senses: what is known by thinking versus what is given by feeling.
abstract.cn: 这个词最老的区分不是聪明与愚笨，而是头脑与感官：哪些是思考得知的，哪些是感觉给予的。

abstract.en: To pick out between things is also to choose a side, so the intellectual life always carries a moral edge: discernment is judgment.
abstract.cn: 在事物之间挑出，也是在选择一边，所以智识生活总带一层道德意味：辨别就是判断。

abstract.en: Every society that praises its intellectuals also invents a word for distrusting them; the adjective can be worn as a badge or a warning.
abstract.cn: 每个赞扬知识分子的社会，也会造出一个不信任他们的词；这个形容词既可以是徽章，也可以是警告。

examples.en: The course offers intellectual challenge rather than easy answers.
examples.cn: 这门课给的是智力上的挑战，而不是轻松的答案。

examples.en: He moved to the city and joined a circle of intellectuals.
examples.cn: 他搬到城里，加入了一个知识分子圈子。

examples.en: The dispute was intellectual; neither man disliked the other.
examples.cn: 这场争论是观念上的，两个人并不讨厌对方。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因特莱克球”——inter（在之间）+ lect（挑出）：在众多说法之间挑出对的，就是智力、有才智的

root: 源自拉丁语 intellectualis“与理解力有关的”，来自 intellectus“辨别、理解”，即 intelligere“理解、辨别”（inter“在……之间”+ legere“挑选、读出”）；legere 上溯重构的原始印欧词根 *leg-“收集”（重构形式，无书面记录，来源不确定）。经古法语 intellectuel 于 14 世纪后期进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of intellectual, all built on one act: picking out between things. The act becomes a faculty, then a quality of a person, then a whole way of life — and finally a caricature of itself.
sensesIntro.cn: intellectual 的九个义项都建立在同一个动作上：在事物之间挑出。这个动作先成为官能，再成为人的品质，再成为一种生活方式——最后变成对自身的讽刺画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind at a lit table, separating, comparing, and picking one thing out of many.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下的一张桌子前，一颗头脑把许多东西分开、比较，再挑出其中一个。

branches.en: THE MIND AT WORK: what is grasped by understanding, and what is judged by reason instead of impulse.
branches.cn: 头脑在工作：由理解力把握的东西，以及由理性而非冲动作出的判断。

branches.en: THE STRONG MIND AND THE PERSON: a high degree of intellect, and the one who lives by ideas.
branches.cn: 强健的头脑与那个人：高度发达的智力，以及靠观念生活的人。

branches.en: THE WORLD OF IDEAS: work for the mental powers, the life of journals and salons, and argument kept on the abstract plane.
branches.cn: 观念的世界：给心智的活儿、刊物与沙龙的生活，以及停留在抽象层面的争论。

branches.en: THE FACULTY ITSELF: an older noun that named the mind rather than the person.
branches.cn: 官能本身：一个更早的名词，命名的是头脑，不是人。

branches.en: THE CARICATURE: too much head, too little life — the complaint that trails the compliment.
branches.cn: 讽刺画像：脑袋太多、生活太少——跟着称赞一起到来的抱怨。

intro.en: Intellectual is built on Latin intelligere 'to understand': intellect and intelligible come from the same verb, while intelligence and intelligentsia are close cousins. The suffix -al turns the noun intellectus into a quality.
intro.cn: intellectual 建立在拉丁语 intelligere“理解”上：intellect 与 intelligible 出自同一个动词，intelligence 与 intelligentsia 则是近亲。后缀 -al 把名词 intellectus 变成一种性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin intelligere 'understand, discern' is inter 'between' + legere 'choose, pick out, read'. Intellectus is the act or faculty of discerning, and intellectualis adds -alis to make 'belonging to that faculty'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intelligere“理解、辨别”由 inter“在……之间”+ legere“挑选、读出”构成。intellectus 是辨别的动作或官能，intellectualis 再加 -alis，表示“属于这一官能的”。

items.meaning: relating to the understanding
items.meaningCN: 智力的；理解力的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The problem needs intellectual effort, not guesswork.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题需要动脑，而不是靠猜。

items.meaning: the power of reasoning and understanding
items.meaningCN: 智力；理解力（直接来自 intellectus）
items.example: Her intellect was matched by her patience.
items.exampleCN: 她的智力与耐心相当。

items.meaning: in terms of the mind or ideas
items.meaningCN: 智力上；思想上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The job is intellectually demanding.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作在脑力上要求很高。

items.meaning: undue emphasis on reasoning
items.meaningCN: 知性主义；过度强调理智（-ism 表主义、倾向）
items.example: His intellectualism kept him at a distance from the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 他的知性气质让他与人群保持距离。

items.meaning: to treat something in a purely reasoning way
items.meaningCN: 使理智化；作理性分析（-ize 表“使……”）
items.example: He tends to intellectualize his own grief.
items.exampleCN: 他倾向于把自己的悲伤作理性化的处理。

items.meaning: hostile to intellectuals or to serious thought
items.meaningCN: 反知识分子的；反智的（anti- 反对）
items.example: The movement had a strong anti-intellectual streak.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动带有强烈的反智倾向。

items.meaning: the capacity to understand; also information
items.meaningCN: 智力；情报（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: The test measures several kinds of intelligence.
items.exampleCN: 这项测验测量几种不同的智力。

items.meaning: able to learn and reason well
items.meaningCN: 聪明的；有理解力的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: An intelligent reader asks better questions.
items.exampleCN: 聪明的读者会提出更好的问题。

items.meaning: able to be understood
items.meaningCN: 可理解的；明白易懂的（-ible 表“能被……”）
items.example: His accent made the lecture hard to follow but intelligible.
items.exampleCN: 他的口音让讲座不易跟上，但仍听得懂。

items.meaning: the educated class who shape ideas
items.meaningCN: 知识界；知识分子阶层
items.example: The reform was debated mainly within the intelligentsia.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革主要在知识界内部被讨论。

latinEntries.meaning: to understand, discern, come to know

definition_zh: 智力；智能；理解力；聪明才智；消息；情报；情报机构
definition_en: the ability to learn, understand and reason; also information, especially secret information gathered about an enemy or a situation
core_image: 一个人在暗处把零散线索摊在桌上，挑出彼此对得上的几条，拼成一幅别人还看不见的图
scene: The agency gathered intelligence on the movement of the ships.
sceneCN: 这里 intelligence 是「情报」（第 05 个义项：秘密收集的信息）；句意：该机构收集关于这些船只动向的情报。画面里桌上的照片、航线和时间戳被挑出、对齐，最后合成一条别人尚未察觉的航线。

pos.zh: 智力；智能；理解力；聪明；消息；情报；情报机构；情报人员

senses.title: The capacity to learn: mind meeting a new problem
senses.titleCN: 学习的能力：头脑遇上新问题
senses.definition: the general capacity to learn, understand, and deal with new situations or problems
senses.definitionCN: 学习、理解并应对新情况或新问题的一般能力
senses.example: The test is designed to measure intelligence, not memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测验测的是智力，不是记忆力。
senses.why: Recorded late 14c. as 'the highest faculty of the mind, capacity for comprehending general truths'. The word names a power of the mind, not a store of facts: it is what lets a mind meet something it has not met before.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期记录为“心智最高的官能、领会普遍真理的能力”。这个词命名的是头脑的一种力量，不是一堆事实：它让头脑能应对从未遇过的东西。

senses.title: Understanding: the faculty that grasps meaning
senses.titleCN: 理解力：抓住意义的那个官能
senses.definition: the faculty of understanding or comprehending, especially in the abstract
senses.definitionCN: 理解或领会的官能，尤指抽象意义上的
senses.example: The book is beyond the intelligence of a young child.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书超出了一个幼儿的理解力。
senses.why: About 1400 the word means 'faculty of understanding, comprehension'. Latin intelligentia is 'understanding, knowledge, power of discerning', from intelligere 'to understand'. The noun names the ability itself, apart from any particular thing understood.
senses.whyCN: 约 1400 年，这个词意为“理解、领会的官能”。拉丁语 intelligentia 是“理解、知识、辨别力”，来自 intelligere“理解”。名词命名的是能力本身，与具体理解了什么无关。

senses.title: Sagacity: understanding better than most
senses.titleCN: 睿智：比多数人理解得更透
senses.definition: superior understanding, quickness of mind, or sound judgment
senses.definitionCN: 超常的理解力、思维敏捷或可靠的判断力
senses.example: She handled the crisis with intelligence and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 她以智慧和耐心处理了这场危机。
senses.why: From early 15c. intelligence means 'superior understanding, sagacity, quality of being intelligent'. The same faculty is now being graded: not just the power to understand, but the quality of understanding well.
senses.whyCN: 从 15 世纪早期起，intelligence 意为“超常的理解力、睿智、聪明的品质”。同一个官能这时被评级：不只是能理解的力量，而是理解得很好的品质。

senses.title: News: what has been passed on
senses.titleCN: 消息：被传过来的情况
senses.definition: information received or imparted; news or tidings about something
senses.definitionCN: 收到或传达的信息；关于某事的消息、音讯
senses.example: Intelligence reached the capital that the harvest had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 收成失败的消息传到了都城。
senses.why: By mid-15c. the word also means 'information received or imparted, news'. If understanding is what a mind gathers, then the thing gathered can be called intelligence too: the word shifts from the act to its content.
senses.whyCN: 到 15 世纪中期，这个词也意为“收到或传达的信息、消息”。如果理解是头脑收集的东西，那么被收集的内容也可以叫 intelligence：词从动作滑到了内容。

senses.title: Secret intelligence: what spies bring back
senses.titleCN: 秘密情报：间谍带回来的东西
senses.definition: secret information, especially about an enemy, a rival, or a hidden situation
senses.definitionCN: 秘密信息，尤指关于敌人、对手或隐秘局势的
senses.example: The agency gathered intelligence on the movement of the ships.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构收集关于这些船只动向的情报。
senses.why: The sense 'secret information from spies' is recorded from the 1580s. Once information is valuable enough to be kept from others, it needs a word that sounds like knowledge but works like a weapon.
senses.whyCN: “来自间谍的秘密信息”这一义在 16 世纪 80 年代有记录。一旦信息重要到必须对别人隐瞒，它就需要一个听起来像“知识”、用起来却像“武器”的词。

senses.title: The service: the body that collects it
senses.titleCN: 情报机构：收集它的那个机关
senses.definition: an organization or service that gathers secret information, or the people who do this work
senses.definitionCN: 收集秘密信息的机构或部门，或从事这项工作的人员
senses.example: He spent thirty years in intelligence before entering politics.
senses.exampleCN: 他从政之前在情报部门工作了三十年。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the product into the producer: what began as the information becomes the bureau that collects it and the career of the people inside. This institutional sense belongs to the modern state and its standing services.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把产物变成生产者：起初是那条信息，后来变成收集它的机关，以及其中人员的职业。这个机构义属于现代国家及其常设部门。

senses.title: A being that understands: an old metaphysical sense
senses.titleCN: 有智力的存在：一个古老的形而上学义
senses.definition: a being endowed with understanding, such as an angel or a spirit (a late medieval usage)
senses.definitionCN: 被赋予理解力的存在，如天使或灵体（中世纪后期用法）
senses.example: The old theologians ranked intelligences above mere matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的神学家把有智力的存在排在纯物质之上。
senses.why: Late 14c. also records 'a being endowed with understanding or intelligence'. In medieval thought the universe was populated by intelligences; the plural intelligences still carries that shadow of separate minds.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期还记录了“被赋予理解力的存在”。在中世纪思想里，宇宙中住满了各种“智能体”；复数 intelligences 至今仍带那种“一个个独立心智”的影子。

senses.title: Artificial intelligence: intelligence made, not born
senses.titleCN: 人工智能：造出来的智能，不是天生的
senses.definition: the capacity of machines or software to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence
senses.definitionCN: 机器或软件执行通常需要人类智力的任务的能力
senses.example: Artificial intelligence now helps radiologists spot small tumours.
senses.exampleCN: 人工智能现在帮助放射科医生发现很小的肿瘤。
senses.why: The phrase artificial intelligence was coined in the mid-20c., and the abbreviation AI is recorded by 1971. The old word for a mind's power is lent to a machine: for the first time the intelligence need not have a mind behind it.
senses.whyCN: artificial intelligence 这一说法在 20 世纪中期被造出，缩写 AI 在 1971 年已有记录。那个指头脑力量的旧词被借给了机器：智力第一次不必有一个头脑在背后。

senses.title: The highest faculty: intelligence as spiritual grasp
senses.titleCN: 最高的官能：作为精神性把握的智力
senses.definition: in medieval and older usage, the highest power of the soul, capable of grasping general and divine truths
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪及更早用法中，指灵魂最高的力量，能把握普遍与神圣的真理
senses.example: Medieval writers placed intelligence among the highest powers of the soul.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪作家把智力列在灵魂最高的力量之中。
senses.why: The earliest sense is 'the highest faculty of the mind, capacity for comprehending general truths'. Before it was a test score or a spy report, intelligence was what let a soul reach truths that the senses could not deliver.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是“心智最高的官能、领会普遍真理的能力”。在它成为测验分数或间谍报告之前，intelligence 是让灵魂抵达感官无法送达的真理的那种力量。

intro.en: Intelligence comes from Latin intelligentia 'understanding, knowledge, power of discerning', from intelligere 'to understand', itself inter 'between' plus legere 'choose, pick out, read'. Old French intelligence (12c.) brought it to English late 14c.; the spy sense is from the 1580s.
intro.cn: intelligence 来自拉丁语 intelligentia“理解、知识、辨别力”，再上溯 intelligere“理解”，由 inter“在……之间”加 legere“挑选、读出”构成。古法语 intelligence（12 世纪）把它带到英语，时在 14 世纪后期；间谍义则始于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: Intelligere 'to understand, comprehend, come to know' is inter 'between' plus legere 'choose, pick out, read'. Understanding is literally picking something out from among things. Legere's PIE root *leg- 'to collect, gather' is reconstructed with no written record, so that deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: intelligere“理解、领会、得知”由 inter“在……之间”加 legere“挑选、读出”构成。理解字面上就是从许多东西里挑出一样。legere 的原始印欧词根 *leg-“收集、聚拢”是重构形式，没有书面记录，因此更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Intelligentia meant 'understanding, knowledge, power of discerning; art, skill, taste', and intelligens was its present participle, 'discerning, appreciative'. The noun covers both the power and the cultivated taste that uses it.
items.cn: intelligentia 意为“理解、知识、辨别力；技艺、技能、品味”，其现在分词 intelligens 意为“有辨别力的、能欣赏的”。这个名词同时覆盖那份力量与使用它的修养品味。

items.en: Old French intelligence carried the Latin noun into medieval French. French was the main channel for Latin abstract vocabulary entering English after the Conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 intelligence 把这个拉丁名词带入中世纪法语。诺曼征服之后，法语是拉丁抽象词汇进入英语的主要通道。

items.en: English records 'the highest faculty of the mind, capacity for comprehending general truths', then about 1400 'faculty of understanding, comprehension'. The word begins as a name for a power of the soul.
items.cn: 英语记录“心智最高的官能、领会普遍真理的能力”，约 1400 年又记“理解、领会的官能”。这个词最初是灵魂某种力量的名称。

items.en: Early 15c. adds 'superior understanding, sagacity'; mid-15c. adds 'information received or imparted, news'; the 1580s add 'secret information from spies'. Faculty, quality, news, and secret all sit in one noun.
items.cn: 15 世纪早期添“超常的理解力、睿智”；15 世纪中期添“收到或传达的信息、消息”；16 世纪 80 年代添“来自间谍的秘密信息”。官能、品质、消息、秘密，全住在同一个名词里。

items.en: Modern English adds the institutional sense, intelligence as the service that gathers the information, and then artificial intelligence in the mid-20c.; the abbreviation AI is recorded by 1971. IQ, from intelligence quotient, dates from 1921.
items.cn: 现代英语添上机构义——收集信息的情报部门；20 世纪中期又添 artificial intelligence，缩写 AI 在 1971 年已有记录。IQ（intelligence quotient，智商）则始于 1921 年。

note.en: The first group looks alike because all four come from intelligere; their endings decide whether they name a capacity, a person, a class, or a clarity. The second group comes at intelligence from meaning: mind, knowledge, and secret information.
note.cn: 第一组形似，因为四个词都出自 intelligere；词尾决定它们命名的是能力、个人、阶层还是清晰度。第二组从词义靠近 intelligence：头脑、知识、秘密信息。

entries.definition: having or showing intelligence; able to learn and reason. It is the adjective, not the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 聪明的；有理解力的。它是形容词，不是名词。

entries.definition: clear enough to be understood. It describes what can be grasped, not the power of grasping.
entries.definitionCN: 明白易懂的。它描述“可被理解”，不是“理解的能力”。

entries.definition: the educated class who deal in ideas. It is a collective social noun, not a faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 知识界；知识分子阶层。它是集合的社会名词，不是官能。

entries.definition: the power of reasoning and understanding. It overlaps intelligence but sounds more formal and less measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 智力；理解力。它与 intelligence 重叠，但更正式、更不“可测量”。

entries.definition: the faculty of reasoning and understanding, considered as a whole. It matches the first sense of intelligence.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的推理与理解官能。对应 intelligence 的第一个义项。

entries.definition: the quality of having sound judgment built from experience and knowledge. It matches intelligence in the sagacity sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由经验与知识积累出的良好判断力。对应 intelligence 的“睿智”义。

entries.definition: facts or details about something. It matches the 'news' sense but carries no secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 关于某事的事实或细节。对应“消息”义，但不含秘密色彩。

entries.definition: the practice of spying to obtain secret information. It matches intelligence in the spy sense but names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 间谍活动；侦察。对应 intelligence 的间谍义，但命名的是活动本身。

entries.definition: a deep and accurate understanding of something. It matches intelligence as a grasp of what is hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 洞察力；深刻的理解。对应 intelligence 中“看穿隐秘”的一面。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: inter 'between' + legere 'pick out' behind intelligence and intellect, the 1580s spy sense, the 1921 IQ, and the 1971 abbreviation AI.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：intelligence、intellect 背后 inter“在之间”+ legere“挑出”，16 世纪 80 年代的间谍义，1921 年的 IQ，以及 1971 年的缩写 AI。

normal.en: intelligence = inter 'between' + legere 'pick out': to be intelligent is to pick the right sign out of a noisy field.
normal.cn: intelligence = inter“在之间”+ legere“挑出”：聪明就是从嘈杂的信息里挑出对的那个信号。

normal.en: The spy sense is just the old sense with a lock on it: information picked out, then kept from others.
normal.cn: 间谍义只是给老义项加了一把锁：挑出来的信息，再对别人藏起来。

normal.en: intelligence test measures the power; intelligence report delivers the content. Same word, act and object.
normal.cn: intelligence test 测的是那份力量；intelligence report 送的是那个内容。同一个词，动作与对象。

normal.en: AI is intelligence without a mind: the word's oldest power lent to a machine.
normal.cn: AI 是没有头脑的 intelligence：把这个词最古老的那份力量借给了机器。

normal.en: counterintelligence is intelligence aimed back at intelligence: one spy watching another.
normal.cn: counterintelligence 是让情报反过来对准情报：一个间谍盯着另一个间谍。

abstract.en: The word keeps sliding between the knower and the known: a power in the mind, then the news that power receives, then the bureau that receives it.
abstract.cn: 这个词一直在“知者”与“所知”之间滑动：头脑里的一份力量，然后是这份力量收到的消息，再然后是收消息的机关。

abstract.en: Intelligence is not the amount of knowledge but the ability to choose among it; the root is literally a choice.
abstract.cn: 智力不是知识的量，而是在知识之间作选择的能力；词根本来就是一次“挑选”。

abstract.en: A society's word for cleverness can become its word for secrets: whatever is picked out first is worth hiding.
abstract.cn: 一个社会用来指聪明的词，也能变成指秘密的词：凡是被挑出来的，先就值得藏起来。

examples.en: The puzzle is a test of intelligence rather than of speed.
examples.cn: 这个谜题考的是智力，而不是速度。

examples.en: Military intelligence warned of the attack two days early.
examples.cn: 军事情报提前两天预警了这次袭击。

examples.en: Artificial intelligence is changing how hospitals read scans.
examples.cn: 人工智能正在改变医院阅片的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因特利金”——inter（在之间）+ lig（挑选）：在杂乱线索之间挑出对的那条，就是智力、情报

root: 源自拉丁语 intelligentia“理解、知识、辨别力”，来自 intelligere“理解、辨别”（inter“在……之间”+ legere“挑选、读出”）；legere 上溯重构的原始印欧词根 *leg-“收集”（重构形式，无书面记录，来源不确定）。经古法语于 14 世纪后期进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of intelligence, all one act: picking out the sign that matters. The act is first a power of the soul, then a quality, then the news that power receives, then the secret, the bureau, and finally a machine that does it without a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: intelligence 的九个义项都是同一个动作：挑出要紧的那个信号。这个动作先是灵魂的一份力量，再是一种品质，再是这份力量收到的消息，然后是秘密、机关，最后是一台没有头脑却能做这件事的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered signs laid out in the dark, the matching ones picked out and made into a picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗处摊开的零散迹象，其中对得上的几条被挑出，拼成一幅图。

branches.en: THE POWER TO GRASP: the capacity to learn, and the faculty that comprehends meaning.
branches.cn: 把握的力量：学习的能力，以及领会意义的官能。

branches.en: THE RANK OF MINDS: superior sagacity in a person, and separate intelligences in older cosmology.
branches.cn: 心智的等级：人身上超常的睿智，以及旧宇宙论中一个个独立的智力存在。

branches.en: THE NEWS: what is received and passed on, before any lock is put on it.
branches.cn: 消息：在被加上锁之前，被收到并传出去的东西。

branches.en: THE SECRET AND THE SERVICE: information kept from others, and the body that collects it.
branches.cn: 秘密与机关：对别人隐瞒的信息，以及收集它的机构。

branches.en: MADE AND UPLIFTED: intelligence built into a machine, and intelligence as the soul's highest grasp.
branches.cn: 造出的与向上的：被造进机器的智能，以及作为灵魂最高把握的智力。

intro.en: Intelligence is the noun of intelligere: intelligent and intelligible are its adjective siblings, intelligentsia is a social collective, and counterintelligence adds direction. Intellect and intellectual share the same verb.
intro.cn: intelligence 是 intelligere 的名词：intelligent 与 intelligible 是它的形容词兄弟，intelligentsia 是社会集合词，counterintelligence 则加上方向。intellect 与 intellectual 共用同一个动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin intelligere 'understand' is inter 'between' + legere 'pick out, read'; intelligentia is the state or power of understanding, and intellegens the one who discerns. The family is about choosing the right thing among many.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intelligere“理解”由 inter“在……之间”+ legere“挑出、读出”构成；intelligentia 是理解的状态或力量，intellegens 则是能辨别的那一个。这个词族讲的是在众多东西中选对。

items.meaning: the power to understand; also information
items.meaningCN: 智力；情报（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Her intelligence showed in the questions she asked.
items.exampleCN: 她的智力从她提的问题里显出来。

items.meaning: having the power to understand
items.meaningCN: 聪明的；有理解力的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: An intelligent plan leaves room for error.
items.exampleCN: 聪明的计划会给错误留出余地。

items.meaning: in a thoughtful, well-judged way
items.meaningCN: 聪明地；明智地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The money was spent intelligently.
items.exampleCN: 这笔钱花得很明智。

items.meaning: able to be understood
items.meaningCN: 可理解的（-ible 表“能被……”）
items.example: The manual is short and intelligible.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册简短易懂。

items.meaning: the quality of being understandable
items.meaningCN: 可理解性；清晰度（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The recording was cleaned to improve its intelligibility.
items.exampleCN: 录音经过降噪，以提高清晰度。

items.meaning: the educated class who live by ideas
items.meaningCN: 知识界；知识分子阶层
items.example: The novel was read chiefly by the intelligentsia.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说主要读者是知识界。

items.meaning: work done to block an enemy's intelligence
items.meaningCN: 反情报；反间谍（counter- 反对 + intelligence）
items.example: Counterintelligence kept the leak secret for years.
items.exampleCN: 反情报工作让这次泄密保密了多年。

items.meaning: a person who brings news or intelligence (archaic)
items.meaningCN: 情报员；报信者（-er 表人，古旧）
items.example: An intelligencer brought word of the fleet's arrival.
items.exampleCN: 一名报信者带来了舰队抵达的消息。

items.meaning: the reasoning and understanding power
items.meaningCN: 智力；理解力（直接来自 intellectus）
items.example: The problem defeated his intellect but not his patience.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题难住了他的智力，却没难住他的耐心。

items.meaning: relating to the understanding; a person of ideas
items.meaningCN: 智力的；知识分子（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The debate was an intellectual pleasure.
items.exampleCN: 这场辩论是一种智性上的享受。

latinEntries.meaning: to understand, comprehend, come to know
